Bixby Vision is a real-time visual recognition feature that analyzes images captured through the device camera and provides context-specific information or actions. It uses both on-device processing and cloud-based AI resources. It was pre-installed on [[Samsung Galaxy]] phones and tablets<ref>{{Cite web |title=Your Samsung Camera Has a Secret AI Assistant—Here's How to Use It |url=https://www.lifewire.com/bixby-vision-11724155 |access-date=2025-11-04 |website=Lifewire |language=en}}</ref> from 2017 to 2026.

Bixby Vision has numerous modes such as 'Text', which identifies text using optical character recognition ([[Optical character recognition|OCR]]) to extract printed or handwritten text seen with the camera for copying, searching, or sharing.<ref name="verge">{{Cite news |last=Bohn |first=Dieter |date=29 March 2017 |title=Three things we know Samsung's new assistant can do on the Galaxy S8 |url=https://www.theverge.com/2017/3/29/15097744/samsung-bixby-galaxy-s8-assistant-vs-siri-alexa-android |access-date=30 August 2018 |work=The Verge}}</ref> The 'Translate' mode detects foreign text and outputs real-time translation on the camera preview.<ref name="verge" />

The 'Discover' mode is a visual search engine powered by [[Pinterest]] Lens.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pinterest will power visual search on the Samsung Galaxy S8 and assistant Bixby |url=https://www.thedrum.com/news/pinterest-will-power-visual-search-the-samsung-galaxy-s8-and-assistant-bixby |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=The Drum |language=en-US}}</ref> Bixby Vision also had a 'Wine' mode specially for recognizing [[wine]] labels and outputting information such as variety and origin.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hall |first=Chris |date=2017-01-30 |title=What is Bixby? Samsung's smart assistant explained |url=https://www.pocket-lint.com/phones/news/samsung/140128-what-is-bixby-samsungs-assistant-explained-and-how-to-use-it/ |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=Pocket-lint |language=en}}</ref> 

A number of [[accessibility]] tools also existed. The 'Scene Describer' mode generates written and spoken descriptions of captured scenes u .sing the camera, while 'Object Identifier' mode identifies and voices real-life items. 'Text Reader' converts detected text into spoken audio using [[text-to-speech]] (TTS) functionality and 'Color Detector' identifies and names colors within the frame.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Samsung Bixby Accessibility Features {{!}} American Foundation for the Blind |url=https://afb.org/bixby-accessibility |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=The American Foundation for the Blind |language=en}}</ref>

Other modes were Home Decor, Makeup, Styling and Places which were removed in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Potts |first=Caleb |date=2020-10-05 |title=Samsung is killing Bixby Vision's AR-powered abilities |url=https://www.androidpolice.com/2020/10/05/samsung-is-killing-bixby-visions-ar-powered-abilities/ |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=Android Police |language=en}}</ref> Many [[augmented reality]] tools were consolidated by Samsung into one single app called [[AR Zone]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mehrotra |first=Pranob |date=2020-10-06 |title=Samsung is discontinuing Bixby Vision's augmented reality features |url=https://www.xda-developers.com/samsung-discontinuing-bixby-vision-augmented-reality-features/ |access-date=2026-10-18 |website=XDA |language=en}}</ref> Bixby Vision was fully dismantled in [[One UI]] 8.5 released in 2026. Its tools have been scattered elsewhere in the system, for example Translate and Text modes are now integrated in the Camera app, object and scene tools are moved to Gallery, while [[Google]]'s Circle To Search serves as a replacement for the Discover visual lookup mode.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adhikari |first=Sumit |date=2026-07-30 |title=Bixby Could Soon Identify Objects, Answer Questions and Complete Purchases |url=https://sammyguru.com/samsung-new-bixby-vision-complete-purchase/ |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=SammyGuru |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Bixby Home ===
[[File:Samsung Bixby screenshot.png|thumb|Bixby Home, the former information screen at launch of Bixby 1.0|300x300px]]Bixby Home was a vertically scrolling home screen displaying cards of information such as weather, fitness activity, and smart home controls.<ref name="verge" /> It was renamed '''Samsung Daily''' with the release of One UI 2.1 in 2020,<ref>{{Cite news |title=Samsung rolling out One UI 2.1 update |date=2020 |url= |access-date= }}</ref> then replaced by '''Samsung Free''' in One UI 3.0.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Samsung Free replaces Samsung Daily on One UI 3.0 |date=2020 |url= |access-date= }}</ref> Samsung Free was eventually discontinued in some markets. Its successor, '''Samsung News''', now functions as a news aggregation service with optional home-screen integration similar to Bixby Home.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Samsung News launches as replacement for Samsung Free |date=2023 |url= |access-date= }}</ref>

=== Bixby Routines ===
Bixby Routines was an automation feature that allowed users to create custom rules based on triggers such as time, location, or device conditions. Beginning with One UI 5.0 released in 2022, it was integrated with [[Microsoft To Do]] and renamed '''Modes and Routines'''.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Samsung introduces Modes and Routines in One UI 5.0 |date=2022 |url= |access-date= }}</ref>

=== Other components ===
Bixby Text Call, introduced in One UI 5.0 (2022) in select regions, enabled users to handle incoming calls via speech-to-text conversion and vice versa.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Samsung adds Bixby Text Call in One UI 5 |date=2022 |url= |access-date= }}</ref> It is now named simply '''Text Call''' and can be found in the Phone app settings.<ref>{{Cite news |title=How to enable Text Call on Samsung phones |date=2023 |url= |access-date= }}</ref>

Bixby Touch allowed users to trigger context-aware actions by touching on-screen content. It analyzed images, text, and other visual elements displayed on the device and provided related options such as translation, image search, product lookup, or other content-based information. Several of its capabilities overlapped with, or were later superseded by, features offered through Bixby Vision.{{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}

Other legacy components including '''Bixby Touch''', '''Bixby Global Action''', '''Bixby Capsules''', '''Bixby Briefing''', '''Bixby Dictation''', and '''Bixby Wakeup''', formed part of the early Bixby suite and have since been phased out, though exact discontinuation details vary by region.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Samsung retires additional legacy Bixby features |date=2018 |url= |access-date= }}</ref>

==Regions and languages==
As of April 2018, Bixby is available in over 195 countries, but only in Korean, English (American), and Chinese (Mandarin).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2017/08/22/samsung-bixby-expands-to-over-200-countries-in-battle-with-alexa-siri.html|title=Samsung Bixby expands to over 200 countries in battle with Amazon Alexa, Apple Siri|last=Kharpal|first=Arjun|date=22 August 2017|work=[[CNBC]]|access-date=27 August 2017}}</ref> The limitation is that the models not intended for the Japanese market, like S10e, are not allowed to login to Bixby services from Japan; therefore Bixby becomes blocked. The choice of languages has since expanded: Samsung has deployed Bixby's voice command function in French,<ref>{{cite web|title=Et la lumière fut : Bixby prend enfin en charge la langue française… en version bêta|date=13 December 2018|url=https://www.frandroid.com/marques/samsung/556737_et-la-lumiere-fut-bixby-prend-enfin-en-charge-la-langue-francaise-en-version-beta#comments|publication-date=25 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Bixby est disponible en français sur le Galaxy Note 9, enfin !|date=12 December 2018|url=https://www.phonandroid.com/bixby-est-disponible-en-francais-sur-le-galaxy-note-9-enfin.html|publication-date=25 February 2019}}</ref> and on 20 February 2019 Samsung announced the addition of further languages: English (British), German, Italian and Spanish (Spain).<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.samsung.com/us/samsung-extends-global-reach-bixby-launches-support-new-european-languages/|title=Samsung Extends Global Reach of Bixby, Launches Support for New European Languages|date=20 February 2019|website=Samsung US Newsroom|language=en-US|access-date=6 June 2019}}</ref> On 22 February 2020, Samsung announced the addition of Portuguese (Brazil), for Galaxy S10 and Note10, in Beta, and later for other models.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Samsung Further Develops Bixby, Introducing a New Language and Setting a Foundation for Future Growth |url=https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-further-develops-bixby-introducing-a-new-language-and-setting-a-foundation-for-future-growth |access-date=2024-02-15 |website=news.samsung.com |language=en}}</ref> In 2022, Spanish (Latin America) was added as a language.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Press |first=Samsung Mobile |title=Samsung Further Develops Bixby, Introducing a New Language and Setting a Foundation for Future Growth |url=https://www.samsungmobilepress.com/articles/samsung-further-develops-bixby-introducing-a-new-language-and-setting-a-foundation-for-future-growth |access-date=2026-10-14 |website=Samsung Mobile Press |language=en}}</ref>

'''CleanMyMac''' is a [[macOS]] maintenance and optimisation utility developed by [[MacPaw]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=April 7, 2015 |title=CleanMyMac 3 Brings Mail &#038; iTunes Cleaning, Maintenance, and Privacy Features |url=https://www.macstories.net/mac/cleanmymac-3-brings-mail-itunes-cleaning-maintenance-and-privacy-features/ |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=MacStories |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Sullivan |first=Mark |date=February 25, 2022 |title=Ukrainian tech companies hope for the best, plan for worst |url=https://www.fastcompany.com/90725211/ukraine-tech-companies |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241204055835/https://www.fastcompany.com/90725211/ukraine-tech-companies |archive-date=December 4, 2024 |access-date=January 12, 2025 |work=[[Fast Company]] |language=en-US |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=February 25, 2022 |title=From WhatsApp to Grammarly: Ukraine's Influence on the World of Tech |url=https://www.gadgets360.com/apps/features/ukraine-russia-war-attack-invasion-whatsapp-paypal-grammarly-snapchat-cleanmymac-macpaw-tech-influence-2789397 |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=Gadgets 360 |language=en}}</ref> first released in 2008. The software is designed to optimize system performance by removing unnecessary files and managing [[disk space]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dirks |first=Brent |date=June 10, 2019 |title=Keep Your Mac in Top Shape With CleanMyMac X |url=https://www.makeuseof.com/tag/cleanmymac-x-mac/ |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=MakeUseOf |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Optimize Your Mac : App Store Story |url=https://apps.apple.com/us/story/id1603294407 |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=App Store |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=CleanMyMac X gets M1 support, a new look, and a new feature |url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/cleanmymac-x-gets-m1-support-a-new-look-and-a-new-feature/ |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=[[ZDNet]] |language=en}}</ref>

As of 2023, the software has been downloaded over 20 million times<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Чистюля. Українські розробники отримали нагороду за програму для Mac |url=https://techno.nv.ua/ukr/made-in-ukraine/ukrajinska-kompaniya-macpaw-otrimala-nagorodu-za-programu-cleanmymac-x-50068608.html |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=[[The New Voice of Ukraine]] |language=uk}}</ref><ref name=":10">{{Cite web |date=February 6, 2020 |title=Українців нагородили за розробку програми для Мас |url=https://gazeta.ua/articles/science/_ukrayinciv-nagorodili-za-rozrobku-programi-dlya-mas/950300 |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=[[Gazeta.ua]] |language=uk}}</ref><ref name=":11">{{Cite web |last=Lysiuk |first=Oksana |date=October 2, 2023 |title=Ukrainian IT company MacPaw has opened an office in Boston. |url=https://ubn.news/ukrainian-it-company-macpaw-has-opened-an-office-in-boston/ |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=UBN |language=en-US}}</ref> and has received multiple awards, including the [[Red Dot Design Award|Red Dot]] Design Award, [[IF Product Design Award|iF Design Award]], the UX Design Award<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=August 12, 2021 |title=CleanMyMac X got the Red Dot Award |url=https://macpaw.com/news/cleanmymac-got-the-red-dot-award |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=macpaw.com |language=en}}</ref> and Stevie Award.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |title=New Product Awards Category Winners |url=https://tiny-jackal.cloudvent.net/ |access-date=2026-06-09 |website=tiny-jackal.cloudvent.net |language=en}}</ref>

== History ==
CleanMyMac was launched in 2008, with its initial code developed by Oleksandr Kosovan, CEO of MacPaw.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sparrow |first=Mark |title=Ukrainian Software Developer MacPaw Updates CleanMyMac Even While Under Fire |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/marksparrow/2022/06/30/ukrainian-software-developer-macpaw-updates-cleanmymac-even-while-under-fire/?sh=75d8cda530ae |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=[[Forbes]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Карпенко |first=Ольга |date=October 22, 2014 |title=Как создать глобальную компанию в 27 лет: история MacPaw |url=https://ain.ua/2014/10/22/kak-iz-lyubvi-k-texnike-apple-poluchilsya-mnogomillionnyj-biznes-istoriya-kompanii-macpaw/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210508152357/https://ain.ua/2014/10/22/kak-iz-lyubvi-k-texnike-apple-poluchilsya-mnogomillionnyj-biznes-istoriya-kompanii-macpaw/ |archive-date=May 8, 2021 |access-date=January 17, 2025 |website={{Interlanguage link|AIN.ua|uk|AIN.ua|WD=}}}}</ref>

Company's major releases launched in 2015,<ref name=":0" /> 2018<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Horwitz |first=Jeremy |date=September 5, 2018 |title=MacPaw releases CleanMyMac X, a macOS Mojave junk and malware killer |url=https://venturebeat.com/mobile/macpaw-releases-cleanmymac-x-a-macos-mojave-junk-and-malware-killer/ |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=[[VentureBeat]] |language=en-US}}</ref> and 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Waichulis |first=Arin |date=October 16, 2024 |title=MacPaw releases major update to CleanMyMac with fresh design and new features |url=https://9to5mac.com/2024/10/16/macpaw-releases-major-update-to-cleanmymac-with-fresh-design-and-new-features/ |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=[[9to5Mac]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=CleanMyMac отримує велике оновлення, яке виводить його за рамки базового клінера Mac — що змінюється |url=https://ain.ua/2024/10/16/macpaw-robit-onovlennia-cleanmymac/ |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website={{Interlanguage link|AIN.ua|uk|AIN.ua|WD=}} |language=uk}}</ref> By 2018, CleanMyMac had gained more than 5 million users.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dillet |first=Romain |date=September 5, 2018 |title=MacPaw releases CleanMyMac X |url=https://techcrunch.com/2018/09/05/macpaw-releases-cleanmymac-x/ |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=[[TechCrunch]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":8">{{Cite web |last=Сапитон |first=Михаил |title=Украинская компания MacPaw выпустила новую версию CleanMyMac |url=https://ain.ua/2018/09/05/cleanmymac-x-ot-mac-paw/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421042011/https://ain.ua/2018/09/05/cleanmymac-x-ot-mac-paw/ |archive-date=April 21, 2021}}</ref>

In 2020, the software received an [[IF Product Design Award|iF Design Award]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":10" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=July 29, 2024 |title=CleanMyMac X keeps your Mac optimized and running smooth |url=https://appleinsider.com/articles/24/07/29/keep-your-mac-running-smoothly-with-cleanmymac-x |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=AppleInsider |language=en}}</ref> In 2021, it received the [[Red Dot Design Award|Red Dot]] Design Award<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=October 11, 2021 |title=How to use CleanMyMac X to make sure you can trust your Mac |url=https://appleinsider.com/articles/21/10/11/how-to-use-cleanmymac-x-to-make-sure-you-can-trust-your-mac |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=[[AppleInsider]] |language=en}}</ref> and added support for [[Apple silicon|Apple Silicon]] processors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Warwick |first=Stephen |date=February 25, 2021 |title=CleanMyMac X gets M1 Mac support, sleek new look in huge update |url=https://www.imore.com/cleanmymac-x-gets-m1-mac-support-sleek-new-look-huge-update |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=[[iMore]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite news name=":11" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=How These Boston Tech Companies are Growing and Connecting to the Community {{!}} Built In Boston |url=https://www.builtinboston.com/articles/how-these-boston-tech-companies-are-growing-and-connecting-community#MacPaw |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=Built In |language=en}}</ref> in addition to an existing office in [[Kyiv]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zibreg |first=Christian |date=February 24, 2022 |title=Setapp, CleanMyMac and other MacPaw software shall continue working without a hiccup name=":1" />

In 2024, MacPaw released an updated version of CleanMyMac and introduced CleanMyPhone.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Barton |first=Katerina |date=2025-03-18 |title=The most innovative companies in Europe, Middle East, and Africa for 2025 |url=https://www.fastcompany.com/91269422/europe-middle-east-africa-most-innovative-companies-2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250725090010/https://www.fastcompany.com/91269422/europe-middle-east-africa-most-innovative-companies-2025 |archive-date=2025-07-25 |access-date=2026-06-09 |work=Fast Company |language=en-US}}</ref>

In January 2025, it launched CleanMyMac Business, a [[device management]] service for [[small and medium-sized enterprises]] (SMEs).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sparrow |first=Mark |title=MacPaw Launches CleanMyMac Business For SMBs |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/marksparrow/2025/01/07/macpaw-launches-cleanmymac-business-for-smbs/ |access-date=2026-06-09 |website=[[Forbes]] |language=en}}</ref> However, the company announced in January 2026 that the service would be discontinued in July 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gallagher |first=William |date=2026-01-15 |title=Setapp Mobile EU app store and CleanMyMac Business both close down for good |url=https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/01/15/setapp-mobile-eu-app-store-cleanmymac-business-both-close-down-for-good |access-date=2026-06-09 |website=AppleInsider |language=en}}</ref>

== Features ==
CleanMyMac offers features aimed at maintaining and optimizing [[macOS]] systems. It includes tools for cleaning [[disk space]] and optimizing performance,<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=Rubenking |first=Neil J. |date=July 22, 2023 |title=CleanMyMac Review |url=https://www.pcmag.com/reviews/cleanmymac |access-date=January 17, 2025 |website=[[PCMag]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":6" /> as well as features for protecting user privacy, updating applications, [[uninstall]]ing software, and detecting [[malware]] and [[adware]]. The software's malware removal functionality is powered by MacPaw's proprietary Moonlock Engine.<ref name=":9" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sparrow |first=Mark |title=CleanMyMac X Now Has New Malware Removal Tool Powered By Moonlock |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/marksparrow/2023/07/19/cleanmymac-x-has-new-malware-removal-tool-powered-by-moonlock/ |access-date=2026-06-09 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>

Key features include the ability to clear unused system files, [[log files]], and [[temporary file]]s. Additionally, the software provides optimization tools such as maintenance scripts, [[Computer disk|disk]] repair functions, and options for resetting system indexes and databases.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Terpstra |first=Brett |date=September 6, 2018 |title=CleanMyMac X Saves Space, Removes Malware, and Speeds Up Your Mac |url=https://lifehacker.com/cleanmymac-x-saves-space-removes-malware-and-speeds-u-1828832877 |access-date=January 17, 2025 |website=[[Lifehacker]] |language=en}}</ref>

Software modules include Smart Care, Cleanup, Protection, Performance, Applications, My Clutter and Assistant.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wolfe |first=Bryan M. |date=January 25, 2022 |title=CleanMyMac X for Mac review |url=https://www.techradar.com/reviews/cleanmymac-x-for-mac-review |access-date=January 17, 2025 |website=[[TechRadar]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wiesend |first=Stephan |date=October 20, 2024 |title=Die neue Version des System-Optimierers CleanMyMac von MacPaw im Test |url=https://www.macwelt.de/article/2489257/die-neue-version-des-system-optimierers-cleanmymac-von-macpaw-im-test.html |access-date=January 17, 2025 |website={{Interlanguage link|Macwelt|de|Macwelt|WD=}} |language=de}}</ref> The Smart Care feature addresses system junk removal, malware detection, and [[RAM]] cleanup in a single process.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8" /> In 2025, the software added a Cloud Cleanup feature for [[File management|managing files]] stored in connected [[cloud services]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sparrow |first=Mark |title=The Latest Version Of MacPaw’s CleanMyMac Can Now Clean Up Cloud Storage Accounts |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/marksparrow/2025/07/29/the-latest-version-of-macpaws-cleanmymac-can-now-clean-up-cloud-storage-accounts/ |access-date=2026-07-12 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>

These tables provide a '''comparison of operating systems''', of computer devices, as listing general and technical information for a number of widely used and currently available [[personal computer|PC]] or handheld (including [[smartphone]] and [[tablet computer]]) [[operating system]]s. The article "[[Usage share of operating systems]]" provides a broader, and more general, comparison of operating systems that includes [[Server (computing)|servers]], [[Mainframe computer|mainframes]] and [[supercomputer]]s.

Because of the large number and variety of available [[Linux distribution]]s, they are all grouped under a single entry; see [[comparison of Linux distributions]] for a detailed comparison. There is also a variety of BSD and DOS operating systems, covered in [[comparison of BSD operating systems]] and [[comparison of DOS operating systems]].

== Nomenclature ==
The nomenclature for operating systems varies among providers and sometimes within providers.
For purposes of this article the terms used are;
;kernel
:In some operating systems, the OS is split into a low level region called the kernel and higher level code that relies on the kernel. Typically the kernel implements processes but its code does not run as part of a process.{{disputed inline|Proposed nomenclature section|date=November 2023}}
:;hybrid kernel
:;monolithic kernel
;Nucleus
:In some operating systems there is OS code permanently present in a contiguous region of memory addressable by unprivileged code; in IBM systems this is typically referred to as the nucleus. The nucleus typically contains both code that requires special privileges and code that can run in an unprivileged state.  Typically some code in the nucleus runs in the context of a dispatching unit, e.g., address space, process, task, thread, while other code runs independent of any dispatching unit.  In contemporary operating systems unprivileged applications cannot alter the nucleus.

License and pricing policies vary widely among different systems.
Among others, the tables below use the following terms:

;[[BSD licenses|BSD]]
:'''BSD licenses''' are a family of [[permissive free software license]]s, imposing minimal restrictions on the use and distribution of covered software.

;bundled
:The fee is included in the price of the hardware

<ref name="license">Most OS distributions include bundled software with various other licenses.</ref>
<ref name="Lisa">{{cite web|url=https://www.folklore.org/StoryView.py?project=Macintosh&story=Hungarian.txt|title=Hungarian|work=The Original Macintosh Anecdotes}}. Although [[Lisa OS]] ran on the same, but a slower variant, microprocessor and was developed by [[Apple Computer Inc.]] at the same time as [[Classic Mac OS]], they were developed as different projects, only sharing a similar GUI between them.</ref>
<ref name="Mac">[[Mac OS 7.6]] was the first Macintosh system software to be labeled [[Classic Mac OS|Mac OS]]. Operating systems before this were named [[System 1|Macintosh System Software]] through [[System 7|System Software 7.5]], and known as System #.# for short.</ref>

{{Reflist|group="t"|refs=
<ref name="GUI">Operating systems where the GUI is not installed and turned on by default are often bundled with an implementation of the [[X Window System]], installation of which is usually optional.</ref>
<ref name="API">Most operating systems use proprietary APIs in addition to any supported standards.</ref>
<ref name="BSDX">NetBSD and OpenBSD include the [[X Window System]] as base install sets, managed in their respective main source repository, including local modifications. Packages are also provided for more up-to-date versions which may be less tested.</ref>
<ref name="WindowsFS">Windows can read and write with Ext2 and Ext3 file systems only when a driver from [http://www.fs-driver.org FS-driver] or [[Ext2Fsd]] is installed. However, using Explore2fs, Windows can read from, but not write to, Ext2 and Ext3 file systems. Windows can also access ReiserFS through [http://p-nand-q.com/download/rfstool.html rfstool] and related programs.</ref>
<ref name="i686">only i686 CPU</ref>
<ref name="AmigaOSinstaller">Amiga OS features since OS 2.0 version a standard centralized Install utility called [[AmigaOS#Workbench 2.0 user interface improvements|Installer]], which could be used by any software house to install programs. It works as a [[Lisp (programming language)|Lisp]] language interpreter, and install procedures could be listed as simple text. AmigaOS can also benefit from a 3rd party copyrighted library called [[XAD (software)|XAD]] that is available for all POSIX ([[Unix]], [[Linux]], BSD, and for [[AmigaOS]], [[MorphOS]], etc.). This library is freely distributable and publicly available on [[Aminet]] Amiga centralized repository of all Open Source or Free programs and utilities. XAD.Library, complete with GUI Voodoo-X, is based on modules and capable to manage over 300 compression methods and package systems (Voodoo-X GUI supports 80 package systems), including those widely accepted as standards such as [[ZIP (file format)|.ZIP]], [[Cabinet (file format)|.CAB]], [[LHA (file format)|.LHA]], .[[LZX]], [[RPM Package Manager|.RPM]], etc.</ref>
<ref name="AmigaOSinstallation">A standard AmigaOS installation requires usually only few files (typically 3 to 10 files) to be copied in their appropriate directory, and libraries and language files for national localization to be put in their standard OS directories. Any Amiga user with some minimal experience knows where these files should be copied and could perform programs installations by hand.</ref>
<ref name="AmiUpdate">AmiUpdate can update AmigaOS files and all Amiga programs which are registered to use the same update program that is standard for Amiga. Updating AmigaOS requires only few libraries to be put in standard OS location (for example all libraries are stored in <code>Libs:</code> standard virtual device and absolute path finder for <code>Libs</code> directory, Fonts are all in <code>Fonts:</code> absolute locator, the files for language localization are all stored in <code>Locale:</code> and so on). This leaves Amiga users with a minimal knowledge of the system almost free to perform by hand the update of the system files.</ref>
<ref name="Wine">using [[Wine (software)|Wine]]</ref>
<ref name="brandz">{{cite web |url=http://opensolaris.org/os/community/brandz/ |title=BrandZ (Community Group brandz.WebHome) - XWiki |publisher=Opensolaris.org |date=October 26, 2009 |access-date=December 18, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090929041214/http://opensolaris.org/os/community/brandz/ |archive-date=September 29, 2009 }}</ref>
}}

{{Reflist|group="s"|refs=
<ref name="unpatched">Comparison of known unpatched vulnerabilities based on [[Secunia]] & [[SecurityFocus]] reports with severity of ''Not critical'' & above. Update lists manually with oldest published date(s).</ref>
<ref name="LinuxACL">Support for the 1997 withdrawn POSIX [[access control list|ACL]] draft is included in Linux 2.6, but requires a file system able to store them (such as [[ext3]], [[XFS]] or [[ReiserFS]]).</ref>
<ref name="LinuxJail">A [[operating system-level virtualization|jail]] mechanism is available separately in the [[Linux-VServer]] project, but is not integrated into any mainline [[Linux kernel]].</ref>
<ref name="OS2ACL">ACLs are available only in [[OS/2]] Server versions with [[High Performance File System|HPFS386]] filesystem.</ref>
<ref name="SolarisJail">"[[Solaris Containers]]" (including "Zones") are a jail-type mechanism introduced with [[Solaris (operating system)|Solaris]] 10.</ref>
<ref name="ZetaSuperuser">Zeta has full Unix file permissions, but the OS is single user, and users always run as superuser.</ref>
<ref name="STOP6Certified">STOP 6 is certified under [[Common Criteria]] at [[Evaluation Assurance Level|EAL5+]].</ref>
<ref name="PCBSDencrypted">Additionally swap space may be encrypted during installation, uses memory based tmp file storage by default.</ref>
<ref name="SolarisEncrypted">Through [[ZFS]]</ref>
<ref name="AIXHardwareNX">AIX use the [[PowerPC]] architecture which offer page-level protection mechanism. Since AIX version 5300-03 (5.3), this feature can be activated using the [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/systems/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.aix.security/doc/security/stack_exec_disable_modes_monitor.htm&tocNode=int_39558 sedmgr command].</ref>
<ref name="FreeBSDstackProtection">The GCC stack protection (a.k.a. ProPolice stack-smashing protector) has been enabled in base system since FreeBSD 8.0-release.</ref>
<ref name="MacACL">ACLs were added to [[Mac OS X]] starting with version 10.4.</ref>

'''Mozilla Firefox''', or simply '''Firefox''', is a [[Free and open-source software|free and open-source]]<ref name="LWNtrademark">{{cite web |url=https://lwn.net/Articles/118268/ |title=Debian and Mozilla – a study in trademarks |date=January 10, 2005 |website=[[LWN.net]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170801163012/https://lwn.net/Articles/118268/ |archive-date=August 1, 2017 |access-date=September 14, 2011 |author=Corbet, Jonathan |url-status=live}}</ref> [[web browser]] developed by the [[Mozilla Foundation]] and its subsidiary, the [[Mozilla Corporation]]. It uses the [[Gecko (software)|Gecko]] [[Browser engine|rendering engine]] to display web pages, which implements current and anticipated web standards.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://download-firefox.org/spread-firefox/gecko-layout-engine-and-mozilla-firefox/ |title=Gecko Layout Engine |date=July 17, 2008 |publisher=download-firefox.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100615131607/http://download-firefox.org/spread-firefox/gecko-layout-engine-and-mozilla-firefox/ |archive-date=June 15, 2010 |access-date=May 10, 2012}}</ref> The software is available for [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]], [[macOS]], and [[Linux]] systems, as well as a [[Mobile web|mobile]] version for [[Android (operating system)|Android]] (see [[Firefox for Android]]) and [[iOS]], with unofficial ports for other platforms such as [[Oracle Solaris]] and [[OpenIndiana]].

Firefox is the [[spiritual successor]] of [[Netscape Navigator]], as the [[Mozilla]] community was created by [[Netscape]] in 1998, before Netscape's acquisition by [[AOL]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.cbc.ca/technology/technology-blog/2008/02/curtains-for-netscape.html |title=Curtains for Netscape – Tech Bytes |last=Jay |first=Paul |date=February 28, 2008 |publisher=CBC News |access-date=June 26, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150705110100/http://www.cbc.ca/technology/technology-blog/2008/02/curtains-for-netscape.html |archive-date=July 5, 2015 |url-status=live}}</ref> Firefox was created in 2002 under the codename "Phoenix" by members of the Mozilla community who desired a standalone browser rather than the [[Mozilla Application Suite]] bundle. During its [[Software release life cycle#Beta|beta]] phase, it proved to be popular with its testers and was praised for its speed, security, and add-ons compared to [[Microsoft]]'s then-dominant [[Internet Explorer 6]]. It was released on November 9, 2004,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/technology/3993959.stm |title=Firefox browser takes on Microsoft |date=November 9, 2004 |work=[[BBC News]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171220113953/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/technology/3993959.stm |archive-date=December 20, 2017}}</ref> and challenged [[Internet Explorer]]'s dominance with 60 million downloads within nine months.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/4508897.stm |title=The assault on software giant Microsoft |last=Weber |first=Tim |date=May 9, 2005 |work=[[BBC News]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170925233936/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/4508897.stm |archive-date=September 25, 2017}}</ref> In November 2017, Firefox began incorporating new technology under the code name "[[Quantum (Mozilla)|Quantum]]" to promote [[Parallel computing|parallelism]] and a more intuitive [[user interface]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://blog.mozilla.org/blog/2017/11/14/introducing-firefox-quantum/ |title=Introducing the New Firefox: Firefox Quantum |last=Mayo |first=Mark |date=November 14, 2017 |website=The Mozilla Blog |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180627114050/https://blog.mozilla.org/blog/2017/11/14/introducing-firefox-quantum/ |archive-date=June 27, 2018 |access-date=May 26, 2018}}</ref>

The current version of Firefox is available for [[Windows 10]] or later versions of Windows, as well as macOS, and Linux. Its unofficial ports are available for various [[Unix]] systems such as [[Oracle Solaris]] and [[OpenIndiana]], as well as for [[Unix-like]] operating systems, including [[FreeBSD]],<ref name="FreeBSD ports2">{{cite web |title=FreeBSD ports |url=https://svnweb.freebsd.org/ports/head/www/firefox/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190323104221/https://svnweb.freebsd.org/ports/head/www/firefox/ |archive-date=March 23, 2019 |access-date=March 24, 2018}}</ref> [[OpenBSD]],<ref name="OpenBSD ports2">{{cite web |title=OpenBSD ports |url=http://cvsweb.openbsd.org/cgi-bin/cvsweb/ports/www/mozilla-firefox/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190120074628/http://cvsweb.openbsd.org/cgi-bin/cvsweb/ports/www/mozilla-firefox/ |archive-date=January 20, 2019 |access-date=March 24, 2018}}</ref> [[NetBSD]],<ref name="NetBSD pkgsrc2">{{cite web |title=NetBSD pkgsrc |url=http://cvsweb.netbsd.org/bsdweb.cgi/pkgsrc/www/firefox/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181101015707/http://cvsweb.netbsd.org/bsdweb.cgi/pkgsrc/www/firefox/ |archive-date=November 1, 2018 |access-date=October 31, 2018}}</ref> and other operating systems, such as [[ReactOS]]. It is the default, pre-installed browser on [[Debian]], [[Ubuntu]], and some other Linux distros. Firefox is also available for [[Android (operating system)|Android]] and [[iOS]]. However, as with all other iOS web browsers, the iOS version uses the [[WebKit]] layout engine instead of Gecko due to platform requirements. An optimized version was also available on the [[Amazon Fire TV]] as one of the two main browsers available with Amazon's [[Amazon Silk|Silk Browser]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Firefox for Fire TV |url=https://www.amazon.com/Mozilla-Firefox-for-Fire-TV/dp/B078B5YMPD |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200707103351/https://www.amazon.com/Mozilla-Firefox-for-Fire-TV/dp/B078B5YMPD |archive-date=July 7, 2020 |access-date=July 17, 2020 |website=Amazon}}</ref> until April 30, 2021, when Firefox was discontinued on that platform.

Firefox usage share grew to a peak of 32.21% in November 2009,<ref name="StatCounter">{{cite web |url=https://gs.statcounter.com/browser-market-share/desktop/worldwide/#monthly-200901-201301 |title=Desktop Browser Market Share Worldwide (Jan 2009 – Jan 2013) |last=StatCounter |website=gs.statcounter.com |access-date=October 23, 2021 |url-status=live |archive-date=October 11, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171011022101/https://gs.statcounter.com/browser-market-share/desktop/worldwide#monthly-200901-201301}}</ref> with [[Firefox 3.5]] overtaking [[Internet Explorer 7]], although not all versions of Internet Explorer as a whole;<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://gs.statcounter.com/#browser_version-ww-weekly-200827-200951 |title=StatCounter Global Stats – Browser, OS, Search Engine including Mobile Usage Share |website=StatCounter Global Stats |access-date=July 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120526/http://gs.statcounter.com/%23mobile_browser-ww-monthly-201012-201111-bar#browser_version-ww-weekly-200827-200951 |archive-date=May 26, 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://gs.statcounter.com/#browser_version-ww-monthly-200902-201006 |title=StatCounter global stats – Top 12 browser versions |publisher=StatCounter |access-date=March 12, 2010 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120526/http://gs.statcounter.com/%23mobile_browser-ww-monthly-201012-201111-bar#browser_version-ww-monthly-200902-201006 |archive-date=May 26, 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref> its usage then declined in competition with [[Google Chrome]].<ref name="StatCounter" /> {{As of|2026|07}}, according to [[StatCounter]], it had a 6.3% [[Usage share of web browsers|usage share]] on traditional PCs (i.e. as a desktop browser), making it the third-most popular PC web browser after Google Chrome (72%) and [[Microsoft Edge]] (10%), and ahead of [[Safari (web browser)|Safari]] (5.2%).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Desktop Browser Market Share Worldwide |url=https://gs.statcounter.com/browser-market-share/desktop/worldwide/#monthly-202606-202606-bar |access-date=July 18, 2026 |website=StatCounter Global Stats }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Desktop Browser Market Share Worldwide |url=https://gs.statcounter.com/browser-market-share/desktop/worldwide/#monthly-202509-202606 |access-date=2026-07-18 |website=StatCounter Global Stats |language=en}}</ref>

== Features ==
{{Main|List of Firefox features}}

Features of the desktop edition include [[tabbed browsing]], full-screen mode, [[spell checking]], [[incremental search]], [[smart bookmark]]s, bookmarking and downloading through [[drag and drop]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Firefox Tip – Drag Bookmarks to your Toolbar |url=https://blog.mozilla.org/theden/2012/07/20/drag-bookmarks-to-your-toolbar/ |website=The Den |date=July 20, 2012 |publisher=Mozilla |access-date=October 29, 2021 |archive-date=October 29, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211029162334/https://blog.mozilla.org/theden/2012/07/20/drag-bookmarks-to-your-toolbar/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Brinkmann |first1=Martin |date=December 28, 2007 |title=Speed up the Download Process in Firefox with drag and drop? – gHacks Tech News |url=https://www.ghacks.net/2007/12/28/speed-up-download-process-in-firefox-with-drag-and-drop/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211029162334/https://www.ghacks.net/2007/12/28/speed-up-download-process-in-firefox-with-drag-and-drop/ |archive-date=October 29, 2021 |access-date=October 29, 2021 |website=gHacks Technology News}}</ref> a [[download manager]], [[User profile#Digital User Profiles|user profile]] management,<ref>{{cite web |title=Profile Manager – Create, remove or switch Firefox profiles {{!}} Firefox Help |url=https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profile-manager-create-remove-switch-firefox-profiles |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211029160607/https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profile-manager-create-remove-switch-firefox-profiles |archive-date=October 29, 2021 |access-date=October 29, 2021 |website=support.mozilla.org}}</ref> [[private browsing]], bookmark tags, bookmark [[data export|exporting]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Export Firefox bookmarks to an HTML file to back up or transfer bookmarks &#124; Firefox Help |url=https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/export-firefox-bookmarks-to-backup-or-transfer |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210812010516/https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/export-firefox-bookmarks-to-backup-or-transfer |archive-date=August 12, 2021 |access-date=August 13, 2021 |website=support.mozilla.org}}</ref> offline mode,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kaufman |first1=Lori |date=July 27, 2016 |title=How to Enable Offline Browsing in Firefox |url=https://www.howtogeek.com/263854/how-to-enable-offline-browsing-in-firefox/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210831132207/https://www.howtogeek.com/263854/how-to-enable-offline-browsing-in-firefox/ |archive-date=August 31, 2021 |access-date=August 31, 2021 |website=How-To Geek}}</ref> a [[screenshot]] tool, [[web development tools]], a "page info" feature which shows a list of page metadata and multimedia items,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Firefox Page Info window – Firefox Help |url=https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/firefox-page-info-window |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210924004942/https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/firefox-page-info-window |archive-date=September 24, 2021 |access-date=September 24, 2021}}</ref> a configuration menu at <code>about:config</code> for [[power user]]s, and location-aware browsing (also known as "[[geolocation]]") based on a Google service.<ref name="mozgeo">{{cite web |title=Location-Aware Browsing |url=https://www.mozilla.com/firefox/geolocation/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230215185449/http://www.mozilla.com/firefox/geolocation/ |archive-date=February 15, 2023 |access-date=July 5, 2009 |publisher=Mozilla Foundation}} (section "''What information is being sent, and to whom? (...)''")</ref> Firefox has an integrated search system which uses Google by default in most markets, but multiple search engines can be selected from a drop-down when searching (or custom ones added) and the default is easily changed.<ref name="techcrunch-google">{{cite web |last1=Lardinois |first1=Frederic |date=November 14, 2017 |title=Mozilla terminates its deal with Yahoo and makes Google the default in Firefox again |url=https://techcrunch.com/2017/11/14/mozilla-terminates-its-deal-with-yahoo-and-makes-google-the-default-in-firefox-again/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171114211602/https://techcrunch.com/2017/11/14/mozilla-terminates-its-deal-with-yahoo-and-makes-google-the-default-in-firefox-again/ |archive-date=November 14, 2017 |access-date=November 14, 2017 |website=TechCrunch}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Thurrott |first=Paul |date=October 9, 2021 |title=Is Mozilla Firefox getting sketchy? |url=https://www.thurrott.com/cloud/web-browsers/mozilla-firefox/258006/is-mozilla-firefox-getting-sketchy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220825172403/https://www.thurrott.com/cloud/web-browsers/mozilla-firefox/258006/is-mozilla-firefox-getting-sketchy |archive-date=August 25, 2022 |access-date=August 25, 2022 |newspaper=Thurrott.com}}</ref> [[DNS over HTTPS]] is another feature whose default behaviour is determined geographically.<ref>{{cite web |last=Porter |first=Jon |date=February 25, 2020 |title=Firefox turns controversial encryption on by default in the US |url=https://www.theverge.com/2020/2/25/21152335/mozilla-firefox-dns-over-https-web-privacy-security-encryption |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220825175408/https://www.theverge.com/2020/2/25/21152335/mozilla-firefox-dns-over-https-web-privacy-security-encryption |archive-date=August 25, 2022 |access-date=August 25, 2022 |publisher=The Verge}}</ref>

Firefox provides an environment for web developers in which they can use built-in tools, such as the Error Console or the [[DOM Inspector]], and [[browser extension|extensions]], such as [[Firebug (software)|Firebug]] and more recently there has been an integration feature with [[Pocket (service)|Pocket]]. Firefox Hello was an implementation of [[WebRTC]], added in October 2014, which allows users of Firefox and other compatible systems to have a video call, with the extra feature of screen and [[file sharing]] by sending a link to each other. Firefox Hello was scheduled to be removed in September 2016.<ref>{{cite news |last=Parrish |first=Kevin |date=August 5, 2016 |title=Hang up the phone: Mozilla to pull the plug on Firefox Hello in September |url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/mozilla-firefox-hello-discontinue-september/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170115104933/https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/mozilla-firefox-hello-discontinue-september/ |archive-date=January 15, 2017 |website=[[Digital Trends]]}}</ref>

Former features include a [[File Transfer Protocol]] (FTP) client for browsing file servers, the ability to block images from individual domains (until version 72),<ref name="FF72">{{cite web |date=January 7, 2020 |title=Firefox 72.0, See All New Features, Updates and Fixes |url=https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/72.0/releasenotes/ |url-status=live inspector]] (versions 11 to 46), tab grouping (until version 44, though a feature with the same name was added in version 137<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/137.0/releasenotes/ |title=Firefox 137.0, See All New Features, Updates and Fixes |website=Mozilla |date=April 1, 2025 |access-date=April 1, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250401150705/https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/137.0/releasenotes/ |archive-date=April 1, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>), and the ability to add customized extra toolbars (until version 28).<ref>{{cite web |date=March 8, 2016 |title=Firefox 45 Will Remove Tab Groups Today, Get This Add-on To Replace It |url=https://news.slashdot.org/story/16/03/08/1446243/firefox-45-will-remove-tab-groups-today-get-this-add-on-to-replace-it |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210812010822/https://news.slashdot.org/story/16/03/08/1446243/firefox-45-will-remove-tab-groups-today-get-this-add-on-to-replace-it |archive-date=August 12, |url=https://www.guidingtech.com/3524/extra-bookmarks-toolbar-firefox/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210812010048/https://www.guidingtech.com/3524/extra-bookmarks-toolbar-firefox/ |archive-date=August 12, 2021 |access-date=August 12, 2021 |website=Guiding === Browser extensions ===
Functions can be added through [[add-on (Mozilla)|add-ons]] created by [[third-party developer]]s. Add-ons are primarily coded using an [[HTML]], [[CSS]], [[JavaScript]], with an [[API]] known as [[WebExtensions]], which is designed to be compatible with [[Google Chrome]] and [[Microsoft Edge]] extension systems.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Browser Extensions |url=https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200719033959/https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions |archive-date=July 19, 2020 |access-date=July 16, 2020 |website=MDN Web Docs}}</ref> Firefox previously supported add-ons using the [[XUL]] and [[XPCOM]] APIs, which allowed them to directly access and manipulate much of the browser's internal functionality. As compatibility was not included in the multi-process architecture, XUL add-ons have been deemed ''Legacy add-ons'' and are no longer supported on Firefox 57 "Quantum" and later versions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Villalobos |first=Jorge |date=August 10, 2017 |title=Upcoming Changes in Compatibility Features |url=https://blog.mozilla.org/addons/2017/08/10/upcoming-changes-compatibility/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171226113447/https://blog.mozilla.org/addons/2017/08/10/upcoming-changes-compatibility/ |archive-date=December 26, 2017 |access-date=December 11, 2017 |website=Mozilla Add-ons Blog}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Bright |first=Peter |date=August 21, 2015 |title=Mozilla sets plan to dump Firefox add-ons, move to Chrome-like extensions |url=https://arstechnica.com/information-technology/2015/08/mozilla-sets-plan-to-dump-firefox-add-ons-move-to-chrome-like-extensions/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201203245/https://arstechnica.com/information-technology/2015/08/mozilla-sets-plan-to-dump-firefox-add-ons-move-to-chrome-like-extensions/ |archive-date=December 1, 2017 |access-date=December 11, 2017 |work=Ars Technica}}</ref>

Mozilla has occasionally installed extensions for users without their permission. This happened in 2017 when an extension designed to promote the show ''[[Mr. Robot]]'' was silently added in an update to Firefox.<ref>{{cite web |last=Brandom |first=Russell |date=December 16, 2017 |title=Mozilla faces blowback after slipping Mr Robot plugin into Firefox |url=https://www.theverge.com/2017/12/16/16784628/mozilla-mr-robot-arg-plugin-firefox-looking-glass |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220825145358/https://www.theverge.com/2017/12/16/16784628/mozilla-mr-robot-arg-plugin-firefox-looking-glass |archive-date=August 25, 2022 |access-date=August 25, 2022 |publisher=The Verge}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Nichols |first=Shaun |date=December 18, 2017 |title=Mozilla's creepy Mr Robot stunt in Firefox flops in touching tribute to TV show's 2nd season |url=https://www.theregister.com/2017/12/18/mozilla_mr_robot_firefox_promotion/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220825145031/https://www.theregister.com/2017/12/18/mozilla_mr_robot_firefox_promotion/ |archive-date=August 25, 2022 |access-date=August 25, 2022 |work=The Register}}</ref>

=== Themes ===
Firefox can have themes added to it, which users can create or download from third parties to change the appearance of the browser.<ref name="ars-webextensions">{{cite web |date=August 21, 2015 |title=Mozilla sets plan to dump Firefox add-ons, move to Chrome-like extensions |url=https://arstechnica.com/information-technology/2015/08/mozilla-sets-plan-to-dump-firefox-add-ons-move-to-chrome-like-extensions/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150822085215/http://arstechnica.com/information-technology/2015/08/mozilla-sets-plan-to-dump-firefox-add-ons-move-to-chrome-like-extensions/ |archive-date=August 22, 2015 |access-date=August 22, 2015 |website=Ars Technica}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Social & Communication: Add-ons for Firefox |url=https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/extensions/social-communication/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151203235652/https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/extensions/social-communication/ |archive-date=December 3, 2015 |access-date=November 16, 2015 |website=addons.mozilla.org}}</ref> Firefox also provides dark, light, and system themes.

=== Standards ===
[[File:Acid3 Mozilla Firefox test.png|thumb|The result of the [[Acid3]] test on Firefox 17]]

Firefox implements many [[web standards]], including [[HTML]], [[XML]], [[XHTML]], [[MathML]], [[SVG]] 1.1 (full),<ref>{{Cite web |title="SVG" {{!}} Can I use... Support tables for HTML5, CSS3, etc |url=https://caniuse.com/?search=SVG |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207173656/https://caniuse.com/?search=SVG |archive-date=December 7, 2023 |access-date=December 13, 2021 |website=caniuse.com}}</ref> SVG 2 (partial),<ref>{{Cite web |title=SVG 2 support in Mozilla |url=https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/SVG_2_support_in_Mozilla |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920222508/https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/SVG_2_support_in_Mozilla |archive-date=September 20, 2016 |access-date=July 13, 2016 |website=MDN Web Docs}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=SVG in Firefox |url=https://developer.mozilla.org/en/SVG_in_Firefox |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080829121506/http://developer.mozilla.org/en/SVG_in_Firefox |archive-date=August 29, 2008 |access-date=September 30, 2007}}</ref> [[CSS]] (with extensions),<ref>{{cite web |date=April 24, 2011 |title=CSS Reference: Mozilla Extensions – MDC |url=https://developer.mozilla.org/en/CSS_Reference/Mozilla_Extensions |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110824232755/https://developer.mozilla.org/en/CSS_Reference/Mozilla_Extensions |archive-date=August 24, 2011 |access-date=August 17, 2011 |publisher=Developer.mozilla.org}}</ref> [[ECMAScript]] ([[JavaScript]]), [[Document Object Model|DOM]], [[XSLT]], [[XPath]], and [[APNG]] (Animated [[PNG]]) images with [[alpha transparency]].<ref>{{cite web |date=January 21, 2007 |title=Which open standards is the Gecko development project working to support, and to what extent does it support them? |url=https://developer.mozilla.org/en/Gecko_FAQ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080913104800/http://developer.mozilla.org/en/Gecko_FAQ |archive-date=September 13, 2008 |access-date=January 24, 2007 |work=Gecko FAQ |publisher=Mozilla Developer Network}}</ref> Firefox also implements standards proposals created by the [[WHATWG]] such as client-side storage,<ref>{{cite web |date=February 7, 2007 |title=WHATWG specification&nbsp;– Web Applications 1.0&nbsp;– Working Draft. Client-side session and persistent storage |url=http://www.whatwg.org/specs/web-apps/current-work/#storage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120801065328/http://www.whatwg.org/specs/web-apps/current-work/#storage |archive-date=August 1, 2012 |access-date=February 7, 2007 |publisher=Web Hypertext Application Technology Working Group}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=September 30, 2007 |title=DOM:Storage |url=https://developer.mozilla.org/en/DOM/Storage |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080901163339/http://developer.mozilla.org/en/DOM/Storage |archive-date=September 1, 2008 |access-date=February 7, 2007 |publisher=Mozilla Developer Network}}</ref> and the [[canvas element]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Dumbill |first=Edd |date=December 6, 2005 |title=The future of HTML, Part 1: WHATWG |url=https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/xml/library/x-futhtml1/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011142035/http://www.ibm.com/developerworks/xml/library/x-futhtml1/ |archive-date=October 11, 2007 |access-date=January 24, 2007 |publisher=[[IBM]]}}</ref> These standards are implemented through the Gecko layout engine, and [[SpiderMonkey]] JavaScript engine. Firefox 4 was the first release to introduce significant HTML5 and CSS3 support.

Firefox has passed the [[Acid2]] standards-compliance test since version 3.0.<ref>{{cite web |last=Fulton |first=Scott M. |date=December 20, 2007 |title=Latest Firefox beta passes Acid2 test, IE8 claims to pass also |url=http://www.betanews.com/article/Latest-Firefox-beta-passes-Acid2-test-IE8-claims-to-pass-also/1198178648 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180628072328/https://betanews.com/2007/12/20/latest-firefox-beta-passes-acid2-test-ie8-claims-to-pass-also/ |archive-date=June 28, 2018 |access-date=December 21, 2007 |publisher=BetaNews}}</ref> Mozilla had originally stated that they did not intend for Firefox to pass the [[Acid3]] test fully because they believed that the SVG fonts part of the test had become outdated and irrelevant, due to [[WOFF]] being agreed upon as a standard by all major browser makers.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bailey |first=Daniel |title=Why Firefox 4 Will Never Pass The Acid3 Test |url=http://www.conceivablytech.com/5430/products/why-firefox-4-will-never-pass-the-acid3-test/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110203005137/http://www.conceivablytech.com/5430/products/why-firefox-4-will-never-pass-the-acid3-test/ |archive-date=February 3, 2011 |access-date=February 1, 2011}}</ref> Because the SVG font tests were removed from the Acid3 test in September 2011, Firefox 4 and greater scored 100/100.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hickson |first=Ian |date=September 17, 2011 |title=Acid3 2011 Update |url=https://plus.google.com/107429617152575897589/posts/JdHnqpuUER4 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111012170339/https://plus.google.com/107429617152575897589/posts/JdHnqpuUER4 |archive-date=October 12, 2011 |access-date=September 17, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Perry |first=Douglas |date=September 20, 2011 |title=Acid3 Test Simplified; All Modern Browsers Score 100 |url=https://www.tomsguide.com/us/acid3-browser-test-web-standard-compatibility-IE9,news-12583.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180628015834/https://www.tomsguide.com/us/acid3-browser-test-web-standard-compatibility-IE9,news-12583.html |archive-date=June 28, 2018 |access-date=July 6, 2018 |website=Tom's Guide |publisher=Purch Group}}</ref>

=== Safe browsing ===
Firefox also implements "Safe Browsing",<ref name="mozcomphishff3">{{cite web |title=Phishing and Malware Protection |url=https://www.mozilla.com/firefox/phishing-protection/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210813112436/https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/how-does-phishing-and-malware-protection-work |archive-date=August 13, 2021 |access-date=November 29, 2009 |publisher=Mozilla Corp. |at=How does Phishing and Malware Protection work in Firefox?}}</ref> a [[proprietary protocol]]<ref name="googsb2prot">{{cite web |title=Client specification for the Google Safe Browsing v2.1 protocol |url=https://code.google.com/p/google-safe-browsing/wiki/Protocolv2Spec |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100211021242/http://code.google.com/p/google-safe-browsing/wiki/Protocolv2Spec |archive-date=February 11, 2010 |access-date=November 29, 2009 |publisher=Google Inc. |quote=Do not use this protocol without explicit written permission from Google. '''Note''': This is not a license to use the defined protocol. [...]}}</ref> from Google used to exchange data related to phishing and malware protection.

=== DRM content ===
Firefox has supported playback of video content protected by [[HTML5]] [[Encrypted Media Extensions]] (EME), since version 38<!-- on Vista-->. For security and privacy reasons, EME is implemented within a wrapper of open-source code that allows execution of a [[proprietary software|proprietary]] [[digital rights management|DRM]] module by [[Adobe Systems]]—Adobe Primetime Content Decryption Module (CDM). CDM runs within a "[[sandbox (computer security)|sandbox]]" environment to limit its access to the system and provide it a randomized device ID to prevent services from [[Device fingerprint|uniquely identifying the device]] for tracking purposes. The DRM module, once it has been downloaded, is enabled and disabled in the same manner as other [[Plug-in (computing)|plug-ins]]. Firefox has supported Google's Widevine CDM on Windows and Mac OS X since version 47.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Firefox 47.0, See All New Features, Updates and Fixes |url=https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/47.0/releasenotes/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160719121556/https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/47.0/releasenotes/ |archive-date=July 19, 2016 |access-date=July 13, 2016 |website=Mozilla}}</ref> Mozilla justified its partnership with Adobe and Google by stating:
{{blockquote|Firefox downloads and enables the Adobe Primetime and Google Widevine CDMs by default to give users a smooth experience on sites that require DRM. Each CDM runs in a separate container called a sandbox and you will be notified when a CDM is in use. You can also disable each CDM and opt out of future updates by following the steps below. Once you disable a CDM, however, sites using this type of DRM may not operate properly. |source=Watch DRM content on Firefox<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/enable-drm |title=Watch DRM content on Firefox &#124; Firefox Support |website=support.mozilla.org |access-date=March 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160725223844/https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/enable-drm |archive-date=July 25, 2016 |url-status=live}}</ref>}}

and that it is "an important step on Mozilla's roadmap to remove [[NPAPI]] plugin support."<!--The Widevine CDM runs in an open-source CDM sandbox in Firefox, providing better user security than NPAPI plugins.--><ref>{{cite web |date=April 8, 2016 |title=Mozilla To Test Widevine CDM in Firefox Nightly |url=https://blog.mozilla.org/futurereleases/2016/04/08/mozilla-to-test-widevine-cdm-in-firefox-nightly/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160607175843/https://blog.mozilla.org/futurereleases/2016/04/08/mozilla-to-test-widevine-cdm-in-firefox-nightly/ |archive-date=June 7, 2016 |access-date=July 13, 2016}}</ref> Upon the introduction of EME support, builds of Firefox on Windows were also introduced that exclude support for EME.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kirk |first=Jeremy |date=May 15, 2014 |title=Mozilla hates it, but streaming video DRM is coming to Firefox |url=https://www.pcworld.com/article/2155440/firefox-will-get-drm-copy-protection-despite-mozillas-concerns.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180515132001/https://www.pcworld.com/article/2155440/firefox-will-get-drm-copy-protection-despite-mozillas-concerns.html |archive-date=May 15, 2018 |access-date=July 6, 2018 |work=PC World}}</ref><ref name="pcw-f38drm">{{cite web |last=Paul |first=Ian |date=May 13, 2015 |title=Firefox 38 arrives with contentious closed-source DRM integrated by default |url=https://www.pcworld.com/article/2922116/firefox-38-arrives-with-contentious-closed-source-drm-integrated-by-default.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150802081751/http://www.pcworld.com/article/2922116/firefox-38-arrives-with-contentious-closed-source-drm-integrated-by-default.html |archive-date=August 2, 2015 |access-date=August 12, 2015 |website=PC World}}</ref> The [[Free Software Foundation]] and [[Cory Doctorow]] condemned Mozilla's decision to support EME.<ref>{{cite web |last=Chesters |first=James |date=May 20, 2014 |title=Mixed reactions greet Mozilla plans to add HTML5 DRM in Firefox |url=https://www.infoq.com/news/2014/05/firefox-drm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190507011817/https://www.infoq.com/news/2014/05/firefox-drm |archive-date=May 7, 2019 |access-date=May 6, 2019 |publisher=InfoQ}}</ref>

===Smart Window===
Since September 1, 2026, ''Smart Window'' [[AI assistant]] is in Firefox 155.0 for users in USA, Canada, and France.<ref name="firefox/155.0/releasenotes">{{cite web |title=Firefox 155.0 Release |url=https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/155.0/releasenotes/ |website=Firefox .com |access-date=2 September 2026 |date=September 1, 2026}}</ref><ref name="betanews/firefox-155">{{cite news |title=Firefox 155: Smart Window comes to France, bugs fixed |url=https://betanews.com/article/firefox-155-smart-window-france-bug-fixes/ |access-date=2 September 2026 |work=betanews |date=1 September 2026}}</ref><ref name="theverge/981283">{{cite web |last1=Bonifield |first1=Stevie |title=Firefox’s Smart Window promises a better AI browser |url=https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/981283/mozilla-firefox-smart-window-ai-features |website=The Verge |access-date=2 September 2026 |date=18 August 2026}}</ref>

== History ==
{{See also|Firefox version history}}
The project began as an experimental branch of the [[Mozilla Application Suite|Mozilla project]] by [[Dave Hyatt]], [[Joe Hewitt (programmer)|Joe Hewitt]], and [[Blake Ross]]. They believed the commercial requirements of [[Netscape]]'s sponsorship and developer-driven [[feature creep]] compromised the utility of the Mozilla browser.<ref>{{cite web |last=Goodger |first=Ben |author-link=Ben Goodger |title=Where Did Firefox Come From? |work=Inside Firefox |publisher=MozillaZine Weblogs |date=February 6, 2006 |url=http://weblogs.mozillazine.org/ben/archives/009698.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110623034401/http://weblogs.mozillazine.org/ben/archives/009698.html |archive-date=June 23, 2011 |access-date=January 7, 2012}}</ref> To combat what they saw as the [[Mozilla Suite]]'s [[software bloat]], they created a standalone browser, with which they intended to replace the Mozilla Suite.<ref name=secrets>{{cite book |last=Yeow |first=Cheah Chu |year=2005 |title=Firefox Secrets |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sfciobmzOOcC |publisher=SitePoint Pty Ltd |isbn=978-0-9752402-4-3 |access-date=December 12, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190323104230/https://books.google.com/books?id=sfciobmzOOcC |archive-date=March 23, 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> Version 0.1, named Phoenix, was released on September 23, 2002.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.wired.com/2012/09/happy-birthday-firefox-the-little-web-browser-that-could-turns-10/ |title=Happy Birthday, Firefox: The Little Web Browser That Could Turns 10 |last=Gilbertson |first=Scott |date=September 24, 2012 |magazine=Wired |access-date=September 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170805143306/https://www.wired.com/2012/09/happy-birthday-firefox-the-little-web-browser-that-could-turns-10/ |archive-date=August 5, 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> On April 3, 2003, the [[Mozilla Foundation|Mozilla Organization]] announced that it planned to change its focus from the Mozilla Suite to Firefox and [[Mozilla Thunderbird|Thunderbird]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www-archive.mozilla.org/roadmap/roadmap-02-Apr-2003.html |title=mozilla development roadmap |last1=Eich |first1=Brendan |author-link=Brendan Eich |last2=Hyatt |first2=David |author-link2=Dave Hyatt |date=April 2, 2003 |publisher=[[Mozilla]] |access-date=August 2, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090410050040/http://www-archive.mozilla.org/roadmap/roadmap-02-Apr-2003.html |archive-date=April 10, 2009 |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Name changes ===
[[File:Phoenix 0.1.png|thumb|left|Screenshot of Phoenix 0.1 on [[Windows XP]] ]]

The Firefox project has undergone several name changes.<ref>See:
