'''HarmonyOS''' ('''HMOS''') ({{lang-zh|s=鸿蒙操作系统|p=Hóngméng Cāozuò Xìtǒng|tr=Vast Mist}}) is a [[distributed operating system]] developed by [[Huawei]] for [[smartphone]]s, [[tablet computer|tablet]]s, [[smart TV]]s, [[smart watch]]es, [[personal computers]] and other [[smart device]]s. It has a [[microkernel]] design with a single framework: the operating system selects suitable kernels from the [[abstraction layer]] in the case of devices that use diverse resources.<ref name="HarmonyOverview">{{Cite web |title=Document – About HarmonyOS |url=https://developer.harmonyos.com/en/docs/documentation/doc-guides/harmonyos-overview-0000000000011903 |access-date=June 17, 2021 |website=developer.harmonyos.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Porter|first=Jon|date=June 2, 2021|title=Huawei's Watch 3 is its first HarmonyOS smartwatch|url=https://www.theverge.com/2021/6/2/22463529/huawei-watch-3-pro-harmonyos-smartwatch-features-specs|access-date=June 16, 2021|website=The Verge}}</ref><ref name="mp"/> The latest stable version is HarmonyOS 6; it was released on 25 November 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Li |first=Deng |date=November 27, 2025 |title=Huawei Releases Stable HarmonyOS 6 Update: Device List |url=https://www.huaweicentral.com/huawei-stable-harmonyos-6-update/ |access-date=March 18, 2026 |website=Huawei Central |language=en-US}}</ref>

From 2019 to 2024, [[HarmonyOS version history#Overview|versions 1 to 4.3]] (4.5 TV) of the operating system were built by integrating the [[Android (operating system)|Android]] Open Source Project (AOSP) with [[OpenHarmony]], allowing it to support both HarmonyOS and Android apps.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 25, 2024 |title=HarmonyOS Next: Huawei gibt Android auf |url=https://www.heise.de/news/HarmonyOS-Next-Huawei-gibt-Android-auf-9776840.html |access-date=June 25, 2024 |website=heise online |language=de}}</ref> The current iteration of HarmonyOS became known as [[HarmonyOS NEXT]] (later it was renamed HarmonyOS 5 in launched of [[Huawei Pura X|Pura X]]). HarmonyOS NEXT was announced on August 4, 2023, and officially launched on October 22, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Li |first=Deng |date=October 22, 2024 |title=Huawei launched HarmonyOS NEXT, its native mobile operating system |url=https://www.huaweicentral.com/huawei-launched-harmonyos-next/ |access-date=November 18, 2024 |website=Huawei Central |language=en-US}}</ref> It also replaced the OpenHarmony multi-kernel system with its own [[HongMeng Kernel]] at its core and removed all Android code. Since version 5, HarmonyOS only supports apps in its [[Native (computing)|native]] "[[App (file format)|App]]" format.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Huawei launches beta of its non-Android phone operating system, HarmonyOS Next |url=https://www.hardwarezone.com.sg/tech-news-huawei-harmonyos-next-beta-launch-hdc-2024-non-android-phone-operating-system |access-date=June 24, 2024 |website=www.hardwarezone.com.sg |date=June 24, 2024 }}</ref><ref name="gizmochina.com">{{Cite web |title=Huawei reveals HarmonyOS NEXT will be based on Harmony Kernel |date=January 19, 2024 |url=https://www.gizmochina.com/2024/01/19/huawei-reveals-harmonyos-next-will-be-based-on-harmony-kernel/}}</ref>

HarmonyOS 5.x+ both discards the common [[Unix-like]] [[Linux kernel]] and replaces the previous multiple-kernel, kernel agnostic system from OpenHarmony with its own bespoke HarmonyOS [[microkernel]] as a single framework.

HarmonyOS was officially launched by Huawei, and first used in [[Honor (brand)|Honor]] [[smart TV]]s, in August 2019.<ref name="HuaweiCommunity">{{Cite web |title=HARMONYOS Everything about HarmonyOS (HongMeng OS) – Features, Eligible Devices, and Release |url=https://consumer.huawei.com/za/community/details/HARMONYOS-Everything-about-HarmonyOS-HongMeng-OS-Features-Eligible-Devices-and-Release/topicId_130783/ |access-date=September 16, 2023 |website=consumer.huawei.com |language=en-ZA}}</ref> It was later used in Huawei [[wireless routers]], [[Internet of things|IoT]] in 2020, followed by [[smartphone]]s, [[Tablet computer|tablets]] and [[smartwatch]]es from June 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Huawei Launches a Range of New Products Powered by HarmonyOS 2 |url=https://www.huawei.com/en/news/2021/6/huawei-launches-products-powered-by-harmonyos-2 |access-date=June 16, 2021 |website=huawei }}</ref>

In May 2025, the first [[Notebook computer|notebook]] with HarmonyOS was launched by Huawei, featuring "HarmonyOS PC", i.e. HarmonyOS 5 for the [[personal computer]] form factor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Matsui |first=Emiko |date=May 8, 2025 |title=Huawei officially introduces HarmonyOS PC operating system |url=https://www.huaweicentral.com/huawei-officially-introduces-harmonyos-pc-operating-system/ |access-date=May 14, 2025 |website=Huawei Central |language=en-US}}</ref>

On November 19, 2025, the first 2-in-1 with HarmonyOS 5.1 was launched by Huawei, with MatePad Edge supporting both tablet mode and full desktop counterpart in line with [[Huawei MateBook]] PC line.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alderson |first=Alex |date=November 20, 2025 |title=Huawei MatePad Edge reveals itself as new Apple iPad Pro and Surface Pro competitor in early previews |url=https://www.notebookcheck.net/Huawei-MatePad-Edge-reveals-itself-as-new-Apple-iPad-Pro-and-Surface-Pro-competitor-in-early-previews.1167276.0.html |access-date=November 25, 2025 |website=Notebookcheck }}</ref>

== Name ==
In 2015, Huawei launched a research and development strategy for self-developed core technologies including operating systems and databases. At that time, its own operating system did not have a name, and there was only a group of engineers designing the architecture, writing code, and designing core technologies.<ref name="wc">{{Cite web |script-title=zh:过去几年，鸿蒙受到大家很多关注，今天来聊聊到底啥是鸿蒙！|url=https://m.weibo.cn/detail/5178226075763762|access-date=June 16, 2025 |website=weibo.cn |publisher={{lang|zh-Hans|余承东}}|language=zh-CN}}</ref>

In 2019, Huawei applied for a trademark called "Huawei Hongmeng" ({{lang|zh-Hans|华为鸿蒙}}) for the kernel of its own operating system. At that time, when the company was still struggling with what to name its operating system, the public mistakenly thought the trademark of the system kernel was the name of an operating system. Finally, the official named the operating system "[[Hong Meng|Hongmeng]]" ({{lang-zh|s=鸿蒙|p=|c=|t=|l=Vast Mist}}). The name "Hongmeng" represents "the vitality of all things at the beginning of their creation". The English name chosen was "HarmonyOS", symbolizing "the interconnection of all things and harmonious coexistence."<ref name="wc"/>

== History ==
{{See also|United States sanctions against China}}

=== Early development ===
Reports surrounding an in-house operating system being developed by Huawei date back as far as 2012 in R&D stages with HarmonyOS system stack going back as early as 2015.<ref name="SCMP2021">{{Cite web|date=June 4, 2021|title=What HarmonyOS 2 means for the Google and Apple duopoly|url=https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3136017/will-huaweis-harmony-operating-system-end-global-duopoly-googles|access-date=June 21, 2021|website=South China Morning Post}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Mishra|first=Yash|date=May 20, 2019|title="Hongmeng" is Huawei's first ever self developed operating system|url=https://www.huaweicentral.com/hongmeng-is-huaweis-first-ever-self-developed-operating-system/|access-date=June 21, 2021|website=Huawei Central|language=en-US}}</ref> These reports intensified during the [[China–United States trade war|Sino-American trade war]], after the [[United States Department of Commerce]] added Huawei to its [[Entity List]] in May 2019 under an indictment that it knowingly exported goods, technology and services of U.S. origin to Iran in violation of [[United States sanctions against Iran|sanctions]]. This prohibited U.S.-based companies from doing business with Huawei without first obtaining a license from the government.<ref name="FederalRegister2019">{{Cite web|date=May 21, 2019|title=Addition of Entities to the Entity List|url=https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2019/05/21/2019-10616/addition-of-entities-to-the-entity-list|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190608070718/https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2019/05/21/2019-10616/addition-of-entities-to-the-entity-list|archive-date=June 8, 2019|access-date=June 8, 2019|website=Federal Register}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Webster|first=Graham|date=May 18, 2019|title=It's not just Huawei. [[Android (operating system)|Android]] on future [[smartphone]] products due to the sanctions.<ref name="FederalRegister2019"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3001685/huawei-confirms-it-has-built-its-own-operating-system-just-case-us|title=Huawei confirms it has its own OS on back shelf as a plan 2019|url-status=live|access-date=May 23, 2019}}</ref>

Prior to its unveiling, it was originally speculated to be a [[mobile operating system]] that could replace Android on future Huawei devices. In June 2019, an Huawei executive told [[Reuters]] that the OS was under testing in China, and could be ready "in months." But by July 2019, some Huawei executives described the OS as being an [[embedded operating system]] designed for IoT hardware, discarding the previous statements for it to be a mobile operating system.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Keane|title=Huawei says Hongmeng OS isn't designed as an Android replacement|url=https://www.cnet.com/news/huawei-says-hongmeng-os-isnt-designed-as-android-replacement/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190719184715/https://www.cnet.com/news/huawei-says-hongmeng-os-isnt-designed-as-android-replacement/|archive-date=July 19, 2019|access-date=July 19, 2019|website=CNET |date=19 July 2019 }}</ref>

Some media outlets reported that this OS, referred to as "Hongmeng", could be released in China in either August or September 2019, with a worldwide release in the second quarter of 2020.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2019/05/23/huawei-our-own-operating-system-could-be-ready-this-year.html|title=Huawei says its own operating system could be ready this year if it can't use Google or Microsoft|first=Arjun|last=Kharpal|date=May 23, 2019|work=CNBC }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.techradar.com/news/huaweis-os-to-be-rolled-out-next-month|title=Huawei says its Android OS replacement launch date is still undecided [Updated]|first1=Naushad K.|last1=Cherrayil|first2=John|last2=McCann|work=[[TechRadar]]|date=May 28, 2019 }}</ref> On 24 May 2019, Huawei registered "Hongmeng" as a [[trademark]] in China.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnet.com/news/huawei-os-reportedly-far-from-ready-after-android-ban-software/|title=Huawei OS may be called 'Hongmeng,' but it's reportedly 'far from ready'|first=Corinne|last=Reichert|website=CNET |date=24 May 2019 }}</ref> The name "Hongmeng" came from Chinese mythology that symbolizes primordial chaos or the world before creation.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Uy |first1=Ed |title=No Google, no problem? Huawei unveils its own OS – Ed Uy |url=https://businessmirror.com.ph/2019/08/17/no-google-no-problem-huawei-unveils-its-own-os/ |access-date=August 19, 2019 |work=BusinessMirror |date=August 17, 2019}}</ref> The same day, Huawei registered trademarks surrounding "Ark OS" and variants with the [[European Union Intellectual Property Office]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.androidheadlines.com/2019/05/hauweis-android-alternative-possible-name-ark-os.html|title=Huawei's Android Alternative May Be Called "Ark OS"|first=Kristijan|last=Lucic|date=May 27, 2019|access-date=May 30, 2019|publisher=Android Headlines}}</ref> In July 2019, it was reported that Huawei had also registered trademarks surrounding the word "Harmony" for desktop and mobile operating system software, indicating either a different name or a component of the OS.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thenextweb.com/plugged/2019/07/15/huawei-wants-to-name-its-android-os-replacement-harmony-in-europe/|title=Huawei wants to name its Android OS replacement 'Harmony' in Europe|last=Lakshmanan|first=Ravie|date=July 15, 2019|website=The Next Web|language=en-us|access-date=July 16, 2019}}</ref>

HarmonyOS 5 official development began in July 2021 under an internal codename "543-2" as part of entire [[OpenHarmony]] codebase Project 543 within Huawei internally since 2015 before being open sourced in September 2020 alongside the [[HongMeng Kernel]] project which officially began internally in 2016. It was first unveiled at HDC 2023, branded as HarmonyOS NEXT Developer Preview on August 4, 2023. Technical demos were on the Mate 40 Pro and MatePad Pro 12.6, which were both powered by the Kirin 9000 chip. Following the August 29, 2023 announcement of the Mate 60 Pro, featuring the Kirin 9000S, Huawei shifted development focus to the new in-house Kirin 9000S custom chip platform. At Huawei's autumn full-scenario launch event on September 25, 2023, Huawei officially launched the "HarmonyOS NEXT Program." The final known build supporting the original Kirin 9000 was HarmonyOS build 4.1.0.73, based on OpenHarmony 4.1, up-streamed with API 11. The semi-finished software Developer Preview officially released to developers on January 18, 2024, which was internally referenced to as "HarmonyOS OH1.0". It originally had selected the old standard [[Linux kernel]] of kernel-agnostic KAL system by default for OpenHarmony standard system for mobile and computing type devices in partner internal developer builds externally before retrofitting the new in-house microkernel, [[HongMeng Kernel]], which was in production on Canary builds of HarmonyOS NEXT Developer Preview on January 18, 2024. It replaced Linux kernel on physical hardware, leaving the old Linux kernel for x86 app development emulators on [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]] and [[macOS]] versions of legacy [[JetBrains]]-based DevEco Studio IDE. This build featured distinct icons and a control center design differing from the RTM version, with placeholder wallpapers. A public preview program followed on June 21, 2024, after Developer Preview 2 in April 2024. Build 5.0.0.102 became the first to identify itself as HarmonyOS 5 after replacing the 'NEXT' suffix on the build numbers throughout pre-consumer public beta builds. The PC version was showcased at the HarmonyOS Computer Technology and Ecosystem Communication Conference using MateBook Pro prototypes on May 8, 2025, as first look.<ref>{{Cite web|title=HarmonyOS 5.x|url=https://betawiki.net/wiki/HarmonyOS_5.x|website=BetaWiki|access-date=December 1, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Huawei unveils HarmonyOS for PCs|url=https://www.gizmochina.com/2025/05/08/huawei-takes-on-windows-and-macos-with-harmonyos-for-pcs/|website=Gizmochina|date=May 8, 2025|access-date=December 1, 2025|language=en-US|last=Rajesh}}</ref>

=== Framework transitions ===
Early versions of classic HarmonyOS, starting from version 1.0, employed a "kernel [[abstraction layer]]" (KAL) subsystem to support a multi-kernel architecture.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Document - About HarmonyOS |url=https://device.harmonyos.com/en/docs/documentation/guide/overview-harmonyos-0000001111162012 |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=device.harmonyos.com}}</ref> This allowed developers to choose different operating system kernels based on the resources available on each device. For low-powered devices such as wearables and Huawei's GT smartwatches, HarmonyOS utilized the LiteOS kernel instead of Linux. It also integrated the [[LiteOS]] [[Software development kit|SDK]] for TV applications and ensured compatibility with Android apps through the [[Ark Compiler]] and a dual-framework approach.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HarmonyOS/README.md at master · Awesome-HarmonyOS/HarmonyOS |url=https://github.com/Awesome-HarmonyOS/HarmonyOS/blob/master/README.md |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=GitHub }}</ref> HarmonyOS 1.0's original L0-L2 source code branch was contributed to the [[OpenAtom Foundation]] to accelerate system development.<ref>{{Cite web |title=en/device-dev/get-code/source-code-acquisition.md · OpenHarmony/docs |url=https://gitee.com/openharmony/docs/blob/bcc8e356b656a5dce685abf27ee6bb826630cbf9/en/device-dev/get-code/source-code-acquisition.md |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=Gitee |language=zh-CN}}</ref>

HarmonyOS 2.0 introduced a modified version of OpenHarmony's L3-L5 source code, expanding its compatibility across smartphones and tablets. Underneath the kernel abstraction layer (KAL) subsystem, HarmonyOS used the [[Linux kernel]] and the [[Android Open Source Project|AOSP]] codebase. This setup enabled Android [[Apk (file format)|APK]] files and [[Android App Bundle|App Bundles]] (AAB) to run natively, similar to older Huawei [[EMUI]]-based devices, without needing [[Rooting (Android)|root]] access.<ref>{{Cite web |title=OpenHarmony 2.0 L2 branch is open source, has pure HarmonyOS app code and not Android's |url=https://consumer.huawei.com/za/community/details/OpenHarmony-2-0-L2-branch-is-open-source-has-pure-HarmonyOS-app-code-and-not-Android-s/topicId_141777/ |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=consumer.huawei.com |language=en-ZA}}</ref><ref name="SCMP2021"/>

Additionally, HarmonyOS supported native apps packaged for [[Huawei Mobile Services]] through the Ark Compiler, leveraging the OpenHarmony framework within its dual-framework structure at the System Service Layer. This configuration allowed the operating system to run apps developed with restricted HarmonyOS [[API]]s.<ref name="HuaweiUpdate2021">{{Cite web |last=Amit |date=June 5, 2021 |title=HarmonyOS applications launched: More icons with HMOS corners |url=https://www.huaweiupdate.com/harmonyos-applications-launched-more-icons-with-hmos-corners/ |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=HU |language=en-US}}</ref>

Until the release of HarmonyOS 5, also known as [[HarmonyOS NEXT]], using its microkernel within a single framework{{Clarify|date=January 2026}}, replacing the operating system dual-framework approach for Huawei's HarmonyOS devices with the AOSP codebase.<ref name="gizmochina.com"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=HarmonyOS and Android: How to Establish an Independent Ecosystem? - Caixin Global |url=https://www.caixinglobal.com/2024-03-09/weekly-preview-harmonyos-and-android-how-to-establish-an-independent-ecosystem-102173753.html |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=Caixin Global }}</ref>

=== Release ===
{{See also|HarmonyOS version history}}

On 9 August 2019, three months after the [[Entity List]] ban, Huawei publicly unveiled HarmonyOS, which Huawei said it had been working on since 2012, at its inaugural developers' conference in [[Dongguan]]. Huawei described HarmonyOS as a [[Free software|free]], [[microkernel]]-based distributed operating system for various types of hardware. The company focused primarily on IoT devices, including smart TVs, [[wearable device]]s, and [[in-car entertainment]] systems, and did not explicitly position HarmonyOS as a mobile OS.<ref name="SCMP2021"/><ref name="Engadget2019">{{Cite web|url=https://www.engadget.com/2019/08/09/huawei-harmony-os-hongmeng-android/|title=Huawei reveals HarmonyOS, its alternative to Android|website=Engadget|date=August 9, 2019 |access-date=August 9, 2019}}</ref><ref name="verge-harmony">{{Cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2019/8/9/20798251/huawei-harmonyos-hongmengos-smartphones-internet-of-things-operating-system-android|title=Huawei's new operating system is called HarmonyOS|last=Porter|first=Jon|date=August 9, 2019|website=The Verge|access-date=August 9, 2019}}</ref>

HarmonyOS 2.0 launched at the Huawei Developer Conference on 10 September 2020. Huawei announced it intended to ship the operating system on its smartphones in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kharpal |first1=Arjun |title=Huawei says its own operating system HarmonyOS will come to smartphones next year |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2020/09/10/huawei-opens-harmonyos-to-third-party-smartphone-makers-after-google-ban.html |website=CNBC |date=September 10, 2020 |access-date=September 21, 2020}}</ref> The first developer beta of HarmonyOS 2.0 was launched on 16 December 2020. Huawei also released the [[DevEco Studio]] [[Integrated development environment|IDE]], which is based on [[IntelliJ IDEA]], and a cloud emulator for developers in early access.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Document – Building and Creating HAPs|url=https://developer.harmonyos.com/en/docs/documentation/doc-guides/build_hap-0000001053342418|access-date=December 20, 2020|website=developer.harmonyos.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Amadeo|first=Ron|date=February 2, 2021|title=Huawei's HarmonyOS: "Fake it till you make it" meets OS development|url=https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2021/02/harmonyos-hands-on-huaweis-android-killer-is-just-android/|access-date=February 14, 2021|website=Ars Technica|language=en-US}}</ref>

Huawei officially released HarmonyOS 2.0 and launched new devices shipping with the OS in June 2021, and started rolling out system upgrades to Huawei's older phones for users gradually.<ref name="ga"/><ref name="mp">{{Cite web|last=Porter|first=Jon|date=June 2, 2021|title=Huawei's HarmonyOS arrives on tablets with the new MatePad Pro|url=https://www.theverge.com/2021/6/2/22463666/huawei-matepad-pro-harmonyos-tablet-features-specs|access-date=June 2, 2021|website=The Verge}}</ref>

On July 27, 2022, Huawei launched HarmonyOS 3, providing an improved experience across multiple devices such as smartphones, tablets, printers, cars and TVs. It also launched Petal Chuxing, a ride-hailing app running on the new version of the operating system.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Huawei launches updated operating system HarmonyOS 3, new ride-hailing platform |url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/huawei-launches-updated-operating-system-093000179.html |access-date=July 30, 2022 |website=finance.yahoo.com |date=July 27, 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Huawei Successfully Launches HarmonyOS 3 Update, Along With The Release Of Chuxing's Ride Hailing Petal App! |url=https://voi.id/en/technology/195638/huawei-successfully-launches-harmonyos-3-update-along-with-the-release-of-chuxing-s-ride-hailing-petal-app |access-date=July 30, 2022 |website=VOI - Waktunya Merevolusi Pemberitaan |archive-date=July 30, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220730045435/https://voi.id/en/technology/195638/huawei-successfully-launches-harmonyos-3-update-along-with-the-release-of-chuxing-s-ride-hailing-petal-app |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Li |first=Deng |date=July 27, 2022 |title=HarmonyOS 3.0 Launched: Be One, Be More |url=https://www.huaweicentral.com/harmonyos-3-0-launched-be-one-be-more/ |access-date=July 30, 2022 |website=Huawei Central |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=July 27, 2022 |title=Huawei updates Android replacement, launches ride-hailing platform |url=https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-war/article/3186813/huawei-launches-updated-operating-system-harmonyos-3-new-ride-hailing |access-date=July 30, 2022 |website=South China Morning Post }}</ref>

== Features ==
=== User interface ===
The HarmonyOS interface is overhauled with native HarmonyOS Design system as "Harmonious aesthetics" philosophy<ref>{{Cite web |last=Li |first=Deng |date=October 22, 2024 |title=Huawei reveals HarmonyOS NEXT 5 UI and Performance |url=https://www.huaweicentral.com/huawei-reveals-harmonyos-next-5-ui-and-performance/ |access-date=October 23, 2024 |website=Huawei Central |language=en-US}}</ref> by Yang Zhiyan, Chief UX Designer at Huawei Consumer BG or the native launcher system that has an emphasis on 'vivid' system colours and reflective 'spatial' visual of light, blur, glow with glassmorphism and [[neumorphism]] soft UI that is a medium between [[skeuomorphism]] and [[flat design]]. In addition to standard folders that require tapping on them to display their contents, folders can be enlarged to always show their contents without text labels directly on the home screen.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Blessy |date=January 18, 2024 |title=Huawei's HarmonyOS NEXT 'Galaxy Edition' Unveiled: A Glimpse into the Future |url=https://gearbytes.co.uk/huaweis-harmonyos-next-galaxy-edition-unveiled-a-glimpse-into-the-future/ |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=Gear Bytes |language=en-US}}</ref>

Apps can support "snippets", which expose a portion of the app's functionality (such as a media player's controls, or a weather forecast) via an iOS style pop-up window by swiping left after holding the app icon in context menu, and can be pinned to the home screen as a [[Software widget|widget]]. Apps and services can provide ''cards''; as of HarmonyOS 3.0, cards can also be displayed as widgets with different sizes and shapes to adapt to the home screen layout, and can also be stacked.<ref name="GSMArena2022">{{Cite web |title=HarmonyOS 3.0 unveiled with improved homescreen, privacy and performance |url=https://www.gsmarena.com/harmonyos_30_unveiled_with_improved_homescreen_privacy_and_performance-news-55218.php |access-date=October 28, 2022 |website=GSMArena.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Document {{!}} Huawei Developers |url=https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/doc/development/quickApp-Guides/quickapp-develop-card-0000001126786241 |access-date=September 12, 2022 |website=developer.huawei.com}}</ref>

The user interface font of HarmonyOS on HarmonyOS Next base is HarmonyOS Sans. It is designed to be easy to read, unique, and universal. The system font was used throughout the operating system alongside previous Android-based EMUI 12 and up, including third-party HarmonyOS and former Android apps.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Amit |date=June 9, 2021 |title=Huawei HarmonyOS Sans font officially launched |url=https://www.huaweiupdate.com/huawei-harmonyos-sans-font-officially-launched/ |access-date=September 3, 2022 |website=Huawei Update |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Applications ===
Devices come with applications preinstalled. Further apps can be downloaded from the Huawei App Gallery. From HarmonyOS 1 to 4, the OS was heavily based on Android. This allowed the vast majority of Android apps to be used. Since the introduction of HarmonyOS 5 and further versions such as HarmonyOS 6, only native apps are available. As of March 2026, there were over 350,000 apps available.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Matsui |first=Emiko |date=March 11, 2026 |title=HarmonyOS 5/6 on its way to reach 50 million devices: Huawei |url=https://www.huaweicentral.com/harmonyos-5-6-on-its-way-to-reach-50-million-devices-huawei/ |access-date=March 18, 2026 |website=Huawei Central |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Software ===
==== Traditional apps ====
Unlike Atomic Services that are installation-free, traditional apps need installation. They are available to users through [[Huawei AppGallery]], which serves as the [[application store]] for HarmonyOS with HarmonyOS-native apps.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Document – Design Overview |url=https://developer.harmonyos.com/en/docs/design/des-guides/service-overview-0000001139795693 |access-date=June 22, 2021 |website=developer.harmonyos.com}}</ref><ref name="HuaweiUpdate2021"/> HarmonyOS-native apps have access to capabilities such as distributed communications and cards.<ref>{{Cite web |script-title=zh:阿里云资深专家崮德：谈谈我对华为HarmonyOS 2.0的看法 |url=https://segmentfault.com/a/1190000040203399 |access-date=June 23, 2021 |website=segmentfault.com |date=June 19, 2021 |language=zh-CN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dudley |first=Gavin |date=May 17, 2021 |title=HarmonyOS poised to disrupt the tech industry |url=https://www.techradar.com/news/harmonyos-poised-to-disrupt-the-tech-industry |access-date=June 24, 2021 |work=[[TechRadar]] }}</ref>

==== Atomic Services ====
Managed and distributed by Huawei Ability Gallery, Meta Services (also known as Atomic Services) replaces legacy HarmonyOS 4.x JS rpk file format Quick Apps are lightweight and consist of one or more [[App (file format)|HarmonyOS Ability Packages]] (HAPs) to implement specific convenient services, providing users with dynamic content and functionality.<ref name="metaservices" /> They are accessible via the Service Center from devices, and presented as cards that can be added to a favorite list or pinned to the home screen.<ref>{{cite web |title=Atomic Service Introduction |url=https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/doc/atomic-guides/atomic-service-definition |website=Huawei Developers |publisher=Huawei |access-date=November 15, 2025}}</ref>

Atomic Services are installation-free since the accompanying code is downloaded in the background.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Li |first=Deng |date=January 13, 2022 |title=Huawei HarmonyOS atomic services platform launched |url=https://www.huaweicentral.com/huawei-harmonyos-atomic-services-platform-launched/ |access-date=October 28, 2022 |website=Huawei Central |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="metaservices">{{Cite web |title=Atomic Service Features |url=https://developer.harmonyos.com/en/docs/documentation/doc-guides/atomic-service-definition-0000001090840664 |access-date=September 11, 2022 |website=developer.harmonyos.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Service Center Overview |url=https://developer.harmonyos.com/en/docs/documentation/doc-guides/service-center-overview-0000001162778433 |access-date=October 28, 2022 |website=developer.harmonyos.com}}</ref> They can also be synchronized across multiple devices, such as updating the driver's location on the watch in real time after the user hails a taxi on the mobile phone.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Use Cases of Atomic Services |url=https://developer.harmonyos.com/en/docs/documentation/doc-guides/atomic-service-use-cases-0000001138025291 |access-date=September 25, 2023 |website=developer.harmonyos.com}}</ref>

==== Service Collaboration Kit ====
The Service Collaboration Kit (SCK) provides users with cross-device interaction, allowing them to use the camera, scanning, and gallery functions of other devices. For example, [[Tablet computer|tablets]] or [[2-in-1 laptop]]s can utilize these features from a connected smartphone. To utilize these features, both devices running HarmonyOS NEXT must be logged into the same Huawei account and have WLAN and Bluetooth enabled.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Service Collaboration Kit丨华为开发者联盟 |url=https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/cn/sdk/service-collaboration-kit/ |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=huawei |language=zh}}</ref>

==== Harmony Intelligence ====
Harmony Intelligence allows users to deploy AI-based applications on HarmonyOS, using [[Huawei PanGu|PanGu]] 5.0 [[Large language model|LLM]] and its embedded variants, alongside new [[Celia (virtual assistant)|Celia]] capabilities, HiAI Foundation Kit, [[MindSpore]] Lite Kit, Neural Network Runtime Kit, and Computer Vision. These features improve performance, reduce power consumption, and enable efficient AI processing on devices with Kirin chips.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HiAI Foundation Kit {{!}} 华为开发者联盟 |url=https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/cn/sdk/hiai-foundation-kit/ |access-date=April 13, 2024 |website=huawei |language=zh}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Neural Network Runtime Kit {{!}} 华为开发者联盟 |url=https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/cn/sdk/neural-network-runtime-kit/ |access-date=April 13, 2024 |website=huawei |language=zh}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=MindSpore Lite Kit {{!}} 华为开发者联盟 |url=https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/cn/sdk/mindspore-lite-kit/ |access-date=April 13, 2024 |website=huawei |language=zh}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |script-title=zh:Core Vision Kit {{!}} 华为开发者联盟 |url=https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/cn/sdk/core-vision-kit/ |access-date=April 13, 2024 |website=huawei |language=zh}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=June 22, 2024 |title=Huawei Introduces Harmony Intelligence – AI Support That Will Be Integrated Into Devices |url=http://www.thecekodok.com/2024/06/huawei-introduces-harmony-intelligence.html |access-date=June 25, 2024 |website=TheCekodok.com - Your Ultimate Destination for Tech Trends and Gadget Reviews }}</ref>

==== Compatibility layer utility apps ====
HarmonyOS 5 native utility compatibility applications supported and co-developed by Chinese software partners with Huawei controlled compatibility environment such as EasyAbroad for Chinese travellers abroad and DroiTong enable Android apps to run in emulation inside a separate container which is introduced since HarmonyOS NEXT/5.x+ versions no longer natively support [[Android (operating system)|Android]] framework with [[Apk (file format)|APKs]] built from [[LXC]] and Huawei's iSula/iSulad [[openEuler]] containerised technology engines respectively integrated with LXC ABI shim interacting with HongMeng Kernel's [[Linux kernel interfaces|Linux ABI/API]] [[Shim (computing)|shim]] module as [[Binary file|binary]] compatible. The compatibility utility apps includes cloud data syncing support that enables Android app migration into the Android container utility apps from heavily modified [[Android 12]]-[[Android 13|13]] HarmonyOS 4.x/[[EMUI]] system container image tied to Huawei account. Apps downloaded via DroiTong and EasyAbroad are automatically placed into a dedicated folder on the home screen. Since HarmonyOS 6.0.0.115 build, they both can now have applications outside of the folder coexisting with native applications on the home screen and on the application center which is the system's app launcher since HarmonyOS 6.0.0.112 semi-beta and stable build. The compatibility layer utility apps are listed on AppGallery and once they become officially native on the HarmonyOS Next iterations of the HarmonyOS 5.x+ platform, the APK is automatically removed.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Surprise! Huawei's HarmonyOS NEXT can run Android apps|url=https://www.phonearena.com/news/android-apps-can-run-on-harmony-os-next_id165637|website=PhoneArena|date=December 9, 2024|access-date=December 1, 2025|language=en-US|first=Alan|last=Friedman}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Installing MetaTrader 5 and Other MetaQuotes Apps on HarmonyOS NEXT |url=https://www.mql5.com/en/articles/18612 |website=MQL5 |publisher=MetaTrader 5 — Trading |access-date=December 1, 2025}}</ref>

Unlike previous versions of HarmonyOS, Android applications are no longer compatible and cannot be downloaded from the store. Large numbers of western apps are therefore not available natively. Yet, applications such as Easy Abroad and DroiTong do allow Android apps to run in emulation inside a separate container. Apps downloaded via DroiTong are automatically placed into a dedicated folder on the home screen.<ref name="fs">{{Cite web |last=CNMO |date=December 10, 2024 |script-title=zh:卓易通App上线华为纯血鸿蒙应用市场 可下载丰富三方应用 |url=https://finance.sina.com.cn/tech/mobile/n/n/2024-12-10/doc-incywkcr2534856.shtml |access-date=July 20, 2025 |website=Sina}}</ref> This includes leading apps such as Amazon, ChatGPT, Facebook, Netflix, YouTube.<ref name="sp">{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2024 |title=Harmony OS Next doesn't natively support Android apps, but that hasn't stopped some people |url=https://www.androidauthority.com/harmony-os-next-android-apps-3505588/ |access-date=July 19, 2025 |website=Android Authority }}</ref> While these apps work, there are issues present with missed notifications, lower resolution, and file transfers in and out of the container. Apps not present include major banking apps, most streaming services, alternative mapping solutions such as Waze as well as some Google services such as Google Assistant and Gemini. Most major Chinese apps are also available, but most Chinese games are still missing.<ref name="fs"/>

For HarmonyOS computer system side powered with Kirin X series silicon custom [[AArch64]] PC chips, there is a virtual machine application on HarmonyOS called Oseasy and KaiMaster/Armor Master built on Huawei's openEuler virtualisation technology stack StratoVirt<ref>{{Cite web|title=StratoVirt - Enterprise Virtualization Platform {{!}} openEuler|url=https://www.openeuler.org/en/other/projects/stratovirt/|website=www.openeuler.org|access-date=December 1, 2025}}</ref> that enables users to run [[Windows 11]] ARM in a virtual environment on Huawei MateBook PCs and MatePad Edge.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tester ran Windows 11 on HarmonyOS PC and it worked|url=https://www.huaweicentral.com/tester-ran-windows-11-on-harmonyos-pc-and-it-worked/|website=Huawei Central|date=May 12, 2025|access-date=December 1, 2025|language=en-US|first=Emiko|last=Matsui}}</ref>
[[File:Terminal of HarmonyOS PC.jpg|thumb|HiShell default terminal on HarmonyOS computer system]]
HiSH, Harmonix, Termony third-party console applications by open source HarmonyOS developer community based on harmony-qemu FOSS project built for pure single framework [[OpenHarmony]]-based HarmonyOS platform that supports [[QEMU]] virtualization adaptations natively<ref>{{Citation|title=openharmony/vendor_ohemu|url=https://github.com/openharmony/vendor_ohemu|publisher=OpenHarmony|date=November 26, 2025|access-date=December 1, 2025}}</ref> that can enable users to run full [[Linux]] console applications and commands alongside the integration of HarmonyOS computer's default HiShell system terminal.<ref>{{Citation|title=harmoninux/HiSH|url=https://github.com/harmoninux/HiSH|publisher=Harmoninux|date=November 30, 2025|access-date=December 1, 2025}}</ref>

==== HarmonyOS computer system ====
===== HiShell system terminal =====
HiShell system terminal built on HarmonyOS PC system is based on the OpenHarmony kernel which supports commonly used debugging commands with platform native commands. Commands can be added and customized to the shell of the OpenHarmony kernel. A thin Linux-ish layer is also created for some replicated Linux-style commands out of the box from OpenHarmony's supported reimplementation of third-party [[Toybox]] command line and [[musl]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=openharmony/third_party_musl |url=https://deepwiki.com/openharmony/third_party_musl |access-date=December 7, 2025 |website=DeepWiki }}</ref> to provide POSIX like functionalities as a compatibility layer with [[HongMeng Kernel|HongMeng kernel]] [[Linux kernel interfaces|Linux API/ABI]] module for developers. However, the shell functions does not comply with the [[POSIX]] compliance standards and are used only for debugging.<ref>{{Cite web |script-title=zh:AtomGit {{!}} GitCode - 全球开发者的开源社区,开源代码托管平台 |url=https://gitcode.com/openharmony/docs/blob/OpenHarmony_feature_20250327/en/device-dev/kernel/kernel-small-debug-shell-overview.md |access-date=December 7, 2025 |website=gitcode.com |language=zh}}</ref> Since HarmonyOS 6, HiShell can be used without Developer option system settings.

Huawei launched the Converged Development Engine, also known as Fusion Development Engine, a lightweight virtualization tool available on AppGallery for HarmonyOS 6.1 computers based on StratoVirt. It allows developers to run the Linux-based [[openEuler]] server operating system environment directly on HarmonyOS PCs with a one‑click startup, supporting most Linux-based command‑line tools, [[Text-based user interface|TUI]] applications, and services integrated with native HiShell openEuler CLI terminal feature that can be used alongside to run with native apps such as CodeArts IDE, [[Remote Desktop Protocol|RDP]] clients as host and browsers with [[VNC|noVNC]] web client or [[localhost]] as well as Android containerized environments with DroiTong and EasyAbroad utility apps. The engine includes a shared folder for data exchange, snapshot backup to prevent data loss, and disk expansion to avoid storage bottlenecks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Huawei HarmonyOS update runs Linux software on desktop PCs using Converged Development Engine |url=https://www.technetbooks.com/2026/04/huawei-harmonyos-update-runs-linux.html |website=technetbooks.com |date=April 2026 |publisher=mgtid |access-date=April 2, 2026}}</ref>

===== CodeArts =====
Huawei CodeArts IDE is a cloud computing–based lightweight web IDE that enables users to  access the environment using a browser to complete coding, build and debugging functionality for [[Python (programming language)|Python]] and [[Java (programming language)|Java]] development as well as enterprise [[Android (operating system)|Android]] app development. The program can be downloaded from the AppGallery.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Min |date=May 7, 2024 |title=Huawei Cloud releases CodeArts IDE for Python |url=https://www.huaweiupdate.com/huawei-cloud-releases-codearts-ide-for-python/ |access-date=December 7, 2025 |website=HU |language=en-US}}</ref>

===== DevEco Studio =====
Huawei DevEco Studio is the official native integrated development environment to create native HarmonyOS universal [[App (file format)|HAP]] applications on PC system of HarmonyOS 6 accessed via AppGallery. Third-party native applications built on the official native IDE can be distributed via [[Huawei AppGallery|AppGallery]] app store with Huawei developer ID account. The IDE provides a suite of tools for HarmonyOS app development, including cross-platform ArkUI-X framework for [[Android (operating system)|Android]], [[iOS]] and [[Web development]], that includes real-time UI previews, ARM-based emulator, debugging, performance profiling, and flexible build options with [[Ark Compiler|ArkCompiler]] high level programming languages like [[ArkTS]] and [[Cangjie (programming language)|Cangjie]] as well as BiSheng for native C/C++ codes on the native toolchain.<ref>{{Cite web |script-title=zh:华为鸿蒙电脑应用数量月底将突破 2500 款，自研全新鸿蒙电脑 IDE DevEco Studio 预览版发布 - IT之家 |url=https://www.ithome.com/0/862/432.htm |access-date=December 7, 2025 |website=ITHome}}</ref> 

=== Super Device ===
HarmonyOS supports cross-platform interactions between supported devices via the "Super Device" interface; devices are paired via a "radar" screen by dragging icons to the centre of the screen.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sin |first=Ben |title=Huawei's 'Super Device' Connects Its Phones, Tablets And Computers For Easy Interaction |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/bensin/2022/02/28/huaweis-super-device-connects-its-phones-tablets-and-computers-for-easy-interaction/ |access-date=September 10, 2022 |website=Forbes }}</ref><ref name="HarmonyOverview"/><ref name="GSMArena2022"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=Document {{!}} HarmonyOS |url=https://developer.harmonyos.com/en/docs/design/des-guides/overview-0000001053563071 |access-date=September 10, 2022 |website=developer.harmonyos.com}}</ref> Examples of Super Device features include allowing users to play back media saved inside a smartphone through a paired PC, [[smart TV]] or [[Smart speaker|speakers]]; share PC screen recordings back to a smartphone; run multiple phone apps in a PC window; share files between a paired smartphone and PC; share application states between the paired devices, etc.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Dobie |first1=Alex |date=February 27, 2022 |title=Huawei's 'Super Device' is greater than the sum of its parts |url=https://www.androidcentral.com/huawei-superdevice-hands-greater-sum-its-parts |access-date=September 10, 2022 |website=Android Central }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=June 2, 2021 |title=HarmonyOS jumps ahead of Android with innovative 'Super Devices' and 'Task Sharing' features – Phandroid |url=https://phandroid.com/2021/06/02/harmonyos-jumps-ahead-of-android-with-innovative-super-devices-and-task-sharing-features/ |access-date=September 10, 2022 |website=phandroid.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Li |first=Deng |date=March 1, 2022 |title=Huawei Super Device, a step towards global HarmonyOS? |url=https://www.huaweicentral.com/huawei-super-device-a-step-towards-global-harmonyos/ |access-date=September 10, 2022 |website=Huawei Central |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== NearLink ===
Incorporated into HarmonyOS 4, [[NearLink]] (previously known as SparkLink) is a set of standards that combine the strengths of traditional [[Wireless communication|wireless technologies]] like [[Bluetooth]] and [[Wi-Fi]], while emphasizing improved performance in areas like response time, energy efficiency, signal range, and security. It consists of two access modes: SparkLink Low Energy (SLE) and SparkLink Basic (SLB). SLE is designed for low-power consumption, low-latency, and high-reliability applications, with a data transmission rate reportedly up to 6 times that of Bluetooth; SLB is tailored for high-speed, high-capacity, and high-precision applications, with a data transmission rate reportedly around 2 times that of Wi-Fi.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 4, 2023 |title=Huawei NearLink Technology Promises A Paradigm Shift In Wireless Connectivity {{!}} SPARROWS NEWS |url=https://sparrowsnews.com/2023/08/04/huawei-nearlink-technology-intro/ |access-date=September 16, 2023 |website=sparrowsnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ganji |first=Hamid |date=August 9, 2023 |title=Huawei NearLink is here to replace Bluetooth |url=https://www.androidheadlines.com/2023/08/huawei-nearlink-is-here-to-replace-bluetooth.html |access-date=September 16, 2023 |website=Android Headlines |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |script-title=zh:"星闪"无线连接技术优势、场景及发展思考_通信世界网 |url=http://www.cww.net.cn/article?id=581804 |access-date=September 16, 2023 |website=www.cww.net.cn |language=zh}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |script-title=zh:星闪无线短距通信技术（SparkLink 1.0）安全白皮书 — 网络安全 |url=http://sparklink.org.cn/uploads/file/20230628203056_537.pdf}}</ref>

=== File system ===
The file system reportedly employs a combining distributed file storage for the distributed file system called Harmony Distributed File System (HMDFS), local storage and integrated cloud storage services, presenting a single, streamlined space to the user. This design is intended to reduce complexity and improve ease of use. HarmonyOS PC system perform continuous, automated background optimization and clean-up of temporary or redundant files and faster boot times compared to the competition. Huawei has stated this integrated functionality aims to eliminate the user's need for third-party system optimization or disk acceleration tools without the need for [[defragmentation]]. Also, it has a built-in [[Antivirus software|anti-virus]] scanner on Files application for PC system on HarmonyOS 6. The operating system utilize the [[EROFS]] (Enhanced Read-Only File System) for critical system partitions. It is claimed to have significant performance and efficiency gains over the Linux-standard EXT4 file system, including read performance, space saving of approximately 1.6GB on system files due to its high-performance compression.  The file manager is designed with a simplified, card-based interface reminiscent of modern [[Windows 11]], Android and classic HarmonyOS 4.x tablets on PC side alongside mobile side, prioritizing quick access and clear visual management of files for ease of use when operating.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Matsui |first=Emiko |date=May 15, 2025 |title=Huawei HarmonyOS PC has faster boot time over Windows and macOS |url=https://www.huaweicentral.com/huawei-harmonyos-pc-has-faster-boot-time-over-windows-and-macos/ |access-date=December 7, 2025 |website=Huawei Central |language=en-US}}</ref>

It also features 'Network Neighbor' functionality, which supports access to shared files of other devices in the LAN network such as other computers and [[Network access server|NAS]] storage devices etc. on HarmonyOS 5.0.1 PC system side post launch.<ref>{{Cite web |script-title=zh:华为 MateBook Fold 非凡大师折叠 PC 获鸿蒙 HarmonyOS 5.0.1.315 升级，支持折叠态使用系统虚拟化能力 - IT之家 |url=https://www.ithome.com/0/862/547.htm |access-date=December 8, 2025 |website=ITHome}}</ref> The feature has been expanded to the tablet system side on HarmonyOS 6.<ref>{{Cite web |script-title=zh:华为鸿蒙 HarmonyOS 6 网络邻居功能适配机型公布，含 MatePad Pro 13.2、Mini 等平板 - IT之家 |url=https://www.ithome.com/0/899/890.htm |access-date=December 8, 2025 |website=ITHome}}</ref>

== Hardware ==
HarmonyOS platform was not designed for a single device at the beginning but developed as a distributed operating system for various devices with memory sizes ranging from 128KB to over 4GB. Hence, the hardware requirements are flexible for the operating system and it may only need 128KB of memory for a variety of smart terminal devices.<ref>{{cite web |title=In HarmonyOS 2.0, 128KB of RAM can run easily |url=https://www.realmicentral.com/2021/06/02/in-harmonyos-2-0-128kb-of-ram-can-run-easily/#:~:text=HarmonyOS%20was%20not%20designed%20for%20a%20single%20device,only%20128KB%20of%20memory%20is%20required%20to%20run. |access-date=August 28, 2022 |website=RealMi Central | date=June 2, 2021 |publisher=RMC Team}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Artashyan |first=Argam |date=September 11, 2020 |title=Harmony OS 2.0 Hardware Requirements Announced |url=https://www.gizchina.com/2020/09/11/harmony-os-2-0-hardware-requirements-announced/ |access-date=September 12, 2022 |website=Gizchina.com |language=en-US}}</ref>
