======================================================================
WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: List of acquisitions by Hewlett-Packard
======================================================================

{{Short description|None}}
[[File:HP logo 2012.svg|thumb|Hewlett-Packard logo]]
{{Use mdy dates|date=May 2014}}
[[Image:Hpwelcomesign.jpg|thumb|right|A welcome sign at the main entrance of the HP headquarters in Palo Alto]]
[[Hewlett-Packard]], commonly referred to as HP, was an electronics technology company based in [[Palo Alto, California]].  Before its 2015 split into two companies, it was known as a leading developer and manufacturer of personal computers, enterprise servers, storage devices, networking products, software, and a range of printers and other imaging products, as well as a provider of services and consulting. In 2012, HP was the largest technology company in the world in terms of revenue, ranking 10th in the [[Fortune Global 500]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://money.cnn.com/magazines/fortune/fortune500/2012/full_list/|title=Fortune 500 2012: Fortune 1000 Companies 1-100 - FORTUNE on CNNMoney.com|website=money.cnn.com}}{{dead link|date=May 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

The company was founded by [[Bill Hewlett]] and [[Dave Packard]] in a small garage on January 1, 1939, initially producing a line of electronic test and measurement equipment.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hp.com/hpinfo/abouthp/histnfacts/timeline/hist_30s.html|title=HP timeline – 1930s|publisher=HP.com| access-date =October 5, 2008}}</ref>

As of 2012, Hewlett-Packard had made a total of 129 [[Mergers and acquisitions|acquisitions]] since 1986;{{ref label|Note1|a|a}}<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.alacrastore.com/mergers-acquisitions/Hewlett_Packard_Company-1007938|title=Hewlett-Packard Company Mergers and Acquisitions|publisher=The Alacra Store| access-date =October 22, 2008}}</ref>  The majority of companies acquired by HP were based in the United States.

Its first acquisition was the FL Moseley Company in 1958. This move enabled HP to enter the [[plotter]] market, the precursor to its leading role in the printer business.<ref name="fifties">{{cite web|url=http://www.hp.com/hpinfo/abouthp/histnfacts/timeline/hist_50s.html|title=HP timeline – 1950s|publisher=HP.com| access-date =October 4, 2008}}</ref> In 1989, HP purchased [[Apollo Computer]] for US$476&nbsp;million,<ref name="apollo_a">{{cite news|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=950DE6DB173FF930A25757C0A96F948260|title=Company News; Apollo Computer Sale To Hewlett-Packard |last=Fisher|first=Lawrence M.|date=April 13, 1989|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|access-date =October 4, 2008}}</ref><ref name="apollo_b">{{cite news|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=950DE7DA143BF937A35756C0A96F948260|title=Company News; Apollo Acquisition Clears U.S. Review |date=May 4, 1989|newspaper=The New York Times|access-date =October 4, 2008}}</ref> enabling HP to become the largest supplier of [[computer workstation]]s.<ref name="apollo_a"/> In 1995, the company bought another computer manufacturer, [[Convex Computer]], for $150&nbsp;million.<ref name="convex">{{cite news|url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0EIN/is_1995_Sept_21/ai_17453733 |title=HP to Acquire Convex Computer |date=September 21, 1995 |publisher=Business Wire |access-date=October 4, 2008 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101129170420/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0EIN/is_1995_Sept_21/ai_17453733/ |archive-date=November 29, 2010 }}</ref> In 2000, HP  [[Corporate spin-off|spun off]] its early measurement, chemical and medical businesses into an independent company named [[Agilent Technologies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hp.com/hpinfo/abouthp/histnfacts/timeline/hist_90s.html|title=HP timeline – 1990s|publisher=HP.com|access-date=October 25, 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081013074626/http://www.hp.com/hpinfo/abouthp/histnfacts/timeline/hist_90s.html|archive-date=October 13, 2008|df=mdy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.agilent.com/about/companyinfo/history/index.html|title=Company History|date=June 6, 2008 |publisher=Agilent Technologies|access-date =October 25, 2008}}</ref> The company's largest acquisition came in 2002, when it merged with [[Compaq]], a personal computer manufacturer, for $25&nbsp;billion.<ref name="compaq a">{{cite press release |title=Hewlett-Packard and Compaq Agree to Merge, Creating $87 Billion Global Technology Leader |publisher=Hewlett-Packard |date=September 3, 2001  |url=http://www.hp.com/hpinfo/newsroom/press/2001/010904a.html |access-date =October 4, 2008}}</ref><ref name="compaq b">{{cite news|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9C02E7DE1739F937A3575AC0A9679C8B63|title=Hewlett-Packard in Deal to Buy Compaq for $25 Billion in Stock  |date=September 4, 2001|newspaper=The New York Times|access-date =October 4, 2008}}</ref> The combined company overtook [[Dell]] for the largest share of the personal computer market worldwide in the second quarter.<ref name="compaq c">{{cite web|url=http://news.cnet.com/2100-1001-944980.html|title=HP holds on to PC lead by a thread|last=Spooner |first=John G|date=July 18, 2002|publisher=CNET.com|access-date =October 25, 2008}}</ref>  Their last pre-split acquisition in the enterprise networking segment was [[Aruba Networks]] in March 2015 for $3&nbsp;billion.

Within IT networking hardware and storage market segments, HP made acquisitions worth over $15&nbsp;billion, including the [[3PAR]] and [[3COM]] acquisitions made in 2010, totaling over $5&nbsp;billion. Its largest IT services and consulting acquisition was [[Electronic Data Systems]] in 2008 for $13.9&nbsp;billion.

In the software products market segment, a stream of acquisitions helped strengthen HP's position.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hp.com/hpinfo/abouthp/histnfacts/timeline/hist_90s.html|title=HP timeline – 2000s|publisher=HP.com|access-date=October 25, 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081013074626/http://www.hp.com/hpinfo/abouthp/histnfacts/timeline/hist_90s.html|archive-date=October 13, 2008|df=mdy-all}}</ref> The largest software company purchased prior to 2011 was [[Mercury Interactive]] for $4.5&nbsp;billion. This acquisition doubled the size of HP's software business to more than $2 billion in annual revenue.<ref name="mercury">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/07/26/technology/26hewlett.html|title=H.P. to Pay $4.5 Billion to Acquire Mercury |date=July 26, 2006|newspaper=The New York Times|access-date =October 4, 2008|last=Darlin|first=Damon }}</ref>

In 2012 and 2013, HP had no acquisitions in any of its business segments as the firm was dealing with the aftermath of an $8.8&nbsp;billion write-off, suffered as a result of its acquisition of British software company [[Autonomy Corporation]] for $11&nbsp;billion in 2011.  In 2014, HP returned to the acquisition market by acquiring computer networking software company Shunra.

On October 6, 2014, HP announced that it would split into two companies, [[Hewlett Packard Enterprise]] and [[HP Inc]]. The former focuses on enterprise infrastructure hardware, software and services, whilst the latter focuses on consumer markets with PCs and printers. On November 1, 2015, they became separate companies.

==Acquisitions==
Each acquisition was for the respective company in its entirety, unless otherwise specified. The agreement date listed is the date of the agreement between HP and the subject of the acquisition, while the acquisition date listed is the exact date in which the acquisition completes. The value of each acquisition is usually the one listed at the time of the announcement. If the value of an acquisition is not listed, then it is undisclosed.

======================================================================
WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: List of built-in macOS apps
======================================================================

{{Short description|none}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=November 2023}}
{{Use American English|date=October 2023}}
{{macOS topics}}

This is a '''list of built-in apps''' and system components developed by [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] for [[macOS]] that come bundled by default or are installed through a system update. Many of the default programs found on macOS have counterparts on Apple's other operating systems, most often on [[iOS]] and [[iPadOS]].

Apple has also included versions of [[iWork]], [[iMovie]], and [[GarageBand]] for free with new device activations since 2013. However, these programs are maintained independently from the operating system itself.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-04-18 |title=Apple Makes iMovie, GarageBand, and iWork Apps for Mac and iOS Free for All Users |author-first1=Juli|author-last1=Clover|url=https://www.macrumors.com/2017/04/18/apple-imovie-garageband-iwork-free-for-all-users/ |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=MacRumors |language=en |archive-date=April 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210413203622/https://www.macrumors.com/2017/04/18/apple-imovie-garageband-iwork-free-for-all-users/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Similarly, [[Xcode]] is offered for free on the [[Mac App Store]] and receives updates independently of the operating system despite being tightly integrated.

== Applications ==

=== App Store ===
{{Main|Mac App Store}}

The Mac App Store is macOS's [[digital distribution]] platform for [[macOS]] apps, created and maintained by [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] based on the iOS version, the platform was announced on October 20, 2010, at Apple's "Back to the Mac" event.<ref name="Jan6">{{cite web |url=https://www.engadget.com/2010/12/16/apple-mac-app-store-open-for-business-starting-january-6th/ |title=Apple Mac App Store: hours of release, Apple announced that there were over one million downloads.<ref>{{cite press release |title=Mac App Store Downloads Top One Million in First Day |publisher=[[Apple Inc.|Apple]] === Automator ===
{{Main|Automator (macOS)}}

'''Automator''' is an app used to create [[workflow]]s for automating repetitive tasks into [[Batch processing|batches]] for quicker alteration via point-and-click (or [[drag and drop]]). This saves time and effort over human intervention to manually change each file separately. Automator enables the repetition of tasks across a wide variety of programs, including [[Macintosh Finder|Finder]], [[Safari (web browser)|Safari]], [[Calendar (Apple)|Calendar]], [[Contacts (application)|Contacts]] and others. It can also work with third-party applications such as [[Microsoft Office]], [[Adobe Photoshop]] or [[Pixelmator]].

=== Books ===
{{Main|Apple Books}}
'''Books''', previously known as iBooks, is an [[Ebook|eBook]] reading application first released with [[OS X Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-06-10 |title=Maps, iBooks, iCloud Keychain coming to OS X Mavericks |url=https://appleinsider.com/articles/13/06/10/maps-ibooks-icloud-keychain-coming-to-os-x-mavericks |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=AppleInsider |language=en |archive-date=December 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231214153635/https://appleinsider.com/articles/13/06/10/maps-ibooks-icloud-keychain-coming-to-os-x-mavericks |url-status=live }}</ref> It allows users to read and purchase digital books, as well as listen to audiobooks. Reading goals can be set which encourage users to read for an amount of time each day.

=== Calculator ===
{{Main|Calculator (Apple)}}

'''Calculator''' is a basic [[calculator]] [[application (software)|application]] made by [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] and bundled with [[macOS]]. It has three modes: basic, scientific, and programmer. Basic includes a number pad, buttons for adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing, as well as memory keys. Scientific mode supports exponents and trigonometric functions, and programmer mode gives the user access to more options related to [[computer programming]].

The Calculator program has a long history going back to the very beginning of the Macintosh platform, where a simple four-function calculator program was a standard [[desk accessory]] from the earliest system versions. Though no [[scientific calculator|higher math]] capability was included, third-party developers provided upgrades, and Apple released the [[NuCalc|Graphing Calculator]] application with the first [[PowerPC]] release (7.1.2) of the Mac OS, and it was a standard component through Mac OS 9. Apple currently ships a different application called [[Grapher]].

Calculator has [[Reverse Polish notation]] support, and can also speak the buttons pressed and result returned.

=== Calendar ===
{{Main|Calendar (Apple)}}

'''Calendar''', previously known as iCal before [[OS X Mountain Lion]], is a personal [[calendaring software|calendar app]] made by [[Apple Inc.|Apple]], originally released as a free download for [[Mac OS X v10.2]] on September 10, 2002, before being bundled with the operating system as iCal 1.5 with the release of [[Mac OS X Panther|Mac OS X v10.3]]. It tracks events and appointments added by the user and includes various holidays depending on the location the device is set to as well as birthdays from contacts. Users are also able to subscribe to other calendars from friends or third-parties.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Apple Calendar Guide: Everything You Need to Know About iCal |url=https://www.calendar.com/apple-calendar/ |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=Calendar |language=en-US |archive-date=November 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221106224708/https://www.calendar.com/apple-calendar/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-10-19 |title=AppleInsider {{!}} Road to Mac OS X Leopard: iCal 3.0 [Page 2] |url=http://www.appleinsider.com/articles/07/10/17/road_to_mac_os_x_leopard_iCal_3_0.html%26page%3D2 |access-date=2023-12-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071019015944/http://www.appleinsider.com/articles/07/10/17/road_to_mac_os_x_leopard_iCal_3_0.html%26page%3D2 |archive-date=October 19, 2007 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

iCal was the first calendar application for Mac OS X to offer support for multiple [[calendar]]s and the ability to intermittently publish/subscribe to calendars on [[WebDAV]] servers. Calendar also offers online cloud backup of calendars using Apple's [[iCloud]] service, or it can synchronize with other calendar services, including [[Google Calendar]] and [[Microsoft Exchange Server]].

=== Chess ===
[[File:Screenshot of Apple Chess.png|thumb|Screenshot of Apple Chess]]
'''Chess''' is a [[Video game graphics|3D]] [[chess]] game for [[macOS]], developed by [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] as a [[Fork (software development)|fork]] of [[GNOME Chess]] (formerly "glChess").<ref name="apple-chess-readme">{{Cite web|url = https://opensource.apple.com/source/Chess/Chess-410.4.1/README|title = Apple Chess README|access-date = January 11, 2016|website = Apple|archive-date = August 14, 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210814194758/https://opensource.apple.com/source/Chess/Chess-410.4.1/README|url-status = live}}</ref> Its history dates back to [[NeXTSTEP]] 1.0 released in September 1989.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Nathan Lineback |title=NeXTSTEP 1.0 Screen Shots |url=http://toastytech.com/guis/ns10.html |publisher=Nathan's Toasty Technology |access-date=5 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260309224243/http://toastytech.com/guis/ns10.html |archive-date=9 March 2026}}</ref> It supports [[chess variant]]s such as [[crazyhouse]] and [[losing chess]]. Apple redistributes the [[github:apple-oss-distributions/Chess/|source code]] under its own Apple Sample Code License, after a special permission has been granted from the original authors of GNOME Chess (which is licensed under [[GPL3]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://opensource.apple.com/source/Chess/Chess-318/|title = Source code of the latest version|access-date = January 11, 2016|website = [[Apple Inc.|Apple]]|archive-date = October 18, 2018|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20181018222444/https://opensource.apple.com/source/Chess/Chess-318/|url-status = live}}</ref><ref name="apple-chess-readme" /> Apple also ships the game with the [[Sjeng (software)|Sjeng]] chess engine ([[GPL]]).

=== Clock ===
{{Main|Clock (Apple)}}

'''Clock''' is a [[Timekeeper|timekeeping]] app first made available in [[macOS Ventura]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hall |first=Zac |date=2022-10-31 |title=Here's how the new Clock app can be useful on Mac |url=https://9to5mac.com/2022/10/31/macos-ventura-clock-timers/ |website=9to5Mac |access-date=December 14, 2023 |archive-date=March 25, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240325091838/https://9to5mac.com/2022/10/31/macos-ventura-clock-timers/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It allows users to view the current time in locations around the world, set alarms and timers, and use their phone as a [[stopwatch]]. Alarms and timers will play a chime once completed, which the user can choose from their ringtone library.

=== Contacts ===
{{Main|Contacts (Apple)}}

'''Contacts''', previously known as Address Book before [[OS X Mountain Lion]], is a computerized [[address book]]. Contacts can be synchronized over [[iCloud]] and other online address book services and allows for the storage of names, phone numbers, email addresses, home addresses, job titles, birthdays, and social media usernames.

=== Dictionary ===
{{Main|Dictionary (software)}}

'''Dictionary''' is an application introduced with OS X 10.4 that provides definitions and synonyms from various sources, serving as a built-in dictionary and thesaurus.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dictionary User Guide for Mac|url=https://support.apple.com/guide/dictionary/welcome/mac|access-date=October 1, 2020|website=Apple Support|language=en|archive-date=January 21, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220121192524/https://support.apple.com/guide/dictionary/welcome/mac|url-status=live}}</ref> The program also includes definitions for a list of Apple-related terms as well as access to [[Wikipedia]] articles. Dictionary supports several languages and currently provides American-English definitions from the ''[[New Oxford American Dictionary]] and Oxford American Writer's Thesaurus.''

=== FaceTime ===
{{Main|FaceTime}}

'''FaceTime''' is a [[videotelephony]] app introduced in [[Mac OS X Snow Leopard|Mac OS X 10.6.6]], replacing the video and audio calling functionality of [[iChat]] on Mac. Users can also make standard phone calls through the FaceTime app if a connected iPhone under the same Apple ID is nearby. In 2018, Apple added group video and audio support to FaceTime which can support up to 32 people alongside the release of [[macOS Mojave]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=How to place a group FaceTime call with macOS Mojave |url=https://www.cnet.com/tech/computing/how-to-place-a-group-facetime-call-with-macos-mojave/ |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=CNET |language=en |archive-date=December 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231214153636/https://www.cnet.com/tech/computing/how-to-place-a-group-facetime-call-with-macos-mojave/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

With the release of [[macOS Monterey]], Apple introduced a feature called SharePlay, which allows users to simultaneously watch videos, listen to music together, or share their display.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clark |first=Mitchell |date=2021-06-07 |title=Apple is building video and music sharing into FaceTime |url=https://www.theverge.com/2021/6/7/22522904/apple-shareplay-facetime-music-hulu-videos-tiktok-wwdc |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=The Verge |language=en |archive-date=June 15, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210615115012/https://www.theverge.com/2021/6/7/22522904/apple-shareplay-facetime-music-hulu-videos-tiktok-wwdc |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Find My ===
{{Main|Find My}}

'''Find My''' is an app and service that enables users to track the locations of [[iOS]], [[iPadOS]], [[macOS]], [[watchOS]], [[AirPods]] and [[AirTag]]s via iCloud.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clover |first=Juli |date=October 7, 2019 |title=Apple Releases macOS Catalina With Find My, Screen Time, and No More iTunes |url=https://www.macrumors.com/2019/10/07/apple-releases-macos-catalina/ |access-date=November 7, 2019 |website=MacRumors |language=en |archive-date=April 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407203036/https://www.macrumors.com/2019/10/07/apple-releases-macos-catalina/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Introduced in [[macOS Catalina]], it replaces [[Find My iPhone|Find My Mac]] and [[Find My Friends]] from previous versions. Missing devices can be made to play a sound at maximum volume, flagged as lost and locked with a passcode, or remotely erased. Users are also able to share their [[Global Positioning System|GPS locations]] with friends and family who own Apple devices of their own and can set notifications for when a person arrives or leaves a destination.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Apple's Find My app can do more than locate a lost iPhone. Here's what you need to know |url=https://www.cnet.com/tech/services-and-software/apples-find-my-app-can-do-more-than-locate-a-lost-iphone-heres-what-you-need-to-know/ |date=May 1, 2021 |first1=Jason |last1=Cipriani |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=CNET |language=en}}</ref>

=== Font Book ===
{{Main|Font Book}}

'''Font Book''' is a [[font manager]] first released with Mac OS X Panther in 2003. It allows users to browse and view all fonts installed on device, as well as install new fonts from [[.otf]] and [[TrueType|.tff]] files. A font can be selected to see its alphabets, complete repertoire of characters, and how it sets a sample text of the user's choice.

=== Freeform ===
{{Main|Freeform (Apple)}}

'''Freeform''' is a virtual [[brainstorming]] app first made available on alongside [[macOS Ventura|macOS 13.1]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-10-25 |title=iOS 16.2, iPadOS 16.2, and macOS Ventura 13.1 Betas Introduce Freeform App |url=https://www.macrumors.com/2022/10/25/ios-16-2-freeform-app/ |first1=Juli |last1=Clover |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=MacRumors |language=en |archive-date=December 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231201105703/https://www.macrumors.com/2022/10/25/ios-16-2-freeform-app/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It allows users to create canvases called "boards", which can display a range of inputs including text notes, photos, documents, and web links. The app offers real-time collaboration between users, with support for [[FaceTime]] and [[iCloud]] syncing.

=== Home ===
{{Main|Apple Home}}

'''Home''' is a [[Home automation|smart-home]] management app released with [[macOS 10.14 Mojave]], that serves as the front-end for Apple's HomeKit software framework.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Apple's Home app is coming to MacOS Mojave so you can control your smart home from your Mac |date=June 4, 2018 |first1=Megan |last1=Wollerton |url=https://www.cnet.com/home/smart-home/apples-home-app-is-coming-to-macos-mojave-so-you-can-control-your-smart-home-devices-from-your-mac/ |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=CNET |language=en}}</ref> It  lets users configure, communicate with, and control their HomeKit enabled smart appliances from a single application. Appliances can be divided into separate rooms and access to home controls can be shared with others.

=== Image Capture ===
'''Image Capture''' is an application that enables users to upload pictures from [[digital cameras]] or [[Image scanner|scanners]] which are either connected directly to their computer or network. It provides no organizational tools like [[Photos (Apple)|Photos]] but is useful for collating pictures from a variety of sources with no need for [[Device driver|drivers]].

=== Mail ===
{{Main|Apple Mail}}

'''Mail''' is an [[email client]] first originating in [[NeXTSTEP|NeXTstep]], before being carried over to Mac OS X. It is preconfigured to work with popular [[Email hosting service|email providers]], such as [[Yahoo! Mail]], [[AOL Mail]], [[Gmail]], [[Outlook.com|Outlook]] and [[iCloud]] (formerly [[MobileMe]]) and supports [[Microsoft Exchange Server|Exchange]]. Mail includes the ability to read and write emails, file emails into folders, search for emails, automatically append signatures to outgoing emails, [[Email filtering|filter out]] [[Email spam|junk mail]], and automatically unsubscribe from newsletters.

=== Maps ===
{{Main|Apple Maps}}

'''Maps''' is a [[web mapping]] app and service introduced to macOS with [[OS X Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brian |first=Matt |date=2013-06-11 |title=Apple Maps coming to OS X Mavericks |url=https://www.theverge.com/2013/6/10/4414348/apple-maps-coming-os-x-mavericks |website=The Verge |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20231009220052/https://www.theverge.com/2013/6/10/4414348/apple-maps-coming-os-x-mavericks |archive-date= Oct 9, 2023 }}</ref> It provides directions and estimated times of arrival for automobile, pedestrian, cycling and [[public transportation]] navigation. Apple Maps features a [[Flyover (Apple Maps)|Flyover]] mode that enables a user to explore certain densely populated urban centers and other places of interest in a 3D landscape composed of models of buildings and structures, as well as [[Apple Look Around|Look Around]], which allows the user to view 360° street-level imagery.

=== Messages ===
{{Main|Messages (Apple)}}

'''Messages''' is an [[instant messaging]] app introduced with [[MacOS|OS X]], replacing the messaging component of [[iChat]] in prior versions while providing support for the [[iMessage]] protocol from iOS.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patel |first=Nilay |date=2012-02-17 |title=Apple OS X 10.8 Mountain Lion preview: Notification Center, iMessage, AirPlay and more |url=https://www.theverge.com/2012/2/16/2801047/mac-os-x-10-8-mountain-lion-preview-photos-video |website=The Verge |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231206190056/https://www.theverge.com/2012/2/16/2801047/mac-os-x-10-8-mountain-lion-preview-photos-video |archive-date= Dec 6, 2023 }}</ref> A number of upgrades have been introduced to the iMessage platform over time, including message effects, editing and deleting messages within a fifteen-minute window, and a dedicated iMessage App Store which allows users to download sticker packs that can be sent in conversations.

=== Music ===
{{Main|Music (app)}}

'''Music''' is a [[Media player software|media player]] introduced macOS Catalina, replacing the music-playing capabilities of iTunes.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Apple Kills iTunes: Everything You Need to Know |url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/apple-kills-itunes-everything-you-need-to-know |first1=Jason |last1=Cohen |date=June 7, 2019 |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=PCMAG |language=en |archive-date=December 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231214153635/https://www.pcmag.com/news/apple-kills-itunes-everything-you-need-to-know |url-status=live }}</ref> It can play music files stored locally on devices and allows users to curate their song library into playlists. Songs can be purchased directly from the [[iTunes Store]] or streamed through [[Apple Music]] if the user has an active subscription. [[Internet radio]] stations can also be found within the app, with both local and international broadcasters available. Music supports lossless and spatial audio, and is capable of video playback, used primarily for music videos, artist interviews, and live performances.

=== News ===
{{Main|Apple News}}

'''News''' is a [[news aggregator]] introduced in selected regions with the release of macOS Mojave 10.14.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aleksandersen |first=Daniel |date=2020-12-22 |title=Get the Apple News app for MacOS in unsupported regions |url=https://www.ctrl.blog/entry/apple-news-macos-worldwide.html |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=ctrl.blog |language=en-US}}</ref> Users can read [[Article (publishing)|news articles]] with it, based on publishers, websites and topics they select, such as technology or politics. On March 25, 2019, Apple News+ was made available within the News app, which is a subscription service allowing access to content from a number magazines and newspapers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Edmond |date=2019-04-02 |title=Media Companies Take a Big Gamble on Apple |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/04/02/business/media/media-companies-take-a-big-gamble-on-apple.html |website=The New York Times |access-date=December 14, 2023 |archive-date=November 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211127011955/https://www.nytimes.com/2019/04/02/business/media/media-companies-take-a-big-gamble-on-apple.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Notes ===
{{Main|Notes (Apple)}}

'''Notes''' is a [[notetaking software|notetaking app]] introduced with [[OS X Mountain Lion]]. It functions as a service for making text notes and sketches, which can be synchronised between devices using Apple's [[iCloud]] service. Notes features support for advanced [[Formatted text|text formatting]] options, several styles of lists, rich web and [[Apple Maps|map]] link previews, support for more file type attachments, a corresponding dedicated attachment browser, and a system share extension point for saving web links and images.

=== Passwords ===
{{main|Passwords (Apple)}}

'''Passwords''' is an app for managing passwords, introduced in [[macOS Sequoia]]. It replaces Keychain Access.

=== Photo Booth ===
{{Main|Photo Booth}}

'''Photo Booth''' is a camera application introduced on devices running [[Mac OS X Tiger]] with a built-in iSight camera,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Apple Introduces the New iMac G5 |url=https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2005/10/12Apple-Introduces-the-New-iMac-G5/ |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=Apple Newsroom |language=en-US |archive-date=December 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231201205438/https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2005/10/12Apple-Introduces-the-New-iMac-G5/ |url-status=live }}</ref> allowing users to take picture and video.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Photo Booth User Guide for Mac|url=https://support.apple.com/en-us/guide/photo-booth/welcome/mac|access-date=January 4, 2021|website=Apple Support|language=en|archive-date=January 21, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220121192536/https://support.apple.com/guide/photo-booth/welcome/mac|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Take a photo or record a video in Photo Booth on Mac|url=https://support.apple.com/guide/photo-booth/take-a-photo-or-record-a-video-pbhlp3714a9d/mac|access-date=January 4, 2021|website=Apple Support|language=en|archive-date=January 13, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220113065118/https://support.apple.com/guide/photo-booth/take-a-photo-or-record-a-video-pbhlp3714a9d/mac|url-status=live}}</ref> Photo Booth displays a preview showing the camera's view in real time, while thumbnails of saved photos and videos are displayed along the bottom of this window, obscuring the bottom of the video preview. These can be shown or played by clicking on the thumbnails. Users can also apply a variety of effects to a photo, which act similarly to [[Filter (social media)|social media filters]].

=== Photos ===
{{Main|Photos (Apple)}}

'''Photos''' is a [[image organizer|photo management]] and [[image editing|editing]] application introduced with [[OS X Yosemite]] 10.10.3,<ref name="ReleasedLifehacker">{{cite web |last1=Klosowski |first1=Thorin |date=April 8, 2015 |title=OS X 10.10.3 Arrives with New Photos App |url=http://lifehacker.com/os-x-10-10-3-arrives-with-new-photos-app-1696493039 |access-date=April 9, 2015 |website=Lifehacker |archive-date=August 9, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160809050020/http://lifehacker.com/os-x-10-10-3-arrives-with-new-photos-app-1696493039 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="ReleasedBBC">{{cite news |last1=Simmons |first1=Dan |date=April 8, 2015 |title=Apple releases Mac app to store photos in iCloud |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-32218379 |access-date=April 9, 2015 |archive-date=October 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211006085214/https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-32218379 |url-status=live }}</ref> replacing both [[iPhoto]] and [[Aperture (software)|Aperture]].<ref name="DiscontinuedTNW">{{cite web |date=June 27, 2014 |title=The demise of Apple's Aperture and iPhoto: What does it mean for you? |url=https://thenextweb.com/creativity/2014/06/27/demise-apples-aperture-iphoto-mean/ |access-date=April 9, 2015 |website=The Next Web |archive-date=February 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210228225859/https://thenextweb.com/creativity/2014/06/27/demise-apples-aperture-iphoto-mean/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="DiscontinuedTechCrunch">{{cite web |last1=Panzarino |first1=Matthew |date=June 27, 2014 |title=Apple To Cease Development Of Aperture And Transition Users To Photos For OS X |url=https://techcrunch.com/2014/06/27/apple-to-cease-development-of-aperture-and-transition-users-to-photos-for-os-x/ |access-date=April 9, 2015 |website=TechCrunch |publisher=[[AOL]] |archive-date=July 31, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160731020941/https://techcrunch.com/2014/06/27/apple-to-cease-development-of-aperture-and-transition-users-to-photos-for-os-x/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Photos is based on the rebuilt version of the in-built app released for [[iOS 8]]. The photos library is organized chronologically on a timeline, determined by the [[metadata]] attached to the photo. Photos can also be sorted manually into albums, searched by location or by tagged persons. Photos can be synced and backed up through the [[iCloud]] Photo Library and shared albums. Photos contains a number of simple editing tools which allow users to crop, rotate, and adjust their photos, with a limited number of editing tools available for videos.

=== Podcasts ===
{{Main|Apple Podcasts}}

'''Podcasts''' is a [[Media player software|media player]] used for playing and subscribing to [[podcast]]s introduced in macOS Catalina to replace the podcasting capabilities of iTunes.<ref name=":2" /> Podcasts can be discovered and followed or subscribed to in the 'Browse' and 'Search' tabs, with the 'Listen Now’ tab showing new episodes of followed podcasts as they are made available. Podcast channels allow users to follow or subscribe to creators rather than individual shows.

=== Preview ===
{{Main|Preview (Apple)}}

'''Preview''' is an [[Image viewer|image]] and [[PDF viewer]] application, first originating in [[NeXTSTEP|NeXTstep]], before being carried over to Mac OS X. It is capable of viewing a number of viewing, printing, and editing a number [[digital image]] formats, as well as [[Portable Document File|Portable Document Format]] (PDF) files. It employs the [[Quartz (graphics layer)|Quartz]] graphics layer, and the ImageIO and [[Core Image]] frameworks.

=== QuickTime Player ===
{{Main|QuickTime}}

'''QuickTime Player''' is an application that can play compatible video and sound files.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Open and play a file in QuickTime Player on Mac|url=https://support.apple.com/guide/quicktime-player/open-and-play-a-file-qtp6cee0761b/mac|access-date=November 8, 2021|website=Apple Support|language=en|archive-date=November 9, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211109020246/https://support.apple.com/guide/quicktime-player/open-and-play-a-file-qtp6cee0761b/mac|url-status=live}}</ref> It is capable of limited editing features, including trimming video clips and exporting to one of four video resolutions or an audio-only format. QuickTime Player can also record video and audio from the device's camera and microphone, or record a user's display for screen recording.

=== Reminders ===
{{Main|Reminders (Apple)}}

'''Reminders''' is a task-managing app introduced to OS X Mountain Lion and later rebuilt from the ground up in [[MacOS Catalina]]. The app allows users to create their own lists of reminders and set notifications for themselves. New reminders can be placed into lists or set as subtasks and can include several details including: a priority tag, a note about the reminder, and an image or URL attachment. Additionally, alarms can be set for reminders, sending a notification to users at a certain time and date, when a geofence around an area is crossed, or when a message starts being typed to a set contact.

=== Safari ===
{{Main|Safari (web browser)}}

'''Safari''' is a graphical web browser based on the [[WebKit]] engine, included with macOS since version [[Mac OS X Panther|10.3 "Panther"]], where it replaces [[Internet Explorer for Mac OS X]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=WebKit |url=https://webkit.org/ |access-date=October 4, 2020 |website=WebKit |archive-date=April 10, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120410164749/http://www.webkit.org/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Websites can be bookmarked, added to a reading list, or saved to the home screen and are synced between devices through [[iCloud]]. In 2010, Safari 5 introduced a reader mode, extensions, and developer tools. Safari 11, released in 2017, added Intelligent Tracking Prevention, which uses artificial intelligence to block [[web tracking]]. Safari 13 added support for Apple Pay, and authentication with [[FIDO2 Project|FIDO2]] security keys. Its interface was redesigned in Safari 15, including a new landing page.

=== Shortcuts ===
{{Main|Shortcuts (Apple)}}

'''Shortcuts''', formerly Workflow, is a [[visual scripting]] app that allows users to create [[Macro (computer science)|macros]] for executing specific tasks on their device. These task sequences can be created by the user and shared online through [[iCloud]]. A number of curated shortcuts can also be downloaded from the integrated gallery.

=== Stickies ===
{{Main|Stickies (Apple)}}

'''Stickies''' is a [[Desktop notes|desktop note]] program first included in [[System 7|System 7.5]], later being re-written in [[Cocoa (API)|Cocoa]] during the transition to [[MacOS|Mac OS X]] in 2001. It allows a user to put [[post-it note]]-like windows on the screen for to write short reminders, notes and other clippings. The ability to collapse note windows, which is present in all versions of Stickies, is a holdover from System 7.5's [[WindowShade]] feature. The window button layout, which is unusual for a modern macOS application, is retained from [[Mac OS 8]].

=== Stocks ===
'''Stocks''' is a stock market tracking app introduced with [[macOS Mojave]].<ref>{{Cite web |author1=Mick Symons |date=2018-09-29 |title=Stocks for Mac: The ultimate guide |url=https://www.imore.com/stocks-mac-ultimate-guide |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=iMore |language=en}}</ref> It allows users to check financial data of any company publicly listed, including the current value of a company and their increase or decrease percentage. A graph shows the trends of each company over time, with a green graph showing positive growth and a red graph showing a decline. Business News is provided when a stock is not selected, which shows [[Apple News]] articles about companies a user is following.

=== System Settings ===
{{Main|System Settings}}

'''System Settings''', formerly System Preferences, is an application included with macOS. It allows users to access information about their device and modify various system settings and options on their device such as the desktop wallpaper, [[Screensaver|screen saver]], notifications, [[Wi-Fi]] and [[Bluetooth]], display and brightness, keyboard and trackpad, accessibility features, and more. With the release of [[macOS Catalina]], a [[IOS 12#Screen Time|Screen Time]] feature was introduced which is intended to help user's focus and combat screen addiction.<ref>{{Cite web |title=What is Screen Time on Mac? |url=https://support.apple.com/en-au/guide/mac-help/mchlfb0b5864/mac |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=Apple Support |language=en |archive-date=December 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231214153635/https://support.apple.com/en-au/guide/mac-help/mchlfb0b5864/mac |url-status=live }}</ref> Furthermore, [[macOS Monterey]] introduces Focus modes, which expand on Apple's previous Do Not Disturb feature to filter notifications during scenarios such as sleeping or working.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sellers |first=Dennis |date=2022-07-22 |title=The Ultimate Guide For How to Use Focus Modes Across Macs, iPhones, and iPads |url=https://eshop.macsales.com/blog/83357-the-ultimate-guide-for-how-to-use-focus-modes-across-macs-iphones-and-ipads/ |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=Rocket Yard |language=en-US |archive-date=December 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231214153636/https://eshop.macsales.com/blog/83357-the-ultimate-guide-for-how-to-use-focus-modes-across-macs-iphones-and-ipads/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== TextEdit ===
{{Main|TextEdit}}

'''TextEdit''' is an open-source [[word processor]] and text editor, first featured in NeXT's NeXTSTEP and OPENSTEP. TextEdit has support for formatted text, justification, and even the inclusion of graphics and other multimedia elements, as well as the ability to read and write to different [[character encoding]]s, including [[Unicode]] ([[UTF-8]] and [[UTF-16]]). It automatically adjusts letter spacing in addition to word spacing while justifying text. TextEdit does not support multiple columns of text.

=== TV ===
{{Main|Apple TV app}}

'''TV''', also known as '''Apple TV''', is a [[Media player software|media player]] introduced in macOS Catalina, replacing the video-playing capabilities of iTunes. The app can be used for viewing television shows and films purchased or rented through the [[iTunes Store]], which can be accessed from within the app. It also houses original content from the [[Apple TV+]] streaming service, and can even directly stream content from some third-party services through the [[A la carte pay television|a la carte]] [[video on demand]] "Apple TV Channels" service.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Holloway |first=Daniel |date=2019-03-25 |title=Apple Reveals New TV Streaming Service |url=https://variety.com/2019/tv/news/apple-tv-streaming-service-1203171335/ |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-date=September 29, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190929220531/https://variety.com/2019/tv/news/apple-tv-streaming-service-1203171335/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-03-25 |title=Apple TV Channels is an a la carte way to watch your favorite networks |url=https://www.engadget.com/2019-03-25-apple-tv-channels.html |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=Engadget |language=en-US |archive-date=December 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231214153635/https://www.engadget.com/2019-03-25-apple-tv-channels.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The TV app can be used to index and access content from other linked video on demand services, allowing programs watched in other apps to appear in a user's Up Next feed, even if they are not subscribed through the Channels service. The TV app is also capable of broadcasting live sports and events, such as through the [[MLS Season Pass]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Jay |date=2023-02-15 |title=Apple TV will stream MLS games in 1080p |url=https://www.theverge.com/2023/2/15/23601561/apple-mls-season-pass-soccer-streaming-service-1080p |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=The Verge |language=en |archive-date=October 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231004145212/https://www.theverge.com/2023/2/15/23601561/apple-mls-season-pass-soccer-streaming-service-1080p |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Voice Memos ===
'''Voice Memos''' is a [[voice recording]] app, introduced in [[macOS Mojave]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Use the Voice Memos app|url=https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT206775|access-date=January 4, 2021|website=Apple Support|language=en|archive-date=January 7, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220107123830/https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT206775|url-status=live}}</ref> designed for saving short snippets of audio for later playback. Saved voice memos can be shared as a [[MP4 file format|.m4a]] file or can be edited, which allows parts of a recording to be replaced, background noise to be removed, or the length of a recording to be trimmed.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Voice Memos User Guide for Mac|url=https://support.apple.com/guide/voice-memos/welcome/mac|access-date=January 4, 2021|website=Apple Support|language=en|archive-date=November 19, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119000229/https://support.apple.com/guide/voice-memos/welcome/mac|url-status=live}}</ref> Other playback options include the ability to change playback speed, skip silent parts of a memo, or enhance a recording. Audio files can also be organised into different folders.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 June 2020 |title=Voice Memos gains Enhanced Recording, Smart Folders in iOS 14 and macOS Big Sur |url=https://appleinsider.com/articles/20/06/30/voice-memos-gains-enhanced-recording-smart-folders-in-ios-14-and-macos-big-sur |access-date=2021-10-21 |website=AppleInsider |language=en |archive-date=April 13, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240413140911/https://appleinsider.com/articles/20/06/30/voice-memos-gains-enhanced-recording-smart-folders-in-ios-14-and-macos-big-sur |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Weather ===
{{main|Weather (Apple)}}

'''Weather''' was introduced to macOS in [[macOS Ventura]].

== Utilities ==

=== Activity Monitor ===
{{Redirect|Activity monitor|the fitness device|Activity tracker|the generic system component|System monitor}}

=== AirPort Utility ===
'''AirPort Utility''' is a program that allows users to configure an [[AirPort]] [[wireless network]] and manage services associated with and devices connected to [[AirPort#AirPort routers|AirPort Routers]]. It comes pre-installed on [[macOS]], and is available to download for [[Microsoft Windows]] and [[iOS]]. AirPort Utility is unique in that it offers network configuration in a native application as opposed to a web application. It provides a graphical overview of AirPort devices attached to a network, and provides tools to manage each one individually. It allows users to configure their network preferences, assign [[Back to My Mac]] accounts to the network, and configure USB attached Printers and hard drives.<ref name="what-is-airport-utility">{{cite web | url=http://switchtoamac.com/guides/applications/utilities/airport-utility/what-is-airport-utility.html | title=What is Airport Utility? | publisher=Switch to a Mac | date=June 15, 2009 | access-date=May 14, 2014 | archive-date=July 26, 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200726160322/https://switchtoamac.com/guides/applications/utilities/airport-utility/what-is-airport-utility.html | url-status=usurped }}</ref> The current versions are 6.3.6 for recent versions of [[macOS]], 5.6.1 for [[Microsoft Windows]] and older versions<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://support.apple.com/downloads/airport|title=Apple – Support – Downloads|website=support.apple.com|access-date=June 22, 2020|archive-date=August 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210814210658/https://support.apple.com/downloads/airport|url-status=live}}</ref> of Mac OS X,<ref name="windows">{{cite web | url=http://support.apple.com/kb/DL1547 | title=Airport Utility 5.6.1 for Windows | publisher=Apple | work=Apple Support | date=June 11, 2012 | access-date=October 14, 2014 | archive-date=February 15, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150215015500/http://support.apple.com/kb/DL1547 | url-status=live }}</ref> and 1.3.4 for [[iOS]].<ref name="itunes">{{cite web | url=https://apps.apple.com/us/app/airport-utility/id427276530 | title=AirPort Utility for iPhone, iPod touch, and iPad on the iTunes App Store | publisher=Apple | work=iTunes Preview | access-date=August 14, 2014 | archive-date=June 10, 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190610190942/https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/airport-utility/id427276530 | url-status=live }}</ref>

On January 30, 2013, Apple released AirPort Utility 6.0 for macOS featuring a redesign of the user interface focused on increasing usability for novice users.<ref name="Martellaro">{{cite web | url=http://www.macobserver.com/tmo/article/airport_utility_6_for_lion | title=AirPort Utility 6 for Lion is for Beginners | work=The Mac Observer | date=February 3, 2012 | access-date=May 14, 2014 | author=John Martellaro | archive-date=December 2, 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201202192522/https://www.macobserver.com/tmo/article/airport_utility_6_for_lion | url-status=live }}</ref> Reception was mixed with some media outlets reporting IT professionals and network administrators being frustrated over some removed features.<ref name="Martellaro" /> It was reported that most end users, however, would not notice the feature omissions.<ref name="Kessler">{{cite web | url=http://reviews.cnet.com/8301-13727_7-57369191-263/airport-utility-6.0-missing-a-number-of-features/ | title=AirPort Utility 6.0 missing a number of features | publisher=CNET | date=January 31, 2012 | author=Topher Kessler | access-date=May 14, 2014 | archive-date=October 21, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131021051319/http://reviews.cnet.com/8301-13727_7-57369191-263/AirPort-utility-6.0-missing-a-number-of-features/ | url-status=live }}</ref> Users requiring the removed features can still access the previous version of AirPort Utility using a workaround.<ref name="forum">{{cite web | url=https://discussions.apple.com/thread/4172563?start=0&tstart=0 | title=How to install AirPort Utility 5.6.1 on Mountain Lion | access-date=December 10, 2012 | archive-date=August 25, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160825232509/https://discussions.apple.com/thread/4172563?start=0&tstart=0 | url-status=live }}</ref>

Starting with [[macOS Golden Gate]], AirPort Utility is no longer included in new installations of macOS.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clover |first=Juli |date=2026-06-22 |title=Apple Dropping AirPort Utility From the App Store With iOS 27 |url=https://www.macrumors.com/2026/06/22/apple-airport-utility-ios-27/ |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=MacRumors |language=en}}</ref>

=== Audio MIDI Setup ===
'''Audio MIDI Setup''' is a utility program that comes with the [[macOS]] operating system for adjusting the computer's [[Sound|audio]] input and output configuration settings and managing [[MIDI]] devices.

It was introduced in [[Mac OS X v10.5|Mac OS X 10.5 Leopard]] as a simplified way to configure MIDI Devices. Users need to be aware that prior to this release, MIDI devices did not require this step, and mention of it might be omitted from MIDI devices from third-party manufactures.

=== Bluetooth File Exchange ===
'''Bluetooth File Exchange''' is a utility that comes with the [[macOS]] [[operating system]], used to exchange files to or from a [[Bluetooth]]-enabled device.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Share files between your Mac and Bluetooth devices |url=https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/mac-help/mchle7fa9e15/mac |access-date=March 9, 2023 |website=Apple Support |language=en |archive-date=March 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230309210239/https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/mac-help/mchle7fa9e15/mac |url-status=live }}</ref> For example, it could be used to send an image to a [[cellphone]], or to receive an image or other documents from a [[Personal digital assistant|PDA]].

=== Boot Camp Assistant ===
{{Main|Boot Camp (software)}}

'''Boot Camp Assistant''' assists users with installing [[Windows]] on their Intel Mac using Boot Camp.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://support.apple.com/boot-camp|title=Boot Camp – Apple Support|website=support.apple.com|language=en-US|access-date=November 20, 2017|archive-date=December 12, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211212084532/https://support.apple.com/boot-camp|url-status=live}}</ref> It does not support Macs with [[Apple silicon#M series|Apple silicon processors]], as [[Microsoft]] does not have a commercial version of [[Windows 10]] that runs on ARM-based processors.

=== ColorSync Utility ===
{{Main|ColorSync}}

'''ColorSync Utility''' is a macOS application used for management of color profiles and filters used in Apple's [[PDF]] workflows, or applying filters to PDF documents. The interface is composed of two parts, the document browser and the utility window. The document browser allows the user to zoom in and out of an image or apply a Filter to it. The utility window has several options, including Profile First Aid, Profiles, Devices, Filters and Calculator.

=== Console ===
'''Console''' is a [[Logging (computing)|log]] viewer developed by [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] and included with [[macOS]]. It allows users to search through all of the system's logged messages, and can alert the user when certain types of messages are logged.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.informit.com/articles/article.aspx?p=169576&seqNum=9|title=Mac OS X Panther Applications and Utilities|access-date=April 30, 2016|archive-date=September 10, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210910075514/https://www.informit.com/articles/article.aspx?p=169576&seqNum=9|url-status=live}}</ref> The Console is generally used for troubleshooting when there is a problem with the computer.<ref name="macrumor">{{cite web|url=http://guides.macrumors.com/Console|title=Console|work=Mac Guides on MacRumors|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202030417/http://guides.macrumors.com/Console|archive-date=February 2, 2017}}</ref> macOS itself, as well as any applications that are used, send a constant stream of messages to the system in the form of log files. The console allows users to read the system logs, help find certain ones, monitor them, and filter their contents.<ref name="macworld">{{Cite web|url=https://www.macworld.com/article/1061222/jan08geekfactor.html|title=Tracking down trouble with the Console|date=November 28, 2007|website=Macworld|access-date=June 22, 2020|archive-date=August 16, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210816115513/https://www.macworld.com/article/1061222/jan08geekfactor.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Clicking on "Show Log List" in the toolbar will bring up the Log List. The Log List opens a sidebar which shows all of the different logs that the system maintains. This list helps in viewing the many different logs maintained in various parts of the system by bringing them all together to one place. By clicking on a particular log category, all of the logs will be shown.<ref name="pondini">{{cite web|url=http://pondini.org/OSX/Logs.html|title=OSX Log Files|access-date=April 30, 2016|archive-date=August 17, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210817220558/http://pondini.org/OSX/Logs.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

The System Log Queries contains all of the logs that have to do with the entire system. This includes [[Operating system|system]] logs as well as individual [[Application software|application]] logs.<ref name="pondini" />

Selecting All Messages gives a live look at your computer's activities, updated live. This includes all activities from both the system as well as any applications running. Logs in this section of the Console are all formatted uniformly. They all include a [[timestamp]], the name of the [[Process (computing)|process]] or [[Application software|application]], and the actual message of the [[Logfile|log]]. When the message displayed includes a paperclip icon next to it, it means that it is a shortened version of a longer report, and clicking the icon will show the complete report.<ref name="tuts">{{cite web |url=http://computers.tutsplus.com/tutorials/how-to-use-console-your-macs-diagnostic-diary--mac-45251 |title=How To Use Console: Your Mac's Diagnostic Diary |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140429044808/http://computers.tutsplus.com/tutorials/how-to-use-console-your-macs-diagnostic-diary--mac-45251 |archive-date=April 29, 2014 |url-status=live}}.</ref>

In addition to viewing all messages, users can also create custom queries with any criteria that they like. These custom queries will filter the messages and will also be shown in the All Messages section. In order to make a new query, choose "New System Log Query" from the File menu.<ref name="MacIssues">{{cite web|url=http://www.macissues.com/2014/03/23/how-to-use-the-system-console-in-os-x/|title=How to use the system console in OS X|date=March 23, 2014|website=MacIssues|access-date=April 30, 2016|archive-date=August 16, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210816191808/http://macissues.com/2014/03/23/how-to-use-the-system-console-in-os-x/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Digital Color Meter ===
'''Digital Color Meter''' is a utility for measuring and displaying the color values of [[pixels]] displayed on the screen of a [[Apple Macintosh|Macintosh]] computer.

The utility presents a "window" onto the screen which includes a [[Cursor (computers)|cursor]] which by default is 1×1 pixel in size. The color displayed in that pixel is shown as a color value which may be represented as decimal or hexadecimal [[RGB color model|RGB]] triplets, [[CIE 1931 color space|CIE 1931]], CIE 1976 or [[Lab color space|CIELAB]] triplets or a [[Tristimulus]] triplet. The displayed color could be copied either as a solid color or as the color value which represents it, to be used in other applications (for instance an RGB triplet may be used in a color specification to be used on a [[World Wide Web]] page).

=== Disk Utility ===
{{Main|Disk Utility}}

'''Disk Utility''' is a system utility for performing disk and disk volume-related tasks. It can create, convert, backup, compress, and encrypt [[logical volume image]]s from a wide range of formats, mount or unmount [[Disk image|disk volumes]], verify a disk's integrity and repair it if damaged, and erase, format, partition, or clone disks.

=== Grapher ===
{{Main|Grapher}}

'''Grapher''' is a [[graphing calculator]] program introduced in [[Mac OS X Tiger]] that is able to create 2D and 3D graphs from simple and complex equations. Users edit the appearance of graphs by changing line colors, adding patterns to rendered surfaces, adding comments, and changing the fonts and styles used to display them. Grapher is able to create animations of graphs by changing constants or rotating them in space.

=== Keychain Access ===
{{Main|Keychain (software)}}

'''Keychain''' is the encrypted password management system in macOS, introduced with Mac OS 8.6. A keychain can contain several types of data, including passwords, [[Public-key cryptography|private keys]], [[Public key certificate|certificates]], and secure notes.

=== Migration Assistant ===
'''Migration Assistant''' is a utility by [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] that transfers data, user accounts, computer settings and apps from one [[Macintosh]] [[computer]] to another computer, or from a full drive backup. As of OS X Lion and later, it can also migrate contacts, calendars, and email accounts and other files from [[Microsoft Windows]].<ref>{{cite web |title=About Windows Migration Assistant | date=September 26, 2023 |url=http://support.apple.com/kb/ht4796?viewlocale=en_US&locale=en_US}}</ref> As of macOS Sequoia 15.4 and later, it is possible to set up a Mac using an iPhone or iPad.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Set up Mac with iPhone or iPad |url=https://support.apple.com/en-us/122216 |access-date=2025-09-26 |website=Apple Support |language=en}}</ref> Migration Assistant can be used during initial setup of a new computer or run manually on a system that has already been set up. It may be used multiple times to copy only applications, user account(s), or settings. Its primary purpose is to duplicate the contents and configuration of an existing computer user account(s) on a new one.

The Migration Assistant does not transfer the operating system of the old computer to the new one. Similarly, applications  and utilities bundled by Apple with the operating system (e.g. [[Safari (web browser)|Safari]]) are not transferred, based on the assumption that the newer machine has the same or newer version already installed. However, settings for these applications (e.g. bookmarks) are transferred.

=== Print Center ===
'''Print Center''' is a utility that allows a user to view all current and pending jobs on any connected printers or fax machines. The program will open automatically when a job is sent from the device to a printer, and allows for pending jobs may to be paused or canceled. Furthermore, it is capable of displaying information about a connected printer including approximate ink supply levels and can open Image Capture if the printer or fax has a scanner attached.

=== Screen Sharing ===
'''Screen Sharing''' is a utility that may be used to control remote computers and access their files. To connect, one may enter a VNC or Apple ID and authenticate as a local user on the remote computer, or, if the computers are linked via the same Apple ID, automatically initialise the connection. It supports features such as a shared clipboard between the two computers and remotely transferring files.
The feature must be enabled in the Sharing [[preference pane]] in [[System Settings]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Share the screen of another Mac |url=https://support.apple.com/en-lk/guide/mac-help/mh14066/mac |access-date=January 7, 2021 |website=Apple Support |language=en |archive-date=November 7, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107212750/https://support.apple.com/en-lk/guide/mac-help/mh14066/mac |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Screenshot ===
'''Screenshot''' is an application introduced with [[macOS Mojave]], replacing Grab which functioned similarly.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Take a screenshot on your Mac|url=https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT201361|access-date=October 4, 2020|website=Apple Support|language=en|archive-date=January 17, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220117100513/https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT201361|url-status=live}}</ref> The app allows for screen recording and taking screenshots, either for a single window, a selected portion of the screen, or the entire screen. Screenshot is initialized whenever the user presses the keyboard shortcuts {{Key press|Cmd|Shift|3}}, {{Key press|Cmd|Shift|4}}, {{Key press|Cmd|Shift|5}}, or {{Key press|Cmd|Shift|6}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Take screenshots or screen recordings on Mac|url=https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/take-screenshots-or-screen-recordings-mh26782/mac|access-date=October 4, 2020|website=Apple Support|language=en|archive-date=October 21, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021214928/https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/take-screenshots-or-screen-recordings-mh26782/mac|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Script Editor ===
{{Main|AppleScript Editor}}

'''Script Editor''', known as '''AppleScript Editor''' starting in Snow Leopard up until Yosemite, is a code editor for the AppleScript and JavaScript for Automation scripting languages, included in classic Mac OS and macOS.

=== System Information ===
{{Redirect|System Profiler|the generic class of programs|System profiler}}

'''System Information''', formerly '''System Profiler''', is a [[software utility]] derived from field service diagnostics produced by Apple's Service Diagnostic Engineering team, at that time located in Apple satellite buildings in [[Campbell, California]], that was bundled with the [[classic Mac OS]] since [[Mac OS 7.6]] under the name Apple System Profiler.  In [[Mac OS X 10.0]], the first release of [[macOS]], it was renamed System Profiler; with the release of [[Mac OS X Lion|Mac OS X 10.7 "Lion"]] it was again renamed to System Information.<ref name="tuaw-lion">{{cite web |last1=Sande |first1=Steven |date=April 6, 2011 |title=Mac OS X 10.7 Lion features new System Information app |url=http://www.tuaw.com/2011/04/06/mac-os-x-10-7-lion-features-new-system-information-app/ |access-date=September 22, 2013 |website=[[The Unofficial Apple Weblog]] |archive-date=September 28, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928035558/http://www.tuaw.com/2011/04/06/mac-os-x-10-7-lion-features-new-system-information-app/ |url-status=usurped }}</ref> Other new features in Lion are the ability to look up support information for the user's hardware model as well.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Etherington |first1=Darrell |date=August 11, 2011 |title=Lion 101: How to know more about your Mac |url=http://gigaom.com/2011/08/11/lion-101-how-to-know-more-about-your-mac/ |access-date=September 22, 2013 |website=GigaOM |archive-date=September 27, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927185917/http://gigaom.com/2011/08/11/lion-101-how-to-know-more-about-your-mac/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In [[OS X Mountain Lion]] and later versions of macOS users can also access System Information by holding down the [[option key]] and "System Information" will replace "About This Mac" in the [[Apple Menu]].

It compiles technical information on all of the installed hardware, devices, drivers, applications, system settings, system software programs and [[kernel extension]]s installed on the host computer. It can export this information as [[plain text]], [[Rich Text Format|RTF]] or in the [[plist]] [[XML]] format. This information is used to diagnose problems. System Profiler can be extremely useful if attempting to diagnose a hardware problem. A user can send the information directly to [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] if the user desires. It has support for scripting automation through AppleScript and some limited support in Automator.

System Information can also be accessed by using the "system_profiler" command through macOS's [[Terminal (macOS)|Terminal]] application.<ref>{{cite web |date=February 2, 2022 |title=How to Find Comprehensive Mac System Info via Terminal |url=https://osxdaily.com/2022/02/02/find-mac-system-info-terminal-system-profiler/ |access-date=March 15, 2022 |website=OSXDaily |archive-date=March 25, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220325034828/https://osxdaily.com/2022/02/02/find-mac-system-info-terminal-system-profiler/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Terminal ===
{{Main|Terminal (macOS)}}

[[File:Appleterminal2.png|thumb|Terminal 2.11 running the [[Top (software)|top]] program under macOS]]
'''Terminal''' is a [[terminal emulator]] program, first originating in [[NeXTSTEP]] and [[OPENSTEP]], before being carried over into Mac OS X.<ref>{{cite web |title=What Is Mac OS X – All Applications and Utilities – Terminal |url=https://www.apple.com/osx/apps/all.html#terminal |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130510222144/http://www.apple.com/osx/apps/all.html#terminal |archive-date=May 10, 2013 |publisher=[[Apple Inc.|Apple]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Wünschiers |first=Röbbe |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dLSqP2jWQEoC&q=terminal+originated+in+NeXTStep+and+OpenStep&pg=PA18 |title=Computational Biology: Unix/Linux, data processing and programming : with 19 figures and 12 tables |date=January 1, 2004 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-3-540-21142-6 |language=en}}</ref> It provides text-based access to the operating system, in contrast to the mostly graphical nature of the user experience of macOS, by providing a [[command-line interface]] to the operating system when used in conjunction with a [[Unix shell]], such as [[Z shell|zsh]] (the default shell since [[macOS Catalina]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Use zsh as the default shell on your Mac |url=https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT208050 |access-date=January 18, 2020 |website=Apple Support
