'''One UI 8.5''' (based on Android 16 QPR2) began initial beta testing on 8 December 2025,<ref>{{Cite news |last=|first=|date=2025-12-08|title=Samsung Launches One UI 8.5 Beta for Next-Level Ease of Use|url=https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-launches-one-ui-8-5-beta-for-next-level-ease-of-use|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260220154935/https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-launches-one-ui-8-5-beta-for-next-level-ease-of-use|archive-date=2026-02-20|access-date=2026-03-26|work=Samsung Newsroom (Global)|language=en}}</ref> and became formally available in February 2026 for the [[Samsung Galaxy S26|Galaxy S26 series]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-25|title=Stable One UI 8.5 arrives with the new Galaxy S26 series|url=https://www.androidauthority.com/one-ui-8-5-stable-3643086/|access-date=2026-03-26|website=Android Authority|language=en}}</ref> and the following month for the [[Samsung Galaxy A37 5G|Galaxy A37 5G]] and [[Samsung Galaxy A57 5G|A57 5G]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Galaxy A57 and Galaxy A37 will get six years of Android OS upgrades |url=https://www.sammobile.com/news/galaxy-a57-and-galaxy-a37-will-get-six-years-of-android-os-upgrades/ |date=2026-03-25 |access-date=2026-03-26 |website=SamMobile |language=en-US |last=Farooqui|first=Adnan|quote=Samsung has confirmed that the Galaxy A57 and Galaxy A37 will receive up to six major Android OS upgrades. Since both devices are being released with Android 16 and One UI 8.5 pre-installed, this promise covers them until Android 22.}}</ref> This version was later released for other devices starting with the [[Samsung Galaxy S25|Galaxy S25 series]] as a software update on 6 May 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shaik|first=Asif Iqbal|date=2026-05-06|title=Official One UI 8.5 rollout has started|url=https://www.sammobile.com/news/official-one-ui-8-5-rollout-has-started/|access-date=2026-05-07|website=SamMobile|language=en-US|quote=The stable One UI 8.5 update will start rolling out today, May 6, 2026, to eligible Galaxy devices. The update will first arrive in South Korea, followed by Europe, Hong Kong, India, Latin America, North America, Southeast Asia, and Taiwan.}}</ref>

This incremental update of One UI is also the first not to be released for certain devices released in 2022 despite those devices already received One UI 8.0.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mishra |first=Abhijeet |date=2026-05-29 |title=Why the Galaxy S22, A53 and other 2022 Samsung devices may not get One UI 8.5 |url=https://www.sammobile.com/news/why-galaxy-s22-a53-other-2022-devices-no-one-ui-8-5/ |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=SamMobile |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-09 |title=One UI 8.5 - why these Galaxy phones may not get the update |url=https://www.techadvisor.com/article/3160472/one-ui-8-5-why-these-galaxy-phones-may-not-get-the-update.html |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=Tech Advisor |language=en}}</ref>

The One UI 8.5 update introduces a fresh visual design, featuring transparent blur effects, floating elements, and smoother animations. Newer features for the Galaxy AI were added, such as improved call screening (with AI assistance), text-based image editing, combining objects from different photos, applying styles to images, continuous AI image generation, and Creative Studio for wallpapers, stickers, and profile images. [[Bixby (software)|Bixby]] was also updated to integrate [[Perplexity AI]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shaik |first=Asif Iqbal |date=2026-05-12 |title=Got One UI 8.5 update? Check out these top ten features |url=https://www.sammobile.com/news/one-ui-8-5-update-top-features/ |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=SamMobile |language=en-US}}</ref> Other features in the update include a built-in document scanner (in Camera app), extensive UI customizations (home screen, lock screen, and quick settings panel), [[Quick Share]] with support for [[AirDrop]], and improvements to system apps.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schoon |first=Ben |date=2026-05-11 |title=Samsung widely rolling out stable One UI 8.5 update, five months after the beta started |url=https://9to5google.com/2026/05/11/samsung-one-ui-8-5-galaxy-update-list/ |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=9to5Google |language=en-US}}</ref>

====One UI 9====
Shortly after the stable release of One UI 8.5, '''One UI 9''' (based on [[Android 17]]) started beta testing on 12 May 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bonggolto |first=Jay |date=2026-05-12 |title=One UI 9 beta arrives to give Galaxy S26 owners a taste of Android 17 |url=https://www.androidcentral.com/phones/samsung-galaxy/one-ui-9-beta-arrives-to-give-galaxy-s26-owners-a-taste-of-android-17 |access-date=2026-05-13 |website=Android Central |language=en}}</ref> It officially launched on 22 July 2026, alongside the [[Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8]] and [[Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8|Galaxy Z Flip 8]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Farooqui |first=Adnan |date=2026-07-22 |title=Stable One UI 9 arrives with the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Galaxy Z Flip 8 |url=https://www.sammobile.com/news/stable-one-ui-9-arrives-with-galaxy-z-fold-8-flip-8/ |access-date=2026-07-23 |website=SamMobile |language=en-US}}</ref> later on the Galaxy S26 FE on 27 August 2026,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sorrentino |first=Mike |date=2026-08-27 |title=Samsung's Galaxy S26 FE Has Flagship Features, but It's Harder to Call It a Bargain |url=https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/samsungs-700-galaxy-s26-fe-is-better-but-its-getting-harder-to-call-it-a-bargain/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=CNET |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-27 |title=Samsung Galaxy S26 FE: Delivering the Latest Flagship Experience, Focused on What Matters Most |url=https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-galaxy-s26-fe-delivering-the-latest-flagship-experience-focused-on-what-matters-most |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=Samsung Newsroom}}</ref> and later on 15 September 2026 as part of the [[Samsung Galaxy A08|Galaxy A08]] and [[Samsung Galaxy A18|Galaxy A18]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vlad |title=Samsung quietly makes the Galaxy A08 official with a bigger battery |url=https://www.gsmarena.com/samsung_quietly_makes_the_galaxy_a08_official_with_a_bigger_battery-news-74614.php |access-date=2026-09-16 |website=GSMArena.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Peter |title=The Samsung Galaxy A18 4G launches with a new chipset, IP64 rating and a notch |url=https://www.gsmarena.com/the_samsung_galaxy_a18_4g_launches_with_a_new_chipset_ip64_rating_and_a_notch-news-74622.php |access-date=2026-09-16 |website=GSMArena.com |language=en|date=2026-09-15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lucic |first=Kristijan |date=2026-09-15 |title=Samsung Galaxy A18 4G Is Now Official — Here Are Its Specs and Price |url=https://www.androidheadlines.com/samsung-galaxy-a18-4g |access-date=2026-09-16 |website=Android Headlines |language=en-US}}</ref> and eventually made its way to other devices, which began on 16 September 2026 with the [[Samsung Galaxy S26|Galaxy S26]] series, through a software update.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schoon |first=Ben |date=2026-09-16 |title=Samsung starts rolling out Android 17 with One UI 9, confirms initial list of Galaxy devices |url=https://9to5google.com/2026/09/16/samsung-android-17-one-ui-9-update-list/ |access-date=2026-09-16 |website=9to5Google |language=en-US}}</ref>

The stable rollout then widened to older flagships. It reached the Galaxy S25 series, [[Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7|Galaxy Z Fold 7]] and [[Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 7|Z Flip 7]] in South Korea by 28 September 2026,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keverenge |first=Hillary |date=2026-09-28 |title=The Galaxy S25 and Z7 series are joining Samsung's stable One UI 9 rollout |url=https://www.androidauthority.com/samsung-one-ui-9-galaxy-s25-fold-7-flip-7-stable-3716021/ |access-date=2026-10-25 |website=Android Authority |language=en}}</ref> the [[Samsung Galaxy S24|Galaxy S24 series]], [[Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 6|Z Fold 6]] and [[Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 6|Z Flip 6]] in the United States on 12 October,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keverenge |first=Hillary |date=2026-10-12 |title=One UI 9 reaches Galaxy S24, Z Fold 6, and Z Flip 6 in the US |url=https://www.androidauthority.com/samsung-one-ui-9-galaxy-s24-fold-6-flip-6-us-rollout-3721884/ |access-date=2026-10-25 |website=Android Authority |language=en}}</ref> and the [[Galaxy Z Fold 5]] and [[Galaxy Z Flip 5]] globally on 20 October.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shaik |first=Abid Iqbal |date=2026-10-20 |title=Samsung releases Galaxy Z Fold 5, Z Flip 5 stable One UI 9.0 update globally |url=https://www.sammobile.com/news/samsung-releases-galaxy-z-fold-5-z-flip-5-stable-one-ui-9-0-update-globally/ |access-date=2026-10-25 |website=SamMobile |language=en-US}}</ref> As with earlier versions, timing varied by model, country and carrier, and firmware for the same model was often published region by region under different CSC codes.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Aviral |date=2026-09-29 |title=One UI 9 Update Tracker: Galaxy Models, Regions and Builds |url=https://samupdater.com/one-ui-9-update-tracker/ |access-date=2026-10-25 |website=SamUpdater |language=en}}</ref>

New features in One UI 9 include My FanCam, which keeps a selected person centered in a recorded video, editable and generative cards in Now Brief, more size options for the brightness, volume and media controls in the Quick Panel, and Text Spotlight, an accessibility tool that shows selected text larger in a floating window. Some features depend on the device and region.<ref>{{Cite press release |date=2026-09-16 |title=Samsung Begins Official Rollout of One UI 9, Bringing the Latest Galaxy Experiences to More Devices |url=https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-begins-official-rollout-of-one-ui-9-bringing-the-latest-galaxy-experiences-to-more-devices |access-date=2026-10-25 |publisher=Samsung Newsroom |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite press release |date=2026-05-12 |title=Samsung Launches One UI 9 Beta for Galaxy S26 Series Users |url=https://www.samsungmobilepress.com/articles/one-ui-9-beta-launch-galaxy-s26-series |access-date=2026-10-25 |publisher=Samsung Mobile Press |language=en}}</ref>

The update makes changes to the lock screen wherein after the 13th failed unlock attempt, it locks the phone, requiring a factory reset to regain access (this only applies to devices that were launched with One UI 9).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mishra |first=Abhijeet |date=2026-07-25 |title=One UI 9 makes major lock screen security change every Galaxy user needs to know |url=https://www.sammobile.com/news/samsung-galaxy-one-ui-9-stricter-lock-screen-security/ |access-date=2026-07-25 |website=SamMobile |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Software support==
Prior to the release of One UI, Samsung provided 2 years of OS upgrades and 3 or 4 years of security updates for most of its devices.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Farooqui |first=Adnan |date=2020-09-22 |title=How long will the Samsung Galaxy S9 and Galaxy S9+ be supported? |url=https://www.sammobile.com/news/how-long-will-galaxy-s9-galaxy-s9-plus-be-supported/ |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=SamMobile |language=en-US |quote=Samsung announced [on August 2020] that it's going to support select devices for three Android OS upgrades. The eligible devices don't include Galaxy S models released before the Galaxy S10. All previous models are not eligible. |archive-date=2025-05-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250512091805/https://www.sammobile.com/news/how-long-will-galaxy-s9-galaxy-s9-plus-be-supported/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Since then, software support has been extended multiple times:
* On 5 August 2020 (during the Galaxy Unpacked event unveiling the Galaxy Note20 series), Samsung announced that it would offer up to 3 years of OS (and One UI) upgrades and 4 years of security updates for select devices released between 2019 and 2023<ref>{{Cite web |title=Samsung Raises the Bar for Mobile Experience Innovation Committing to Three Generations of Android OS Upgrades |url=https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-raises-the-bar-for-mobile-experience-innovation-committing-to-three-generations-of-android-os-upgrades |date=5 December 2020 |access-date=9 April 2021 |website=news.samsung.com |language=en |archive-date=1 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220501221909/https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-raises-the-bar-for-mobile-experience-innovation-committing-to-three-generations-of-android-os-upgrades |url-status=live }}</ref>
* On 9 February 2022 (also during the Galaxy Unpacked event unveiling the Galaxy S22 series), Samsung announced that it would offer up to 4 years of OS (and One UI) upgrades and 5 years of security updates for select phones and most tablets released between 2021 and 2024, rugged tablets released since 2024, and smartwatches released between 2021 and 2025<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |title=Samsung Sets the New Standard With Four Generations of OS Upgrades To Ensure the Most Up-to-Date and More Secure Galaxy Experience |url=https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-sets-the-new-standard-with-four-generations-of-os-upgrades-to-ensure-the-most-up-to-date-and-more-secure-galaxy-experience |access-date=2022-02-10 |website=news.samsung.com |language=en |archive-date=2023-10-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231006115357/https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-sets-the-new-standard-with-four-generations-of-os-upgrades-to-ensure-the-most-up-to-date-and-more-secure-galaxy-experience |url-status=live }}</ref>
* On 17 January 2024 (during the Galaxy Unpacked Event unveiling the Galaxy S24 series),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ivan |title=We asked Samsung why it gave its flagships 7 years of support |url=https://www.gsmarena.com/we_asked_samsung_why_it_decided_give_its_phones_7_years_of_support-news-62229.php |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=GSMArena.com |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-06-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250628174629/https://www.gsmarena.com/we_asked_samsung_why_it_decided_give_its_phones_7_years_of_support-news-62229.php |url-status=live }}</ref> Samsung announced that it would offer up to 7 years of both OS upgrades and security updates for select devices released since 2024, becoming the second manufacturer to offer 7 years of support (the first brand to do so was Google with the release of the Pixel 8 lineup<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-21 |title=Here's how Pixel's software update policy changed over the years |url=https://www.androidauthority.com/google-pixel-software-update-policy-3482984/ |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=Android Authority |language=en |quote=Google launched its seven-year software support pledge alongside the Pixel 8 series in 2023 |archive-date=2025-06-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250603055248/https://www.androidauthority.com/google-pixel-software-update-policy-3482984/ |url-status=live }}</ref>).
Enterprise edition devices have a slightly longer software support. An example would be the Enterprise edition of the Galaxy S25 series, which, for the first time on any Android device, have support for 8 OS upgrades and 8 years of security updates.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sagar |date=2025-04-06 |title=Samsung Galaxy S25 series Enterprise Edition phones will get 8 OS upgrades instead of 7 |url=https://www.gsmarena.com/samsung_galaxy_s25_series_enterprise_edition_software_update_details-news-67267.php |access-date=2026-06-01 |website=GSMArena.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

The extended software support was followed by Samsung's low-end and mid-range phones released since 2025 and smartwatches sold since 2026:

*It expanded with 6 years of OS and security updates with the release of Galaxy A16,<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |date=27 November 2024 |title=Samsung Galaxy A16 5G: Built to Last with 6x OS Upgrades |url=https://news.samsung.com/my/samsung-galaxy-a16-5g-built-to-last-with-6x-os-upgrades |website=Samsung Newsroom (Malaysia) |access-date=9 February 2025 |archive-date=21 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250821154552/https://news.samsung.com/my/samsung-galaxy-a16-5g-built-to-last-with-6x-os-upgrades |url-status=live }}</ref> Galaxy A26, A36, A56,<ref name=":11">{{Cite web |last=Jain |first=Anshuman |date=2025-03-02 |title=Samsung Unveils 2025 Galaxy A Series with new AI Goodies, 6-Year Update Promise |url=https://beebom.com/samsung-2025-galaxy-a-series-a56-a36-a26-announced/ |access-date=2025-03-08 |website=Beebom |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-08-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250824182316/https://beebom.com/samsung-2025-galaxy-a-series-a56-a36-a26-announced/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and the Galaxy A07<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peter |title=Samsung Galaxy A07 (4G) unveiled with Helio G99, 6 years of OS updates |url=https://www.gsmarena.com/samsung_galaxy_a07_4g_unveiled_with_helio_g99_6_years_of_os_updates-news-69194.php |access-date=2025-08-30 |website=GSMArena.com |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-08-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250826015906/https://www.gsmarena.com/samsung_galaxy_a07_4g_unveiled_with_helio_g99_6_years_of_os_updates-news-69194.php |url-status=live }}</ref> (including their respective Galaxy M and F series counterparts).
*Additionally, they provided 4 years of OS and security updates only for the following devices: the Galaxy A06 5G, and its rebranded versions, Galaxy F06 5G (sold in India), Galaxy M06 5G (sold online in select countries), and the Galaxy A25 (Japan variant).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ivan |title=Samsung resurrects Galaxy A25 5G as a dual-camera version for Japan |url=https://www.gsmarena.com/samsung_resurrects_galaxy_a25_5g_as_a_dualcamera_version_for_japan-news-66547.php |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=GSMArena.com |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-02-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250218030434/https://www.gsmarena.com/samsung_resurrects_galaxy_a25_5g_as_a_dualcamera_version_for_japan-news-66547.php |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Valiyathara |first=Anvinraj |date=2025-02-13 |title=Samsung Galaxy F06 5G launched for Rs 9,499, promises four 4 years of OS upgrades |url=https://www.gizmochina.com/2025/02/13/samsung-galaxy-f06-5g-launched-for-rs-9499-promises-four-4-years-of-os-upgrades/ |access-date=2025-02-15 |website=Gizmochina |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gsmarena.com/mwc_is_here_infinix_nothing_samsung_apple_make_announcements_week_10_in_review-news-66857.php |title=MWC 2025 saw announcements from Samsung, Nothing and others, Week 10 in review |publisher=GSMArena |date=March 10, 2025 |last=Ivan |accessdate=May 7, 2025 |archive-date=August 22, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250822054414/https://www.gsmarena.com/mwc_is_here_infinix_nothing_samsung_apple_make_announcements_week_10_in_review-news-66857.php |url-status=live }}</ref>
*It currently provides 5 years of OS and security updates for the Galaxy Watch 9 series and later smartwatches as well.<ref name=":12" />

Galaxy Book devices are subject to the Windows support life cycle. Samsung has no control on restricting Windows feature updates and Microsoft does not restrict feature updates on computers.

WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: Outline of Apple Inc.
======================================================================

{{Short description|American multinational technology company}} <!-- Should describe the topic, not the "Outline of" portion of the title; See [[WP:SDLIST]] -->
<!--               This is an outline,
        part of the set of 870+ outlines listed at

The following '''outline of Apple Inc.''' is a topical guide to [[List of Apple products|the products]], [[History of Apple Inc.|history]], [[Apple Store|retail stores]], [[List of mergers and acquisitions by Apple|corporate acquisitions]], and personnel under the purview of the American [[multinational corporation]].

[[Apple Inc.]] was founded as Apple Computer Company on April 1, 1976, to produce and market [[Steve Wozniak]]'s [[Apple I]] personal computer. The company was incorporated by Wozniak and [[Steve Jobs]] in 1977. Apple became the first publicly traded U.S. company to be [[Trillion-dollar company|valued at over $1&nbsp;trillion]] in August 2018, $2&nbsp;trillion in August 2020, and at $3&nbsp;trillion in January 2022. Since 2011, Apple has been the world's [[List of public corporations by market capitalization|largest company by market capitalization]] except when [[Microsoft]] held the position between January and June 2024.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Microsoft Tops Apple to Become Most Valuable Public Company – The New York Times |work=The New York Times |date=January 12, 2024 |access-date=February 21, 2024 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/01/12/technology/microsoft-apple-most-valuable-company.html|archive-date=January 31, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240131175132/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/01/12/technology/microsoft-apple-most-valuable-company.html|url-status=live |last1=Mickle |first1=Tripp |last2=Weise |first2=Karen}}</ref> As of March 2014, the company has 425 stores in 16 countries<ref>[http://www.apple.com/retail/storelist|title=Apple Retail Store – Store List]</ref> and an online store in 39 countries.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://store.apple.com/us/browse/open/country_selector |title=Apple Store – International |date=January 19, 2016}}</ref>

**[[MacBook Pro]] &ndash; pro notebook
*[[iMac]] &ndash; all-in-one consumer desktop
*[[Mac Mini]] &ndash; small form factor desktop

*[[iPhone 18 Pro|iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max]] – high-end iPhones

Apple's tablet lineup:
*iPad – the name for Apple's entry-level iPads

*[[iPad Pro]] – pro iPad

=== Mergers and acquisitions ===
*[[List of mergers and acquisitions by Apple|Apple Inc. mergers and acquisitions]] &ndash; a list of company [[mergers and acquisitions]] by Apple (in alphabetical order):
**AlgoTrim &ndash; (bought August 2013), a Swedish [[data compression]] company, especially focused on still/video image compression, founded by Anders Berglund, Anders Holtsberg, and Martin Lindberg in 2005.
**[[Anobit]] &ndash; (bought December 2011), an Israeli [[fabless]] [[flash memory]] company, founded by Ehud Weinstein, [[Anobit#Background|Ariel Maislos]], and Ofir Shalvi in 2006.
**[[AuthenTec]] &ndash; (bought July 2012), security hardware and software for PCs and mobile device company, founded in 1998.
**[[Beats Electronics]] &ndash; (bought August 2014), music headphones and streaming service
**[[Chomp (search engine)|Chomp]] &ndash; (bought February 2012), an [[application software|app]] [[search engine (computing)|search engine]] company, founded by Ben Keighran and Cathy Edwards in 2009.
**[[Cue (search engine)|Cue]] &ndash; (bought October 2013), a personal assistant [[application software|app]] company, founded by Daniel Gross and Robby Walker in 2010.
**[[Emagic]] &ndash; (bought July 2002), music software and hardware company, best known for its [[music sequencer]], [[Logic Pro|Logic]].
**Embark &ndash; (bought August 2013), a startup company focused on developing transit information apps for user public transportation navigation in major US cities, founded by John Hering, David Hodge, Taylor Malloy, and Ian Leighton in 2011.
**[[FingerWorks]] &ndash; (bought early 2005), a gesture recognition company, founded by John Elias and Wayne Westerman in 1998.
**[[HopStop.com|HopStop]] &ndash; (bought July 2013), an online [[public transport|transit]] guide with [[rapid transit|subway]], bus directions, and maps, founded by Chinedu Echeruo in 2005.
**[[Intrinsity]] &ndash; (bought April 2010), [[fabless semiconductor company]], founded as EVSX in 1997 on the remnants of [[Exponential Technology]], then renamed Intrinsity in 2000.
**[[Lala (website)|Lala]] &ndash; (bought December 2009), online music store company, founded by [[Bill Nguyen]].
**Locationary &ndash; (bought July 2013), a Canadian crowdsourced location data management company, founded by Grant Ritchie in 2009.
**Matcha &ndash; (bought August 2013), a [[second screen]] [[television|TV]]/video startup, previously available as a media discovery iOS app (closed in May 2013), founded by Guy Piekarz, Ilan Ben Zeev, and Paul Petrick in September 2010.
**[[NeXT]] &ndash; (bought December 1996), computer company, founded in 1985 by Apple Inc. co-founder Steve Jobs after he was fired from Apple the same year. Current macOS, iOS, watchOS, and tvOS operating systems are largely built on its [[application programming interface|programming environment]] standard, [[OpenStep]]. Early versions of [[Mac OS X Server]] (codename Rhapsody) were OPENSTEP with a Mac-look and feel.
**[[Nothing Real]] &ndash; (bought February 2002), a high-end digital effects software development company for the feature film, broadcast and interactive gaming industries, founded by Allen Edwards and Arnaud Hervas in October 1996.
**[[P.A. Semi]] &ndash; (bought April 2008), a fabless semiconductor company founded by [[Daniel W. Dobberpuhl]] in 2003.
**Particle &ndash; (bought September 2012), a [[HTML5]] [[web app]] company, founded by Ericson de Jesus, Cole Rise, and Aubrey Anderson in 2008.
**Passif Semiconductor &ndash; (bought August 2013), an [[Oakland, California]] based [[semiconductor]] company specializing in low energy wireless chips, founded by Ben Cook and Axel Berny in 2007.
**[[PrimeSense]] &ndash; (bought November 2013), an [[Israel]]i [[fabless manufacturing|fabless semiconductor]] company specializing in 3D sensing, founded by Aviad Maizels, Alexander Shpunt, Ophir Sharon, Tamir Berliner and Dima Rais in 2005.
**Redmatica &ndash; (bought June 2012), an Italian music editing software company, known for Keymap Pro sampler software, founded by Andrea Gozzi in 2004.
**[[Silicon Color]] &ndash; (bought October 2006), "FinalTouch" color correction software and [[non-linear editing system|non-linear]] [[video editing software]] development company, now known as Apple's [[Final Cut Pro]] software.
**[[Siri (software)|Siri]] &ndash; (bought April 2010), an [[intelligent personal assistant]] and [[knowledge navigator]] software company, founded by Dag Kittlaus, [[Adam Cheyer]], [[Tom Gruber]], together with [[Norman Winarsky]] in 2007. Apple initially integrated the software into iOS, the later to the [[watchOS]] and [[tvOS]] platforms.
**[[Spruce Technologies]] &ndash; (bought July 2001), a [[DVD authoring]] company, founded by Dr. Hiromu Soga in 1996.
**[[Topsy (analytics)|Topsy]] &ndash; (bought December 2013), a US [[data analysis|data analytics]] company, founded by [[Vipul Ved Prakash]], [[Rishab Aiyer Ghosh]], Gary Iwatani, and Justin Foutts in 2007.
**WiFiSlam &ndash; (bought March 2013), an indoor location services company, founded by former Stanford students Darin Tay, Joseph Huang, Jessica Tsoong and Dave Millman in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bizjournals.com/sanjose/news/2013/03/25/apple-buys-indoor-gps-company-wifislam.html|title=Apple pays $20M for indoor GPS company WiFiSLAM|author=Cromwell Schubarth|date=March 25, 2013|website=[[Silicon Valley Business Journal]]}}</ref>

==Media==
*[[List of Apple Inc. media events|Media events]] &ndash; special events where Apple Inc. announce the release of their products and services. Usually, this is done by Apple's current CEO often featuring other executives, previously most notably [[Steve Jobs]].
**[[Stevenote]] &ndash; keynote addresses, usually held at the beginning of media events, where former CEO Steve Jobs would announce the release of new Apple products. Noted for his idiosyncratic style of presenting, and also for his "[[Stevenote#.22One more thing....22|One More Thing...]]" surprise announcements at the end.
*[[Apple Inc. advertising|Advertising]] &ndash; various Apple Inc. advertising techniques and campaigns.
**[[1984 (advertisement)]] &ndash; specific TV and print ad campaign, inferring how Mac computers will free users from tyrannies similar to those prophesied in the [[George Orwell]] novel ''[[Nineteen Eighty-Four]]''. Launched the first [[Apple Macintosh|Macintosh]] computer; the [[Macintosh 128K]].
**[[Think different]] &ndash; specific TV & print ad campaign, inferring how Macs do things differently (meaning ''better'') to other computers used in the home and small to medium-sized businesses.
**[[Get a Mac]] &ndash; TV ad campaign, humorously inferring the superior nature of a Mac vs. Windows PC.
**[[iPod advertising]] &ndash; various iPod ad campaigns since its initial release in 2001.

==Apple-related==
*[[Apple community]] &ndash; the many various online websites and offline groups where Apple Inc.'s products and services are discussed and analyzed, as well as future products rumored about.
*[[Apple Campus]] &ndash; the [[Cupertino]], [[California]]-based set of buildings forming the basis of Apple Inc.'s main campus business headquarters, where most office staff are based. A new, mostly single building, called [[Apple Park|Apple Campus 2]], opened in 2017.
*[[Apple litigation]] &ndash; various legal disputes the company has been involved in.
*[[Criticism of Apple Inc.]] &ndash; various criticisms leveled at Apple Inc.
*[[Mac transition to Intel processors]] &ndash; the process of Apple changing the [[CPU]] of [[Apple Macintosh|Macintosh]] computers from [[PowerPC]] processors to [[Intel]] [[x86]] processors, during 2006.
**[[Apple–Intel architecture]] &ndash; the [[CPU design|architecture]] of Intel-based Apple computers, using [[Intel]] [[x86]] processors rather than the [[PowerPC]] and <!-- Pre-PowerPC -->[[68k]] processors used in their predecessors.
**[[Universal binary]] &ndash; in [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] parlance, an [[executable file]] or [[application bundle]] that runs natively on either [[PowerPC]] or [[Intel]]-manufactured [[IA-32]] or [[Intel 64]]-based [[Apple Macintosh|Macs]]; it is an implementation of the concept more generally known as a [[fat binary]].
***[[Xslimmer]] &ndash; [[macOS]] utility application developed by LateNiteSoft, designed to tweak [[Universal binary|universal binaries]] applications by stripping the binary from either its [[PowerPC]] or [[Intel Corporation|Intel]] code (depending on the system architecture used), in order to save hard disk space.
**[[Rosetta (software)|Rosetta]] &ndash; a [[Binary translation#Dynamic binary translation|dynamic binary translator]] application for [[Mac OS X]] allowing many [[PowerPC]] apps to run on certain [[x86|Intel]]-based [[Macintosh|Macs]] without modification. Released in 2006 for the transition from PowerPC to Intel processors on the Macintosh [[Computing platform|platform]], but it was dropped in [[Mac OS X Lion|Lion]] so Snow Leopard is the last version of Mac OS X that is able to run PowerPC-only applications.
**[[Mac 68k emulator]] &ndash; lower-level program, similar in purpose to [[Rosetta (software)|Rosetta]] but instead used during the transition from [[680x0]] to [[PowerPC]] processors.
*[[Macintosh clone]] &ndash; a personal computer made by a manufacturer other than Apple, using (or compatible with) Macintosh [[firmware]] and [[system software]].
**[[Star Trek project|Star Trek]] &ndash; code name of [[prototype]] project between Apple and [[Novell]] from February/March 1992 to 1993, which was to be a version of the [[classic Mac OS]] running as a [[GUI]] on [[Intel]]-compatible [[x86]] [[personal computer|PC]]s on top of Novell's next in-development version of [[operating system|OS]], [[DR DOS]].
**OSx86/[[Hackintosh]] &ndash; (from ''OS X'' and ''x86'') is a collaborative [[Hacker (hobbyist)|hacking]] project to run OS X on non-Apple [[personal computers|PCs]] with [[x86 architecture]] and [[x86-64]] compatible processors. Computers built to run this type of {{nowrap|OS X}} are often known as a ''Hackintosh'' or ''Hackbook'' (respectively, [[portmanteau]]s of words "hack" with "Macintosh" or "notebook computers").
* After finishing college, Apple's [[Senior Vice President|SVP]] of [[Industrial Design]] and Human Interface, [[Jony Ive]], co-founded a [[London]] design agency, [[Jony Ive#Tangerine|Tangerine]].<ref name="Mahalo Ive tangerine">{{cite web|title=Jonathan Ive|url=http://www.mahalo.com/jonathan-ive|publisher=[[Mahalo.com]]|access-date=January 14, 2013}}</ref> After leaving Apple, he and colleague [[Marc Newson]] started new agency, [[LoveFrom]].<ref name="LF 1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/jony-ive-is-departing-apple-but-he-started-leaving-years-ago-11561943376|title=Jony Ive Is Leaving Apple, but His Departure Started Long Ago|first=Tripp|last=Mickle|newspaper=Wall Street Journal|date=July 2019}}</ref><ref name="LF 2">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/story/jony-ive-leaves-apple/|title=Jony Ive Is Leaving Apple|magazine=Wired|via=www.wired.com|last1=Matsakis|first1=Louise}}</ref>

'''Roboto''' ({{IPAc-en|r|oʊ|'|b|Q|t|.|oʊ}})<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6WxACOHm0_g |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/6WxACOHm0_g |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|title=Making Material Design: Refining Roboto|date=28 May 2015 |access-date=July 22, 2019|publisher=Google Design}}{{cbignore}}</ref> is a [[typeface family]] developed by [[Google]]. The first typeface was created as the system font for its [[Android (operating system)|Android]] operating system, and released in 2011 for [[Android Ice Cream Sandwich]].<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.wired.com/2011/10/android-ice-cream-sandwich-3 |title=Google Unwraps Ice Cream Sandwich, the Next-Generation Android OS |last=Isaac |first=Mike |date=October 19, 2011 |magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]] |access-date=November 18, 2017}}</ref>

The entire font family has been licensed under the [[Apache license]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fontsquirrel.com/license/roboto |title=License for font family 'Roboto' |website=Font Squirrel |access-date=November 18, 2017}}</ref> In 2014, Roboto was redesigned for [[Android Lollipop|Android 5.0 "Lollipop"]]. Most variants of Roboto have been licensed or re-licensed under the [[SIL Open Font License|OFL]]: Roboto (the default [[Sans-serif|sans serif]] font),<ref>{{Cite web | title=Roboto - Google Fonts | url=https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Roboto/license | access-date=2025-07-26 | website=fonts.google.com}}</ref> Roboto Condensed,<ref>{{Cite web | title=Roboto Condensed - Google Fonts | url=https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Roboto+Condensed/license | access-date=2025-07-26 | website=fonts.google.com}}</ref> Roboto Flex,<ref>{{Cite web | title=Roboto Flex - Google Fonts | url=https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Roboto+Flex/license | access-date=2025-07-26 | website=fonts.google.com}}</ref> Roboto Mono,<ref>{{Cite web | title=Roboto Mono - Google Fonts | url=https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Roboto+Mono/license | access-date=2025-07-26 | website=fonts.google.com}}</ref> and Roboto Serif.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Roboto Serif - Google Fonts | url=https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Roboto+Serif/license | access-date=2025-07-26 | website=fonts.google.com}}</ref>

==Usage==
Roboto is one of the most popular typeface families on the Internet<ref>{{cite web |url=https://fonts.google.com/analytics |title=Analytics - Google Fonts | access-date=2025-12-30}}</ref> and has been used on Google services such as [[Google Play]], [[YouTube]], [[Google Maps]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.alphr.com/blogs/2013/05/17/hands-on-with-the-new-google-maps |title=Hands on with the new Google Maps |last=Graham-Smith |first=Darien |date=May 17, 2013 |website=[[Alphr]] |access-date=November 18, 2017}}</ref> and [[Google Images]] since 2013. It is the default system font on [[Android (operating system)|Android]], while Roboto Bold is the default font in [[Unreal Engine 4]], and in [[Kodi (software)|Kodi]]'s then default skin, Confluence, until 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://kodi.tv/article/xbmc-110-may-cycle-updated |title=XBMC 11.0 – May Cycle (updated) |last=Betzen |first=Nathan |date=June 5, 2012 |website=[[Kodi (software)|Kodi]] |access-date=November 18, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Aufranc |first=Jean-Luc |date=2016-03-09 |title=Meet Estuary and Estouchy, The New Default Skins for Kodi 17 and Beyond - CNX Software |url=https://www.cnx-software.com/2016/03/09/meet-estuary-and-estouchy-the-new-default-skins-for-kodi-17-and-beyond/ |access-date=2026-07-24 |website=CNX Software - Embedded Systems News |language=en-US |quote=I've only known XBMC / Kodi since the open source media center started to show up on ARM based Android and Linux mini PCs around the mid of 2012, and in most devices the default skin called Confluence was used with Kodi/XBMC. It has been used as the default since 2009, and Kodi developers have decided a refresh would be good for Kodi 17 Krypton which will feature two new skins: Estuary for media players and HTPCs, and Estouchy for devices with a touchscreen such as smartphones and tablets.}}</ref> Roboto was also the basis of another popular typeface [[Inter (typeface)|Inter]], although later versions of Inter were developed independent of Roboto.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.figma.com/blog/the-birth-of-inter/ |title=The birth of Inter: How the new open-source typeface used by GitHub and Mozilla came to be | access-date=2025-12-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://fontsinuse.com/typefaces/93554/inter |title=Inter in use - Fonts In Use | access-date=2025-12-30}}</ref>

Roboto was used on the [[Technology of the New York City Subway#Mainline B Division and Flushing Line clocks|LCD countdown clocks]] of the [[New York City Subway]]'s [[B Division (New York City Subway)|B Division]] lines in 2017. Roboto Condensed is used to display Information on European versions of [[Nintendo Switch]] packaging, including physical releases of games.

[[Utsav Plus|Utsav Network]] uses Roboto for its wordmark.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bizasialive.com/exclusive-first-look-at-the-new-utsav-branding/ |title=Exclusive: First look at Star TV's new Utsav TV branding |last=Baddhan |first=Lakh |date=January 11, 2021 |website=BizAsia |access-date= June 4, 2021}}</ref> The Indonesian news TV channel [[iNews]] also uses a slightly modified Roboto on its logo. Since October 2022, [[Global News]] has also used Roboto in its on-air presentation, however the font is not used in main network presentation. In addition, the [[United Nations]] uses Roboto on its website and in official documents.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.un.org/styleguide/ |website=UN web style guide |publisher=United Nations |title=UN Web Style Guide }}</ref>

== History ==
Android's previous system typeface, [[Droid (typeface)|Droid Sans]], was designed for the low-resolution displays of the very early Android devices, and did not display well in larger, higher-resolution screens of later models.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://nymag.com/intelligencer/2014/07/google-is-designing-the-font-of-the-future.html |title=Google Is Designing the Font of the Future. Here's How |last=Roose |first=Kevin |date=July 16, 2014 |website=New York Magazine |access-date=March 8, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://blog.gsmarena.com/googles-matias-duarte-talks-about-thew-new-roboto-font-in-ice-cream-sandwich |title=Google's Matias Duarte talks about the new Roboto font in Ice Cream Sandwich|date=11 November 2011 }}</ref> It was decided that a more modern typeface, designed from scratch, was needed for the newer displays.

=== Early development (2011) ===
[[File:Roboto (typeface).svg|200px|right|thumb|Sample text of Roboto in 2013 in various font weights and sizes, prior to the redesign for Android 5. Unlike now, the leg of the R has a curl, the same as in Helvetica.]]
The new typeface, Roboto, was designed entirely in-house by Christian Robertson who previously had released an expanded [[Ubuntu Titling]] font through his personal type foundry Betatype.<ref name="Frankenfont">{{cite web |url=http://typographica.org/on-typography/roboto-typeface-is-a-four-headed-frankenstein |title=Roboto Was a Four-headed Frankenfont |last=Coles |first=Stephen |date=October 19, 2011 |website=Typographica |access-date=November 18, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.christianrobertson.com |title=Christian Robertson. Interface, type designer. |access-date=November 18, 2017}}</ref> The font was officially made available for free download on 12 January 2012, on the newly launched Android Design website.

Compared to the humanist sans-serif Droid Sans, Roboto belongs to the [[Sans-serif#Classification|neo-grotesque]] genre of sans-serif typefaces. It includes Thin, Light, Regular, Medium, Bold and Black [[Font#Weight|weights]] with matching [[oblique type|oblique]] styles rather than true italics. It also includes [[Font#Width|condensed]] styles in Light, Regular and Bold, also with matching [[oblique type|oblique]] designs.

=== "Material Design" redesign (2014) ===
On 25 June 2014, [[Matias Duarte]] announced at [[Google I/O]] that Roboto was significantly redesigned for [[Android Lollipop|Android 5.0 "Lollipop"]].<ref name="Frankenfont" /><ref name="Kellen Android L">{{cite web |title=Download: New Roboto for Android L and Material Design |url=https://www.droid-life.com/2014/06/25/download-new-roboto-for-android-l-and-material-design/ |website=Droid Life |date=25 June 2014 |access-date=30 May 2019}}</ref> Punctuation marks and the [[tittles]] in the lowercase "i" and "j" were changed from square to rounded, the leg part of the uppercase "R" were changed from curved to straight, the bottom surface of the top part of the number "1" points downwards instead of horizontal, the tail part of the numbers "6" and "9" have been slightly shortened (in resemblance to "[[Trebuchet MS]]"), the stem part of the number "7" becomes curved to straight, and the entire typeface was made "slightly wider and rounder" with many changes in details.<ref name="Frankenfont" /><ref name="Kellen Android L"/> The newly-redesigned version of Roboto is also offered in a wider range of [[font weight]]s, adding Thin (100), Medium (500), and Black (900) alongside Light (300), Regular (400), and Bold (700).

== Language support ==
Roboto supports [[Latin script|Latin]], [[Greek script|Greek]] and [[Cyrillic script|Cyrillic]] scripts.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Roboto |title=Roboto |last=Robertson |first=Christian |date=2015 |website=[[Google Fonts]] |access-date=November 18, 2017}}</ref>

On Android, the [[Noto fonts]] are used for languages not supported by Roboto, including [[Chinese script|Chinese]] (simplified and traditional), [[Japanese script|Japanese]], [[Korean script|Korean]], [[Thai script|Thai]] and [[Hindi script|Hindi]] (as of June 2026)

Roboto Mono is a [[monospace]] font based on Roboto. It is available in seven weights: thin, extra-light, light, regular, medium, semi-bold and bold, with oblique stylings for each weight.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Roboto+Mono |title=Roboto Mono |last=Robertson |first=Christian |website=[[Google Fonts]] |access-date=November 18, 2017}}</ref>
{{clear}}

=== Roboto Serif ===
Roboto Serif is a companion typeface with serifs designed by Greg Gazdowicz of [[Commercial Type]]. It was debuted in 2022 to fill the serif niche.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/google-introduces-reading-optimized-roboto-serif-typeface|title=Google Introduces Reading-Optimized Roboto Serif Typeface|date=2022-02-19|access-date=2022-02-24}}</ref> It is a readable retro-styled typeface whose letters have been redrawn from scratch, with the same vertical height as Roboto.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2022/2/18/22940753/google-roboto-serif-font-typeface-design-easier-reading-retro|title=Google's new retro-style font brings back serifs for more comfortable reading|last1=Gartenberg|first1=Chaim |date=18 February 2022 }}</ref> Roboto Serif has both a regular and a true italic form.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Roboto Serif - Google Fonts | url=https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Roboto+Serif | access-date=2025-07-26 | website=fonts.google.com}}</ref> Roboto Serif is a variable font with four axes: Weight, width, optical size, and a "grade" axis which can make the font thinner or thicker without affecting its metrics.<ref>{{Cite web | title=GitHub - googlefonts/roboto-serif | url=https://github.com/googlefonts/roboto-serif | access-date=2025-07-26 | website=github.com}}</ref>

=== Roboto Slab ===
{{Infobox typeface
| name = Roboto Slab

| style = [[Serif]]

}}
Roboto Slab is a [[slab serif]] font based on Roboto. It was introduced in March 2013, as the default font in Google's note-taking service [[Google Keep]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.androidpolice.com/2013/03/27/closer-look-google-keep-actually-shipped-with-a-new-serif-font-introducing-roboto-slab-download |title=Closer Look: Google Keep Actually Shipped With A New (Serif) Font – Introducing Roboto Slab |last=Spradlin |first=Liam |date=March 27, 2013 |website=Android Police |access-date=November 18, 2017}}</ref> (The font was changed to the sans-serif Roboto in 2018.)<ref>{{Cite web|last=Staff|date=2018-10-18|title=Google Keep Notes gets Material Design, brings sans-serif Roboto font and solid white background|url=https://www.bgr.in/news/google-keep-notes-material-design-october-2018-sans-serif-roboto-font-solid-white-background/|access-date=2019-07-04|website=BGR India|language=en-US|archive-date=2019-07-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190704051258/https://www.bgr.in/news/google-keep-notes-material-design-october-2018-sans-serif-roboto-font-solid-white-background/|url-status=dead}}</ref> It is available in four weights: thin, light, regular and bold. However, no oblique versions were released for it.

In November 2019, the typeface was updated, adding five new weights (Extra-Light, Medium, Semi-Bold, Extra-Bold and Black) and a variable font axis ranging from 100 to 900, along with modifications to certain characters, matching the updated (2014) version of the sans-serif Roboto.
{{clear}}

=== Variable Fonts ===
As of 2026, Roboto has two [[variable font]] versions, namely Roboto VF and Roboto Flex.

==== Roboto VF ====
Roboto VF is intended to be a 1:1 match with the static version of Roboto and has three adjustable axes.<ref name="Roboto VF">{{cite web |url=https://github.com/googlefonts/roboto-3-classic |title=Roboto VF |access-date=2025-12-30}}</ref>

==== Roboto Flex ====
Roboto Flex has 12 adjustable axes, including [[optical size]].<ref name="Roboto Flex - Google Fonts">{{cite web |url=https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Roboto+Flex |title=Roboto Flex - Google Fonts |access-date=2023-07-31}}</ref> However, unlike Roboto VF, Roboto Flex is not designed to perfectly match with the static version of Roboto. Roboto Flex supports Latin, Greek, and Cyrillic characters.

=== Heebo ===
Heebo is an extension of Roboto that includes [[Hebrew alphabet|Hebrew characters]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://github.com/meirsadan/heebo |title=Heebo open source Hebrew font |website=[[GitHub]] |access-date=November 18, 2017}}</ref>

=== Piboto ===
Piboto is a fork of Roboto, based on the original version of Roboto before the 2014 redesign.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://pi3g.com/interview-with-simon-long-of-raspberry-pi-about-the-raspberry-pi-desktop-ui-design-and-much-more/ |title=Interview with Simon Long of Raspberry Pi about the Raspberry Pi Desktop, UI design, and much more! | website=pi3g.com |date=4 January 2019 |access-date=June 6, 2023}}</ref> Adopted by Simon Long (UX engineer at Raspberry Pi), Piboto was used as the system font on [[Raspberry Pi OS]] until October 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.opensourcefeed.org/raspberry-pi-os-trixie-release/ |title=Raspberry Pi OS Trixie Released with New Theme, Control Centre, and Modular Packaging | access-date=2025-12-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bacloud.com/en/blog/212/raspberry-pi-os-trixie--a-new-era-based-on-debian-13.html |title=Raspberry Pi OS "Trixie" – A New Era Based on Debian 13  | access-date=2025-12-30}}</ref>

[[File:Raspberry_Pi_OS_10_on_small_screen_(screenshot).png|220x124px|thumb|right|Previous version of Raspberry Pi OS featuring Piboto as the system font]]

Piboto is released under a mix of the [[SIL Open Font License]] and the [[Apache License]]. The type family has been archived and is publicly available.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://archive.raspberrypi.org/debian/pool/main/f/fonts-piboto/ |title=fonts-piboto | access-date=2025-12-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://github.com/thunderbird-1990/fonts-piboto |title=Piboto | website=[[GitHub]] | access-date=2025-12-30}}</ref>

== Reception ==
Google developed Roboto to be "modern, yet approachable" and "emotional",<ref name="ICE">{{cite web |url=https://www.engadget.com/2011/10/18/roboto-and-the-new-design-philosophy-of-android-4-0-ice-cream-s |title=Roboto font and the new design philosophy of Android 4.0, Ice Cream Sandwich |last=O'Brien |first=Terrence |date=October 18, 2011 |website=[[Engadget]] |access-date=November 17, 2017}}</ref><ref name="Cream">{{cite web |url=https://news.in.msn.com/technology/article.aspx?cp-documentid=5526341 |title=Android Ice Cream Sandwich: Top 10 features that make it delicious |date=October 19, 2011 |website=[[MSN]] |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121209084519/http://news.in.msn.com/technology/article.aspx?cp-documentid=5526341 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 9, 2012 }}</ref> but the initial release (i.e., before the Android 5.0 redesign) received mixed reviews.

[[Joshua Topolsky]], Editor-In-Chief of technology news and media network ''[[The Verge (website)|The Verge]]'', describes the typeface as "clean and modern, but not overly futuristic – not a science fiction font".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theverge.com/2011/10/18/exclusive-matias-duarte-ice-cream-sandwich-galaxy-nexus |title=Exclusive: Matias Duarte on the philosophy of Android, and an in-depth look at Ice Cream Sandwich |last=Topolsky |first=Joshua |author-link=Joshua Topolsky |date=October 18, 2011 |website=[[The Verge]] |access-date=November 18, 2017}}</ref>

The 2014 redesign for Android 5.0 Lollipop was largely seen as an improvement, with reviewers noting the font was made "rounder and wider," giving it a more pleasant look, and improving clarity on a spectrum of devices from smartphones to large-format displays.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-11-14 |title=Android 5.0 Lollipop review: Google's biggest mobile update in years |url=https://www.engadget.com/2014-11-14-android-lollipop-review.html |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=Engadget |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Kuang |first=Cliff |title=How Google's New Font Tries to Anticipate the Future |url=https://www.wired.com/2014/07/how-googles-new-font-tries-to-anticipate-the-future/ |access-date=2025-07-28 |magazine=Wired |language=en-US |issn=1059-1028}}</ref>

Industry reaction to Roboto's evolution was generally positive, especially regarding its utility in UI and UX contexts. The typeface was widely adopted even outside of the Android ecosystem, serving as a default or recommended font in numerous Google services and third-party applications, and becoming a go-to choice for web designers seeking a modern, legible, and versatile sans-serif font. Quantitative studies have confirmed this ubiquity: by 2024, Roboto—together with [[Open Sans]]—was found to account for 51% of all Google Font views,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Choi |first1=Jiin |last2=Hyun |first2=Kyung Hoon |date=2024-12-28 |title=Typeface network and the principle of font pairing |journal=Scientific Reports |language=en |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=30820 |doi=10.1038/s41598-024-81601-w  |doi-access=free|pmid=39730572 |bibcode=2024NatSR..1430820C |issn=2045-2322|pmc=11681221 }}</ref> while other analytics reported more than 200 billion views and extensive use on tens of millions of websites.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pearce |first=Scott |date=2024-09-24 |title=Google Fonts Trends: A Data-Driven Approach to Font Selection |url=https://datumcp.com/google-fonts-trends-a-data-driven-approach-to-font-selection/ |access-date=2025-07-28 |website=Datum Creative Media |language=en}}</ref>

In user and laboratory-based analyses, Roboto has demonstrated good on-screen legibility, typically ranking highly among sans-serif fonts. Studies have shown that Roboto performs comparably to other major screen fonts like Arial and Open Sans in terms of user preference and readability metrics, with slight differences in specific areas such as reading speed and comprehension.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Vecino |first1=Sara |last2=Mehtali |first2=Jonas |last3=de Andrés |first3=Javier |last4=Gonzalez-Rodriguez |first4=Martin |last5=Fernandez-Lanvin |first5=Daniel |date=2022 |title=How does serif vs sans serif typeface impact the usability of e-commerce websites? |journal=PeerJ Computer Science |volume=8 |article-number=e1139 |doi=10.7717/peerj-cs.1139 |doi-access=free |issn=2376-5992 |pmc=9680897 |pmid=36426257}}</ref>
