===2001===
Loki published ''[[Heavy Metal: F.A.K.K. 2|Heavy Metal: F.A.K.K.²]], [[Kohan: Immortal Sovereigns]], [[Mindrover: The Europa Project]], [[Myth II: Soulblighter]], Postal Plus, [[Rune (video game)|Rune]], [[Rune (video game)|Rune: Halls of Valhalla]], [[Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri]]'', and [[Tribes 2]] for Linux.<ref name=":04"/>

Linux Game Publishing was founded in 2001 in response to the impending demise of Loki. Creature Labs ported ''[[Creatures (artificial life program)#Creatures Internet Edition / Creatures Gold|Creatures: Internet Edition]]'' to Linux, which was published by LGP.

Hyperion Entertainment ported ''Shogo: Mobile Armor Division'' to Linux, and Tribsoft created a Linux version of ''Jagged Alliance 2'', both published by Titan Computer.

[[Illwinter Game Design]] released ''Conquest of Elysium II'' and ''Dominions: Priests, Prophets & Pretenders'' for Linux. [[Introversion Software]] released ''[[Uplink]]'' for Linux.

BlackHoleSun Software released ''Bunnies'', and worked on ''Atlantis: The Underwater City – Interactive Storybook'' published by Sterling Entertainment.<ref name="Wilson"/>

GLAMUS GmbH released a Linux version of their game ''[[Mobility (computer game)|Mobility]]'' and Oliver Hamann released the driving game ''Odyssey by Car''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=Hamish |date=4 June 2023 |title=Building a Retro Linux Gaming Computer Part 29: The Odyssey |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2023/07/building-a-retro-linux-gaming-computer-part-29-the-odyssey/ |website=GamingOnLinux |access-date=29 January 2024}}</ref>

Small Rockets published ''Small Rockets BackGammon, Small Rockets Mah Jongg'', and ''Small Rockets Poker'' for Linux.{{citation needed|date=December 2024}}

The company [[Findev|TransGaming]] marketed as a monthly subscription its own proprietary fork of [[Wine (software)|Wine]] called WineX in October 2001, later renamed [[Cedega (software)|Cedega]] in 2004 and discontinued in 2011, which aimed for greater compatibility with [[Microsoft Windows]] games.
A special Gaming Edition of [[Mandrake Linux]] 8.1 was released that featured WineX packed in with ''[[The Sims (video game)|The Sims]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.linux.com/news/review-mandrake-81-gaming-edition-opens-linux-more-games-more-users/|title=Review: Mandrake 8.1 Gaming Edition opens Linux to more games, more users|first=F. Grant|last=Robertson|website=[[Linux.com]]|date=12 December 2001|access-date=30 June 2023}}</ref> The fact that the fork of Wine did not release source back to the main project was also a point of contention, despite promises to release code after achieving a set number of subscribers.<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20011225200125/http://www.newsforge.com/article.pl?sid=01/10/22/0051250|url=http://www.newsforge.com/article.pl?sid=01/10/22/0051250|title=TransGaming, Mandrake team up to bring PC games directly to Linux|website=NewsForge|date=22 October 2001|access-date=30 May 2023|archive-date=25 December 2001|first=Grant|last=Gross}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.linux.com/news/finally-its-time-wine/|title=Finally, it's time for Wine|date=12 June 2008|access-date=27 May 2024|first=Steven J.|last=Vaughan-Nichols|website=[[Linux.com]]|quote=According to White in a 2006 NewsForge interview, this forking caused Wine’s development to slow down for years. “Historically, the main interest for volunteer Wine developers was games; that was the main focus for most of Wine’s early years (~1993–2000). When Transgaming started in 2001, they promised that they would release their DirectX improvements back to Wine. That cast a chill over games in Wine — why work on DirectX if all these improvements would ‘soon’ be coming back? Of course, no meaningful improvements have ever come back, which had the effect of creating a huge hole in what had been Wine’s very best facility.” By 2007, White says, “The Wine community had recovered from the hole created by Transgaming.”}}</ref>

The release of [[ScummVM]] in 2001,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2012/01/maniac-tentacle-mindbenders-of-atlantis-how-scummvm-kept-adventure-gaming-alive/ |title=Maniac Tentacle Mindbenders: How ScummVM's unpaid coders kept adventure gaming alive |work=[[Ars Technica]] |date=16 January 2012 |access-date=16 February 2016 |first=Richard |last=Moss}}</ref> [[Dosbox]] in 2002,<ref>{{cite web|first=Liam |last=Dawe| date=15 July 2019 |title=DOSBox-X and DOSBox Staging both had new releases lately|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2021/07/dosbox-x-and-dosbox-staging-both-had-new-releases-lately/ |website=GamingOnLinux |access-date=5 February 2023}}</ref> and [[video game console emulator]]s like [[MAME]] from 1997 and released as open source in 2016, helped make Linux a viable platform for [[retro gaming]] (facilitated by the [[RetroArch]] frontend since 2010).<ref>{{cite news|first=Derrik|last=Diener| date=5 February 2018| title=How To Play Arcade Games Using MAME On Linux|newspaper=Addictivetips |url=https://www.addictivetips.com/ubuntu-linux-tips/play-arcade-games-on-linux-using-mame/ |access-date=5 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Liam |last=Dawe| date=15 July 2019 |title=RetroArch, the front-end app for emulators and more is heading to Steam|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2019/07/retroarch-the-front-end-app-for-emulators-and-more-is-heading-to-steam/ |website=GamingOnLinux |access-date=5 February 2023}}</ref> This is especially the case for the [[GP2X]] series of [[handheld game console]]s by [[GamePark Holdings]] in addition to the community driven [[Pandora (computer)|Pandora]] and [[DragonBox Pyra]]. Dedicated [[emulation (computing)|emulation]] setups are also built on [[single-board computers]] like the [[Raspberry Pi]] released in 2012, which are most often [[Linux]] based including with [[Raspberry Pi OS]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Liam |last=Dawe| date=30 April 2020 |title=If you have the retro gaming itch RetroPie 4.6 is out with support for the Raspberry Pi 4|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2019/07/retroarch-the-front-end-app-for-emulators-and-more-is-heading-to-steam/ |website=GamingOnLinux |access-date=5 February 2023}}</ref> [[Wine (software)|Wine]] is also useful for running older Windows games,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.makeuseof.com/tag/play-retro-windows-games-linux/|title=How to Play Retro Windows Games on Linux|first=Moe|last=Long|website=MakeUseOf|date=23 September 2016|access-date=16 February 2023}}</ref> including [[16-bit]] and even some [[32-bit]] applications that no longer work on modern [[64-bit]] Windows.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://vulcanhammer.info/2020/05/11/is-the-best-place-to-run-old-windows-software-on-linux-or-a-mac/|title=Is the Best Place to Run Old Windows Software... on Linux or a Mac?|website=Vulcan Hammer|first=Don|last=Warrington|date=11 May 2020|access-date=16 February 2023}}</ref> The [[Sharp Zaurus]] [[personal data assistant]]s adopted a Linux derived system called [[OpenZaurus]], which attracted its own gaming scene.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.linuxjournal.com/article/5902|website=[[Linux Journal]]|title=Applications for the Sharp Zaurus|first=Guylhem|last=Aznar|date=2 July 2002|access-date=28 October 2023|quote=''An excellent way to start using the Zaurus is by playing games. The best way to play games on the Zaurus is to install an emulator.''}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.newbreedsoftware.com/zaurus/|website=New Breed Software|first=Bill|last=Kendrick|title=Zaurus Software|access-date=28 October 2023}}</ref> This was also the case with the [[Agenda VR3]], advertised as the first "pure Linux PDA".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linuxdevices.com/articles/AT4992223978.html |title="Agenda's agenda – a Linux-based "Open PDA"" |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080513071354/http://www.linuxdevices.com/articles/AT4992223978.html |archivedate=13 May 2008}}, LinuxDevices.com, retrieved 17 July 2008</ref><ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061017141822/http://www.agendawiki.com/cgi-bin/asr.pl?action=showcat&category=Games|url=http://agendawiki.com:80/cgi-bin/asr.pl?action=showcat&category=Games|archive-date=17 October 2006|access-date=8 December 2023|title=Games|website=Agenda Wiki}}</ref>

===2002===
[[File:Ryan-Gordon-SELF-2009.png|thumb|left|200px|Former Loki Software employee Ryan C. Gordon]]

After Loki's closure, the Linux game market experienced some changes.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kepley |first=Travis |date=13 May 2010|title=A brief history of commercial gaming on Linux (and how it's all about to change) |url=https://opensource.com/life/10/5/brief-history-commercial-gaming-linux |website=[[Opensource.com]] |access-date=5 February 2023}}</ref> Although some new firms, such as [[Linux Game Publishing]] and RuneSoft, would largely continue the role of a standard porting house,<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030602025952/http://www.linuxhardware.org/article.pl?sid=03/04/18/169209|url=http://www.linuxhardware.org/article.pl?sid=03/04/18/169209|title=
Gaming and Linux in 2003|first=Dana|last=Olson|website=LinuxHardware.org|date=18 April 2003|archive-date=2 June 2003|access-date=1 July 2023}}</ref> the focus began to change with Linux game proponents encouraging game developers to port their game products themselves or through individual contractors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.phoronix.com/scan.php?page=news_item&px=ODkwOA|title=Alternative Games Is All About Linux Gaming|publisher=[[Phoronix]]|date=14 December 2010|last=Larabel|first=Michael|author-link=Michael Larabel}}</ref> Influential to this was [[Ryan C. Gordon]], a former Loki employee who would over the next decade port several game titles to multiple platforms, including Linux.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hardware.no/artikler/ryan_c_gordon_and_michael_simms/68450/2|title=Porting games to Linux|publisher=hardware.no|date=10 March 2009|last=Heggelund Hansen|first=Robin|access-date=16 March 2011|archive-date=22 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140322083056/http://www.hardware.no/artikler/ryan_c_gordon_and_michael_simms/68450/2|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Ryan ported America's Army, Candy Cruncher, Serious Sam: The First Encounter, and Unreal Tournament 2003 to Linux.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://linux.sys-con.com/node/32796 |title=A mixed welcome for Unreal Tournament 2003 on Linux – LinuxWorld |access-date=7 December 2009 |archive-date=29 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120229163905/http://linux.sys-con.com/node/32796 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bluesnews.com/s/61558|title=Mac, Linux America's Army - Blue's News Story|website=www.bluesnews.com}}</ref><ref name="bluesnews.com">{{Cite web|url=https://www.bluesnews.com/s/29251|title=Serious Sam 2nd Encounter Q&A & Linux News - Blue's News Story|website=www.bluesnews.com}}</ref>

Linux Game Publishing had initially tried to pick up the support rights to many of Loki's titles, but in the end it was only able to acquire the rights to MindRover: The Europa Project. They released the updated version of Mindrover and its downloadable update for owners of the old Loki version.<ref>[http://blog.linuxgamepublishing.com/2009/05/15/lgp-history-pt-1-how-lgp-came-to-be/ LGP History pt 1: How LGP came to be] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713212344/http://blog.linuxgamepublishing.com/2009/05/15/lgp-history-pt-1-how-lgp-came-to-be/ |date=13 July 2011}} Linux Game Publishing Blog, 15 May 2009 (Article by Michael Simms)</ref>

Return to Castle Wolfenstein was released for [[Linux]] and with the Linux port done in-house by [[Timothee Besset]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bluesnews.com/s/30526 |title=On Wolf's Goldness |access-date=25 March 2017 |author=Furness, James |date=15 November 2001 |publisher=Blue's News |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170326054637/https://www.bluesnews.com/s/30526 |archive-date=26 March 2017}}</ref>

[[Chronic logic]] released Bridge Construction Set and Triptych for Linux.

Sunspire Studios released in retail commercial expansion of the game titled ''[[Tux Racer]]''.<ref name=tuxracer.com>{{cite web|url=http://tuxracer.com/|title=Tux Racer website|publisher=Sunspire Studios|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040904142508/http://tuxracer.com/|archive-date=4 September 2004}}</ref>

===2003===
Ryan ported ''Devastation, Medal of Honor Allied Assault'', and ''Serious Sam: The Second Encounter'' to
Linux.<ref name="bluesnews.com"/>

LGP took interest in publishing Pyrogon games on physical CDs and they released Candy Cruncher.<ref>[http://www.linuxgames.com/archives/5902 Linux Game Publishing and Pyrogon Announcement] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004225902/http://www.linuxgames.com/archives/5902 |date=4 October 2013}} [[LinuxGames]], 10 September 2002</ref> Mathieu Pinard from Tribsoft got LGP in contact with Cyberlore to save the Linux port of Majesty because Titan Computer get out of Linux publishing. This turn of events helped LGP to release a Majesty for Linux after Pinard closed his company in 2002.<ref>[http://www.linuxgames.com/archives/5282 Majesty, Tribsoft, and LGP] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110614052930/http://www.linuxgames.com/archives/5282 |date=14 June 2011}} [[LinuxGames]], 3 January 2002</ref> 
 
Timothee Bessett from id Software ported Wolfenstein: Enemy Territory to Linux.<ref name="phoronix.com">[https://www.phoronix.com/news/MTA0OTE id Software's Main Linux Game Developer Resigns] [[Phoronix]], 27 January 2012</ref>

Around this time many companies, [[John Carmack#Open-source software|starting with]] id Software, also began to release legacy [[source code]] leading to a proliferation of [[source port]]s of older games to Linux and other systems.<ref name="Crider">{{cite web|url=https://www.howtogeek.com/335259/the-best-modern-open-source-ports-of-classic-games/|title=The Best Modern, Open Source Ports of Classic Games|website=How-To Geek|first=Michael|last=Crider|date=24 December 2017|access-date=20 March 2023}}</ref> This also [[Open-source video game#3D games and source releases|helped expand]] the already existing free and open-source gaming scene, especially with regards to the creation of free [[first person shooters]].<ref name="ljquake3">{{cite web |url=http://www.linuxjournal.com/article/9867 |title=Quake, Meet GPL; GPL, Meet Quake |date=1 December 2007 |access-date=12 January 2012 |publisher=[[Linux Journal]]}}</ref> In addition, numerous [[game engine recreation]]s have [[List of game engine recreations|been produced]] to varying levels of accuracy using [[reverse engineering]] or underlying engine code supporting the original game files including on Linux and other niche systems.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bolding|first=Jonathan |date=4 September 2022|title=Y'all know about these huge lists of free, open-source game clones, right? |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/yall-know-about-these-huge-lists-of-free-open-source-game-clones-right/ |website=[[PC Gamer]]|access-date=4 February 2023}}</ref><ref name="Kumar 2021">{{cite web|url=https://linuxhint.com/open_source_prts_commercial_game_engines/|title=Open Source Ports of Commercial Game Engines|first=Nitesh|last=Kumar|date=2021|website=LinuxHint|access-date=20 March 2023}}</ref>

===2004===
Ryan ported ''Unreal Tournament'' 2004 to Linux for Epic Games<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20050309061407/http://www.macologist.org/viewtopic.php?t=607 Interview with Ryan Gordon: Postal², Unreal & Mac Gaming]}} Macologist, 10 November. 2004</ref> and Timothee Bessett from id Software ported ''Doom 3'' to Linux.<ref name="phoronix.com"/>

David Hedbor, founder and main programmer of [[Eon Games]] ported ''[[NingPo MahJong]]'' and ''[[Hyperspace Delivery Boy!]]'' to Linux, which later were published by LGP.<ref>[http://www.linuxgames.com/archives/5883 Hyperspace Delivery Boy Port] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150204130450/http://www.linuxgames.com/archives/5883 |date=4 February 2015}} [[LinuxGames]], 6 September 2002</ref>

===2005–2007===
Ryan ported ''Postal²: Share the Pain'' to Linux published by LGP.<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20050309061407/http://www.macologist.org/viewtopic.php?t=607 Interview with Ryan Gordon: Postal2, Unreal & Mac Gaming]}} Macologist, 10 November. 2004</ref>

[[CodeWeavers]] offered an enhanced version of Wine called [[CrossOver|CrossOver Games]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Christopher |last=Rice| url=https://www.anandtech.com/show/2897 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100330101419/http://www.anandtech.com/show/2897 |url-status=dead |archive-date=30 March 2010 |title=Linux Gaming: Are We There Yet? |date=28 December 2009 |access-date=2 February 2023 |publisher=[[AnandTech]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first=Jeff |last=Hoogland |url=https://linuxgazette.net/173/hoogland.html |title=Codeweavers vs. Cedega, Commercial Wine Product Comparison |date=April 2010 |access-date=2 February 2023 |publisher=[[Linux Gazette]]}}</ref> The reliance on such compatibility layers remains controversial with concerns that it hinders growth in native development,<ref>{{cite web |first=Stefan |last=Vrabie |url=https://www.linux.com/news/cedega-and-linux-let-windows-games-begin/ |title=Cedega and Linux: Let the Windows games begin |date=31 July 2006 |access-date=2 February 2023 |publisher=[[Linux.com]]}}</ref><ref name="Lees">{{cite web |first=Jennie |last=Lees |url=https://www.engadget.com/2005-12-04-linux-gaming-made-easy.html |title=Linux gaming made easy |date=4 December 2005 |access-date=2 February 2023 |publisher=[[Engadget]]}}</ref> although this approach was defended based on Loki's demise.<ref>{{cite web |first=Salvator |last=Dave |url=https://www.extremetech.com/computing/56768-linux-takes-on-windows-gaming |title=Linux Takes on Windows Gaming |date=28 July 2004 |access-date=2 February 2023 |publisher=[[Extreme Tech]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first=Elizabeth |last=Millard |url=https://www.ecommercetimes.com/story/transgaming-updates-winex-for-linux-gaming-34702.html |title=TransGaming Updates WineX for Linux Gaming |date=24 June 2004 |access-date=2 February 2023 |publisher=Ecommerce Times |archive-date=4 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230204063506/https://www.ecommercetimes.com/story/transgaming-updates-winex-for-linux-gaming-34702.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> [[PlayOnLinux]], established in 2007, provides a community alternative,<ref>{{cite web|first=Angelo|last=M|title=PlayOnLinux vs Wine: The Differences|url=https://www.imaginelinux.com/playonlinux-vs-wine/|website=ImagineLinux|date=2 February 2021|access-date=5 February 2023}}</ref> with various guides being written on how to get games to run through Wine.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.osnews.com/story/8245/opinion-regarding-the-linux-gaming/|website=[[OSNews]]|title=Opinion: Regarding the Linux Gaming|first=Steve|last=Husted|date=13 September 2004|access-date=6 April 2024}}</ref>

The Linux gaming market also started to experience some growth towards the end of the decade with the rise of [[independent video game development]],<ref name="OSNews.com">{{cite web |url=http://www.osnews.com/story/25328/The_State_of_Linux_Gaming_2011 |title=The State of Linux Gaming 2011 |date=14 November 2011 |access-date=12 January 2012 |publisher=OSNews.com |quote=''In short: indie games are thriving on Linux. The Humble Bundles have not only helped publicize the games, but have also helped prove that there is an untapped market for games on Linux, and that Linux users have no problem paying to support the developers who support them.''}}</ref> with many "indie" developers [[Mac gaming#Linux gaming and free software games|favouring support]] for multiple platforms.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.wolfire.com/2008/12/why-you-should-support-mac-os-x-and-linux/|first=Jeffrey|last=Rosen|title=Why you should support Mac OS X and Linux|website=[[Wolfire Games]]|date=28 December 2008|access-date=5 April 2023}}</ref> The [[Humble Indie Bundle]] initiatives inaugurated in 2010 helped to formally demonstrate this trend,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/news/2011/03/humble-bundle-creator-on-ars-influence-and-why-linux-is-important.ars |title=Humble Bundle creator on Ars' influence and why Linux is important |date=1 March 2011 |access-date=2 March 2011 |first=Ben |last=Kuchera |publisher=Ars Technica}}</ref> with Linux users representing a sizable population of their purchase base, and as being the most consistently financially generous in spending.<ref name="humble gdc">{{cite web|title=GDC 2011: Humble Indie Bundle Creators Talk Inspiration, Execution|url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/console/gdc-2011-humble-indie-bundle-creators-talk-inspiration-execution|website=[[Game Developer (website)|Game Developer]]|first=Kyle|last=Orland|date=28 February 2011|access-date=5 April 2023|quote=''Linux users tended to be the most generous of these, leading Graham to suggest indie developers go after underserved markets. "If you support Mac and Linux as an independent developer you have a good chance of doubling your revenue," Graham said.''}}</ref><ref name="humblemoney">{{cite web |url=http://www.omgubuntu.co.uk/2011/12/linux-users-continue-to-most-for-the-humble-indie-bundle/ |title=Linux Users Continue To Pay Most for the @Humble Indie Bundle |first=Joey |last=Sneddon |date=21 December 2011 |access-date=12 January 2012 |publisher=[[OMG! Ubuntu!]]}}</ref> The Humble Indie Bundle V in 2012 faced controversy for featuring a Wine-based release of ''[[Limbo (video game)|Limbo]]'' prepared by [[CodeWeavers]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.indiegamemag.com/linux-users-petition-against-humble-bundle-v-due-to-non-native-version-of-limbo/ |title=Linux Users Petition Against 'humble Bundle V' Due To Non-native Version of 'Limbo' |first=Chris |last=Priestman |date=4 June 2012 |access-date=14 June 2012 |work=Indie Game Magazine |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120608074718/http://www.indiegamemag.com/linux-users-petition-against-humble-bundle-v-due-to-non-native-version-of-limbo/ |archive-date=8 June 2012}}</ref> while a native version was later released in 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gamingonlinux.com/articles/limbo-dark-platformer-fully-native-linux-version-released-no-more-wine.3922 |title=LIMBO Dark Platformer Fully Native Linux Version Released, No More Wine |date=19 June 2014 |first=Liam |last=Dawe |access-date=12 July 2014 |publisher=[[GamingOnLinux]] |archive-date=15 July 2014 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140715022114/http://www.gamingonlinux.com/articles/limbo-dark-platformer-fully-native-linux-version-released-no-more-wine.3922 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Humble eventually began offering Windows-only games in their bundles and on their store.<ref name="thq ars">{{cite web |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2012/11/humble-thq-bundle-threatens-to-ruin-the-brands-reputation/ |title=Humble THQ Bundle threatens to ruin the brand's reputation (Updated) |publisher=[[Ars Technica]] |first=Kyle |last=Orland |date=29 November 2012 |access-date=29 November 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2022/01/humble-subscription-service-is-dumping-mac-linux-access-in-18-days/ |title=Humble subscription service is dumping Mac, Linux access in 18 days |first=Sam |last=Machkovich |date=14 January 2022 |access-date=14 January 2022 |work=[[Ars Technica]]}}</ref>

In 2009, the small indie game company Entourev LLC published ''Voltley'' to Linux which is the first commercial exclusive game for this operating system.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.entourevllc.com/product.php?id=0001 |title=Voltely product page |access-date=5 February 2023 |publisher=Entourev LLC |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141222225801/http://www.entourevllc.com/product.php?id=0001 |archive-date=22 December 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.linuxexperten.com/content/linux-native-games |title=Native Linux Games |access-date=5 February 2023 |publisher=Linuxexperten.com |archive-date=5 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230205195021/https://www.linuxexperten.com/content/linux-native-games |url-status=dead}}</ref> In the same year, LGP released ''[[Shadowgrounds]]'' which was the first commercial game for Linux using the Nvidia PhysX middleware.<ref>{{cite web |first=Michael| last=Larabel| url=https://www.phoronix.com/news/NzAyMw |title=LGP Is Now Porting Shadowgrounds: Survivor |date=29 January 2009 |access-date=4 February 2023 |publisher=[[Phoronix]]}}</ref> The GamingOnLinux website was launched on 4 July 2009, and eventually succeeded LinuxGames as the main source of news and commentary.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://linuxgamingcentral.com/posts/interview-with-liam-from-gol/ |title=An Interview with Liam Dawe, Owner of GamingOnLinux |date=20 April 2022 |access-date=3 February 2023 |publisher=Linux Gaming Central}}</ref>

The release of a Linux version of [[Desura]] in 2011,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.h-online.com/open/news/item/Desura-games-now-also-for-Linux-1381658.html|website=The H Online|title=Desura games now also for Linux|date=18 November 2011|access-date=3 July 2024}}</ref> a [[digital distribution]] platform with a main focus on small [[independent game development|independent developers]], was heralded by several commentators as an important step to greater acknowledgement of Linux as a gaming platform.<ref name="OSNews.com" /><ref name="cheese">{{cite web |url=http://www.twolofbees.com/cheesetalks/desura.php |title=cheese talks to himself – Desura Beta |date=11 October 2011 |access-date=7 November 2011 |publisher=twolofbees.com}}</ref><ref name="arstechnica2015">{{cite web |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2015/02/the-state-of-linux-gaming-in-the-steamos-era/1/ |title=The state of Linux gaming in the SteamOS era |date=26 February 2015 |access-date=27 February 2015 |publisher=[[Ars Technica]]}}</ref> Shortly before this, [[Canonical (company)|Canonical]] launched the [[Ubuntu Software Center]] which also sold digital games.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.unixmen.com/will-it-be-desuras-linux-client-vs-usc/ |title=Will it be Desura's Linux client Vs USC? |first=M. |last=Zinoune |date=27 November 2011 |access-date=2 July 2012 |publisher=Unixmen}}</ref> The digital store Gameolith also launched in 2011 focused principally on Linux before expanding in 2012 and closing in 2014.<ref>{{cite web |last=Dawe|first=Liam |date=21 August 2011|title=Interview with Jonathan Prior of Gameolith.com |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2011/08/interview-with-jonathan-prior-of-gameolithcom/ |website=GamingOnLinux|access-date=4 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.phoronix.com/news/OTYyMg|title=A New Linux Game Store Is Launching Next Week|website=[[Phoronix]]|first=Michael|last=Larabel|date=11 July 2011|access-date=18 February 2023}}</ref>

===2012–2016===
In July 2012, game developer and content distributor [[Valve Corporation|Valve]] announced a port of their [[Source (game engine)|Source engine]] for Linux as well as stating their intention to release their [[Steam (service)|Steam]] digital distribution service for Linux.<ref>{{cite web|last=Albanesius |first=Chloe |url=https://www.pcmag.com/article2/0,2817,2407237,00.asp |title=Valve Moves Forward With Steam for Linux &#124; News & Opinion |publisher=PCMag.com |date=17 July 2012 |access-date=18 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://blogs.valvesoftware.com/linux/steamd-penguins/ |title=Steam'd Penguins |publisher=[[Valve Corporation|Valve]] |date=16 July 2012 |access-date=16 July 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theverge.com/gaming/2012/7/16/3163717/left-4-dead-2-to-be-first-valve-game-on-linux |title='Left 4 Dead 2' to be first Valve game on Linux |first=Tracey |last=Lein |date=16 July 2012 |access-date=16 July 2012 |publisher=[[The Verve]]}}</ref> The potential availability of a Linux Steam client had already attracted other developers to consider porting their titles to Linux,<ref name="arstechnica2015" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.vg247.com/2012/07/25/serious-sam-3-bfe-headed-to-steam-ubuntu/ |title=Serious Sam 3: BFE headed to Steam Ubuntu |first=Brenna |last=Hillier |date=24 July 2012 |access-date=24 July 2012 |publisher=[[VG247]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.phoronix.com/scan.php?page=news_item&px=ODI4NA |title=Valve's Linux Play May Lead More Games To Follow Suit |first=Michael |last=Larbel |date=25 May 2010 |access-date=29 October 2012 |publisher=[[Phoronix]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.phoronix.com/scan.php?page=news_item&px=MTIzMTY |title=Egosoft Wants To Bring Games To Steam On Linux |first=Michael |last=Larbel |date=18 November 2010 |access-date=25 November 2012 |publisher=[[Phoronix]]}}</ref> including previously [[Mac OS]] only porting houses such as [[Aspyr Media]] and [[Feral Interactive]].<ref name="GOLEditorial">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/articles/editorial-linux-gaming-will-be-fine-even-without-steam-machines-succeeding.4992|title=Editorial: Linux Gaming Will Be Fine Even Without Steam Machines Succeeding|publisher=[[GamingOnLinux]]|date=20 February 2015|access-date=27 February 2015}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref>

In November 2012, [[Unity Technologies]] ported their [[Unity (game engine)|Unity engine]] and game creation system to Linux starting with version 4. All of the games created with the Unity engine can now be ported to Linux easily.<ref name="UnityLinux">{{cite web|url=http://www.marketwire.com/press-release/unity-40-launches-1726144.htm|title=Unity 4.0 Launches|publisher=[[Marketwire]]|date=14 November 2012|access-date=3 April 2013}}</ref>

In September 2013, Valve announced that they were releasing a gaming oriented Linux based operating system called [[SteamOS]] with Valve saying they had "come to the conclusion that the environment best suited to delivering value to customers is an operating system built around Steam itself."<ref name="arstechnica2015" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://uk.gamespot.com/news/valve-reveals-steamos-6414851 |title=Valve reveals SteamOS |date=23 September 2013 |access-date=25 September 2013 |first=Eddie |last=Makuch |work=GameSpot |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130926171011/http://uk.gamespot.com/news/valve-reveals-steamos-6414851 |archive-date=26 September 2013}}</ref> This was used for their [[Steam Machine]] platform released on 10 November 2015, and discontinued in 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.polygon.com/2015/6/4/8727269/steam-machine-launch-date |title=The first official Steam Machines hit Oct. 16, on store shelves Nov. 10 |first=Brian |last=Crecente |date=4 June 2015 |access-date=4 June 2015 |publisher=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]}}</ref>

In March 2014, [[GOG.com]] announced they would begin to support Linux titles on their [[Digital rights management|DRM]] free store starting the same year, after previously stating they would not be able due to too many distributions.<ref name="GOGLinux">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamingonlinux.com/articles/gogcom-are-going-to-support-linux-confirmed.3288|title=GOG.com Are Going To Support Linux, Confirmed!|first=Liam|last=Dawe|publisher=[[GamingOnLinux]]|date=18 March 2014|access-date=18 March 2014}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot}}</ref> GOG.com began their initial roll out on 24 July 2014, by offering 50 Linux supporting titles, including several new to the platform.<ref name="GOGLinuxLaunch">{{cite web|url=http://www.gamingonlinux.com/articles/gog-com-now-officially-support-linux-games.4076|title=GOG Com Now Officially Support Linux Games|first=Liam|last=Dawe|publisher=[[GamingOnLinux]]|date=24 July 2014|access-date=24 July 2014}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot}}</ref>

Despite previous statements, GOG have confirmed they have no plans to port their Galaxy client to Linux.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamingonlinux.com/articles/gog-com-now-officially-support-linux-games.4076|title=GOG finally remove the false 'in progress' note about GOG Galaxy for Linux|publisher=GamingOnLinux|date=1 July 2022|access-date=4 February 2023}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot}}</ref> The free software [[Lutris]] started in 2010,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2022/12/lutris-v0512-out-now-fixing-origin-epic-store-ubisoft-connect-gog/ |title=Lutris v0.5.12 out now fixing Origin, Epic Store, Ubisoft Connect, GOG|publisher=GamingOnLinux|date=5 December 2022|access-date=4 February 2023}}</ref> GameHub from 2019,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2019/03/gamehub-is-another-open-source-game-launcher-giving-lutris-some-competition/|title=GameHub is another open source game launcher, giving Lutris some competition|publisher=GamingOnLinux|date=18 March 2019|access-date=5 February 2023}}</ref> MiniGalaxy from 2020,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2020/11/minigalaxy-the-simple-gog-client-for-linux-has-a-big-10-release/|title=Minigalaxy the simple GOG client for Linux has a big 1.0 release|publisher=GamingOnLinux|date=30 November 2020|access-date=5 February 2023}}</ref> and the Heroic Games Launcher from 2021,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2021/01/heroic-games-launcher-is-a-new-unofficial-epic-games-store-for-linux/|title=Heroic Games Launcher is a new unofficial Epic Games Store for Linux|publisher=GamingOnLinux|date=5 January 2021|access-date=5 February 2023}}</ref> offer support for GOG as well as the [[Epic Games Store]], [[Ubisoft Connect]] and [[Origin (service)|Origin]].

In March and April 2014, two major developers [[Epic Games]] and [[Crytek]] announced Linux support for their next generation engines [[Unreal Engine 4]] and [[CryEngine]] respectively.<ref name="UE4Linux">{{cite web|url=https://www.unrealengine.com/blog/41-update-preview|title=Unreal Engine 4.1 Update Preview|date=3 April 2014|access-date=18 December 2015}}</ref><ref name="CryengineLinux">{{cite web|url=http://www.crytek.com/news/conference-attendees-can-also-see-a-brand-new-mobile-game-extra-engine-updates-and-much-more-at-crytek-s-booth|title=CRYENGINE adds Linux Support as Crytek Prepare to Offer New Possibilities at GDC|date=11 March 2014|access-date=18 December 2015}}</ref>

Towards the end of 2014, the game host [[itch.io]] announced that Linux would be supported with their developing [[open source]] game client.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dawe |first=Liam |date=29 December 2014 |title=The Itch Games Store Are Working On An Open Source Client |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2014/12/the-itch-games-store-are-working-on-an-open-source-client/ |access-date=2 February 2023 |website=GamingOnLinux |language=en}}</ref> This was fully launched simultaneously on [[Windows]], [[Mac OS X]], and Linux on 15 December 2015.<ref>{{cite web|last=Corcoran|first=Leaf|date=14 December 2015|title=Say hello to the itch.io app: itch|url=http://blog.itch.io/post/135196264464/say-hello-to-the-itchio-app-itch|website=Itch.io|access-date=15 December 2015}}</ref> The service had supported Linux since it was first unveiled on 3 March 2013, with creator Leaf Corcoran personally a Linux user.<ref>{{cite web|last=Orphanides|first=K.G.|date=8 August 2018|title=Crossing Platforms: a Talk with the Developers Building Games for Linux|url=https://www.linuxjournal.com/content/crossing-platforms-talk-developers-building-games-linux|website=[[Linux Journal]]|access-date=2 February 2023}}</ref> The similar [[Game Jolt]] service also supports Linux and has an open source client released on 13 January 2016.<ref>{{cite web|last=Prakash|first=Abhishek|date=19 January 2023|title=Fantastic Linux Games and Where to Find Them|url=https://itsfoss.com/download-linux-games/|website=It's FOSS|access-date=3 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Kerr |first=Chris |date=13 January 2016 |title=Indie marketplace Game Jolt releases open source desktop client |url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/console/indie-marketplace-game-jolt-releases-open-source-desktop-client |website=Game Developer |access-date=3 February 2023}}</ref> [[GamersGate]] also sells games for Linux.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lee|first=Joel|date=30 August 2015|title=Where to Download the Best Linux Games Without Any Hassle|url=https://www.makeuseof.com/tag/6-digital-distribution-services-linux-gamers/|website=MakeUseOf|access-date=3 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Sohail|first=Mohd|date=23 December 2016|title=Popular Gaming Platforms For Linux|url=https://www.linuxandubuntu.com/home/some-of-the-popular-gaming-platforms-for-linux|website=LinuxAndUbuntu|access-date=3 February 2023}}</ref>

In 2015, started OpenXRay project — an improved version of the [[:ru:X-Ray (игровой движок)|X-Ray Engine]], the game engine used in the world-famous [[S.T.A.L.K.E.R.]], with Linux and macOS support.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 November 2018 |title=OpenXRay, an enhanced game engine for S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Call of Pripyat shows off Linux progress |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2018/11/openxray-an-enhanced-game-engine-for-stalker-call-of-pripyat-shows-off-linux-progress/ |access-date=1 July 2025 |website=GamingOnLinux |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cartwright |first=John |title=Stalker game running on Linux with Open Xray. – Securitron Linux blog. |url=https://www.securitronlinux.com/it/stalker-game-running-on-linux-with-open-xray/ |access-date=1 July 2025 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=10 July 2020 |title=Новая версия открытого движка OpenXRay (S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Call of Pripyat) версии 730 |url=https://www.linux.org.ru/news/games/15803435 |access-date=1 July 2025 |website=www.linux.org.ru |language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Isaac |date=2 December 2018 |title=OpenXRay: an improved graphics engine for STALKER: Call of Pripyat |url=https://blog.desdelinux.net/en/openxray-an-improved-graphics-engine-for-stalker-call-of-pripyat/ |access-date=1 July 2025 |website=Desde Linux |language=en}}</ref>

===2017–present===
[[File:Steam Deck (front).png|thumb|right|Steam Deck, a handheld game console running a Linux-based operating system]]

On 22 August 2018, Valve released their fork of [[Wine (software)|Wine]] called [[Proton (compatibility layer)|Proton]], aimed at gaming.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.siliconera.com/steam-play-proton-to-improve-game-support-for-linux-users/|title=Steam Play Proton To Improve Game Support For Linux Users|first=Alistair|last=Wong|website=[[Siliconera]]|date=25 August 2018|access-date=4 April 2023}}</ref> It features some improvements over the vanilla Wine such as [[Vulkan]]-based [[DirectX 11]] implementation, Steam integration, better full screen and game controller support and improved performance for multi-threaded games.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/221410/announcements/detail/1696055855739350561|title=Steam for Linux :: Introducing a new version of Steam Play|date=21 August 2018|access-date=10 September 2018|language=en}}</ref> It has since grown to include support for [[DirectX 9]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton/wiki/Changelog/664d37be002868c1b6ed27fc2b49adebcd8d1f49|title=Changelog · ValveSoftware/Proton Wiki|date=31 July 2018|access-date=8 December 2019|language=en}}</ref> and [[DirectX 12]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton/wiki/Changelog/403c39180aef0b7a5c7cf8386d5bd3288e0b206d|title=Changelog · ValveSoftware/Proton Wiki|date=8 November 2018|access-date=8 December 2019|language=en}}</ref> over Vulkan. The itch.io app added its own [[Wine (software)|Wine]] integration in June 2020,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dawe |first=Liam |date=7 September 2020 |title=The itch.io app can now use a system installed Wine on Linux for Windows-only games |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2020/09/the-itchio-app-can-now-use-a-system-installed-wine-on-linux-for-windows-only-games |access-date=3 February 2023 |website=GamingOnLinux |language=en}}</ref> while [[Lutris]] and [[PlayOnLinux]] are long-standing independent solutions for compatibility wrappers.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kenlon|first=Seth|date=25 October 2018|title=Lutris: Linux game management made easy|url=https://opensource.com/article/18/10/lutris-open-gaming-platform |website=Opensource.com|access-date=5 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Saive|first=Ravi|date=18 July 2022|title=PlayOnLinux – Run Windows Software and Games in Linux|url=https://www.tecmint.com/playonlinux-install-windows-software-in-linux/ |website=TechMint|access-date=5 February 2023}}</ref>

As with Wine and Cedega in the past, concerns have been raised over whether Proton hinders native development more than it encourages use of the platform.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nuclearmonster.com/2021/07/native-linux-games-vs-windows-api-compatibility-layers-on-the-steam-deck/|title=Native Linux Games vs Windows API Compatibility Layers on the Steam Deck|first=Jack|last=Slater|website=Nuclear Monster|date=19 July 2021|access-date=4 April 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.publish0x.com/late-to-the-show-and-games/the-linux-gaming-conundrum-proton-vs-native-linux-support-xnxqryr|title=The Linux Gaming Conundrum: Proton vs. Native Linux Support|author=LateToTheParty|date=22 July 2021|website=Publish0x|access-date=4 April 2023}}</ref> ''[[Prodeus]]'' dropped native support in favour of Proton shortly before final release<ref>{{cite web |title=Prodeus cancels the Native Linux version, focusing on Proton compatibility (updated) |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2022/09/prodeus-cancels-the-native-linux-version-focusing-on-proton-compatibility/ |last=Dawe |first=Liam |date=6 September 2022 |website=GamingOnLinux |language=en}}</ref> and [[Arcen Games]] cancelled planned native support for ''[[Heart of the Machine]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Heart of the Machine from Arcen Games dropping Native Linux for Proton |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2023/08/heart-of-the-machine-from-arcen-games-dropping-native-linux-for-proton/ |last=Dawe |first=Liam |date=14 August 2023 |website=GamingOnLinux |language=en}}</ref> Valve has expressed no preference over Proton or native ports among developers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2021/11/valve-answers-the-question-should-developers-do-native-linux-support-or-proton/|title=Valve answers the question: should developers do native Linux support or Proton?|first=Liam|last=Dawe|date=13 November 2021|access-date=4 April 2023}}</ref>

On 25 February 2022, Valve released [[Steam Deck]], a [[handheld game console]] running SteamOS 3.0.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Dawe |first=Liam |date=25 February 2022 |title=The Steam Deck has released, here's my initial review |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2022/02/steam-deck-initial-review/ |access-date=27 February 2022 |website=GamingOnLinux |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Larabel |first=Michael |date=25 February 2022 |title=For Linux Enthusiasts Especially, The Steam Deck Is An Incredible & Fun Device |url=https://www.phoronix.com/scan.php?page=article&item=steam-deck-steamos-linux |access-date=27 February 2022 |website=[[Phoronix]] |language=en}}</ref> The deployment of Proton and other design decisions were based on the limited response to their previous [[Steam Machines]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/steam-deck-valve-explains-how-it-learned-from-past-mistakes ==Commercial games for non-x86 instruction sets==
[[File:Alpha-Centauri-Logo.svg|thumb|right|200px|''[[Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri]]'' was released for numerous architectures.]]

Some companies ported games to Linux running on instruction sets other than x86, such as [[DEC Alpha|Alpha]], [[PowerPC]], [[SPARC]], MIPS or ARM.

[[Loki Entertainment Software]] ported ''[[Civilization: Call to Power]]'', ''[[Eric's Ultimate Solitaire]]'', ''[[Heroes of Might and Magic III]]'', ''[[Myth II: Soulblighter]]'', ''[[Railroad Tycoon II Gold Edition]]'' and ''[[Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri]]'' with ''[[Alien Crossfire]]'' expansion pack to Linux PowerPC.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linuxgames.com/?s=PPC+loki|title=PPC games made by Loki software – related posts LinuxGames|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019170037/http://www.linuxgames.com/?s=PPC+loki|archive-date=19 October 2013}}</ref> They also ported ''Civilization: Call to Power'', ''Eric's Ultimate Solitaire'', ''Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri'' with ''Alien Crossfire'' expansion pack to Linux Alpha and ''Civilization: Call to Power,'' ''Eric's Ultimate Solitaire'' to Linux SPARC.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linuxgames.com/archives/5171|title=Loki Holiday Info and Deals LinuxGames|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131020115618/http://www.linuxgames.com/archives/5171|archive-date=20 October 2013}}</ref>

[[Linux Game Publishing]] published ''[[Candy Cruncher]]'', ''[[Majesty Gold]]'', ''[[NingPo MahJong]]'' and ''[[Soul Ride]]'' to Linux PowerPC. They also ported ''Candy Cruncher'', ''Soul Ride'' to Linux SPARC and ''Soul Ride'' to Linux Alpha.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linuxgamepublishing.com/info.php?id=10& |title=Candy Cruncher Linux Sparc |date=9 September 2005 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050909024159/http://www.linuxgamepublishing.com/info.php?id=10& |archive-date=9 September 2005}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linuxgazette.com/node/10249 |title=Linux Game Publishing: Interview with Michael Simms |publisher=[[Linux Gazette]] |date=6 March 2005 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050712080821/http://www.linuxgazette.com/node/10249 |archive-date=12 July 2005}}</ref>

[[Illwinter Game Design]] ported ''[[Dominions: Priests, Prophets and Pretenders]]'', ''[[Dominions II: The Ascension Wars]]'' and ''[[Dominions 3]]'' to Linux PowerPC, as well as ''[[Conquest of Elysium 3]]'', ''[[Dominions 4: Thrones of Ascension]]'' to Raspberry Pi.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linuxgames.com/archives/6674 |title=Dominions II: The Ascension Wars 2.12 |date=8 June 2004 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131202235722/http://www.linuxgames.com/archives/6674 |archive-date=2 December 2013}}</ref>

[[Hyperion Entertainment]] ported ''[[Sin (video game)|Sin]]'' to Linux PowerPC published by [[Titan Computer]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amiga-news.de/en/news/AN-2000-08-00266-EN.html|title=Linux Version of SiN Almost Finished|publisher=amiga-news.de|date=28 August 2008|access-date=3 January 2024}}</ref> and ''[[Gorky 17]]'' to Linux PowerPC which later was published by LGP.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.exec.pl/wydarzenie.jsp?nid=2815&Gorky_17_dla_Linuxa_PPC|title=Gorky 17 dla Linuxa PPC|publisher=eXec.pl|date=8 June 2006|access-date=3 January 2024}}</ref>

Runesoft hired Gunnar von Boehn which ported ''[[Robin Hood – The Legend of Sherwood]]'' to Linux PowerPC.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amiga-news.de/en/news/AN-2006-07-00103-EN.html|title=Linux: PowerPC port of Robin Hood|publisher=amiga-news.de|date=30 July 2006|access-date=3 January 2024}}</ref> Later Runesoft ported ''[[Airline Tycoon Deluxe]]'' to [[Raspberry Pi]] was running [[Debian]] GNU/Linux.{{citation needed|date=November 2020}}

[[Laminar Research]] ported [[X-Plane_(simulator)|X-Plane]] 8 to Linux PowerPC.

Iain McLeod ported [[Spheres of Chaos]] to Linux on the PlayStation 2 consoles and later re-released it as a freeware game.

==Market share==
{{See also|Linux adoption#Desktop Linux adoption}}
The [[Steam (service)|Steam]] Hardware Survey reports that as of August 2026, 3.9% of users are using some form of Linux as their platform's main operating system.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-11 |title=Steam Linux Market Share & Usage Statistics (Updated Aug-2026) |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/steam-tracker/ |access-date=2026-09-14 |website=GamingOnLinux |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://store.steampowered.com/hwsurvey/|title=Steam Hardware & Software survey|date=July 2021}}</ref> The [[Unity (game engine)|Unity]] [[game engine]] used to<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://forum.unity.com/threads/wheres-the-unity-stats-page-gone.514106/|title=Where's the Unity stats page gone?|website=Unity Forum|date=24 January 2018 |language=en-US|access-date=14 May 2019}}</ref> make their statistics available and in March 2016 reported that Linux users accounted for 0.4% of players.<ref>[http://hwstats.unity3d.com/pc/os.html Platforms Top on 2016-03] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170627193942/http://hwstats.unity3d.com/pc/os.html |date=27 June 2017}} ''Windows players: 97.3%, Mac OS X players: 2.3%, Linux players: 0.4%''</ref> In 2010, in the first [[Humble Bundle]] sales, Linux formed 18% of purchases.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.wolfire.com/humble/stats|title=Humble Budle data}}</ref>

==Supported hardware==
[[File:PandoraFront.JPG|thumb|right|200px|The [[Pandora (console)|Pandora]] was a Linux integrated [[game console]] from 2010.]]

Linux as a gaming platform can also refer to operating systems based on the Linux kernel and specifically designed for the ''sole purpose'' of gaming. Examples are [[SteamOS]], which is an operating system for [[Steam Machines]], [[Steam Deck]] and general computers, [[video game console]]s built from components found in the classical home computer, (embedded) operating systems like [[Tizen]] and [[Pandora (console)|Pandora]], and [[handheld game console]]s like [[GP2X]], and [[Neo Geo X]]. The [[Nvidia Shield]] runs Android as an operating system, which is based on a modified Linux kernel.{{Citation needed|date=October 2019}}

The [[Open-source software|open source]] design of the Linux software platform allows the operating system to be compatible with various computer [[instruction set]]s and many [[peripherals]], such as [[game controller]]s and [[head-mounted display]]s. As an example, [[HTC Vive]], which is a [[virtual reality]] head-mounted display, [[list of games with HTC Vive support|supports]] the Linux gaming platform.{{Citation needed|date=October 2019}}

===Performance===
In 2013, tests by [[Phoronix]] showed real-world performance of games on Linux with proprietary Nvidia and AMD drivers were mostly comparable to results on Windows 8.1.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.phoronix.com/scan.php?page=article&item=gpus_windows81_ubuntu&num=1 |title=Ubuntu Linux Gaming Performance Mostly On Par With Windows 8.1 |publisher=[[Phoronix]] |date=27 October 2013 |access-date=4 March 2014}}</ref> [[Phoronix]] found similar results in 2015,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.phoronix.com/review/win10-nv-ubu1504/4|title=NVIDIA GeForce: Windows 10 vs. Ubuntu 15.04 Linux OpenGL Benchmarks Review|website=www.phoronix.com}}</ref> though [[Ars Technica]] described a 20% performance drop with Linux drivers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2015/11/ars-benchmarks-show-significant-performance-hit-for-steamos-gaming/|title=SteamOS gaming performs significantly worse than Windows, Ars analysis shows|date=13 November 2015}}</ref>

==Software architecture==
An operating system based on the Linux kernel and customized specifically for gaming, could adopt the [[Vanilla (software)|vanilla]] Linux kernel with only little changes, or—like the Android operating system—be based on a relative extensively modified Linux kernel. It could adopt [[GNU C Library]] or [[Bionic (software)|Bionic]] or something like it. The entire [[middleware]] or parts of it, could very well be closed-source and [[proprietary software]]; the same is true for the video games. There are free and open-source video games available for the Linux operating system, as well as proprietary ones.{{Citation needed|date=October 2019}}

===Linux kernel===
The subsystems already mainlined and available in the [[Linux kernel]] are most probably performant enough so to not impede the gaming experience in any way,{{Citation needed|date=February 2017}} however additional software is available, such as e.g. the [[Brain Fuck Scheduler]] (a process scheduler) or the Budget Fair Queueing (BFQ) scheduler (an I/O scheduler).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://algo.ing.unimo.it/people/paolo/disk_sched/ |title=Budget Fair Queueing I/O Scheduler |access-date=7 March 2014 |archive-date=11 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140311090210/http://algo.ing.unimo.it/people/paolo/disk_sched/ |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Similar to the way the Linux kernel can be, for example, adapted to run better on supercomputers, there are adaptations targeted at improving the performance of games. A project concerning itself with this issue is called Liquorix.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.phoronix.com/review/liquorix_311_kernel|title=Liquorix 3.11 Kernel Benchmarks|website=www.phoronix.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://liquorix.net/|title=Liquorix Kernel|website=liquorix.net}}</ref>

[[Enterbrain]]'s [[RPG Maker MV]] was released for Linux.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gamefromscratch.com/rpg-maker-mv-comes-to-linux/|title=RPG Maker MV Comes to Linux|website=GameFromScratch|date=24 March 2017|access-date=16 September 2023}}</ref> In addition, open-source, cross-platform clones of the [[RPG Maker]] series exist such as Open RPG Maker, MKXP and EasyRPG,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.phoronix.com/news/MTU2Mzg|title=MKXP: Open-Source, Linux Engine To RPG Maker XP|website=[[Phoronix]]|first=Michael|last=Larabel|date=8 January 2014|access-date=16 September 2023}}</ref> as well as the similar [[Official Hamster Republic Role Playing Game Construction Engine|OHRRPGCE]] and Solarus.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2020/03/solarus-is-a-free-and-open-source-cross-platform-game-engine-for-2d-action-rpgs/|website=GamingOnLinux|title=Solarus is a free and open source cross-platform game engine for 2D action-RPGs|first=Liam|last=Dawe|date=6 March 2020|access-date=17 September 2023}}</ref> The [[Adventure Game Studio]] editor is not yet ported to Linux, although games made in it are compatible, and the [[Wintermute Engine|Wintermute]] and SLUDGE<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cheesetalks.net/sludge.php|website=Cheese Talks|last=Bush|first=Josh|title=Cheese talks to himself (about the SLUDGE engine)|date=9 July 2015|access-date=17 September 2023}}</ref> adventure game engines are available. ZGameEditor,<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=DeKPDAAAQBAJ|title=Learning and Education Games: Volume Two: Bringing Games into Educational Contexts|first=Karen|last=Schrier Shaenfeld|date=10 April 2016|page=265 |publisher=Lulu.com |isbn=978-1329703568}}</ref> Novashell,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.brighthub.com/computing/linux/articles/51816/?expand_article=1|website=Bright Hub|title=Open Source Game Creation Software: Working in 2D|date=7 October 2009}}</ref> GB Studio,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2020/08/make-retro-game-boy-games-with-the-open-source-gb-studio-now-with-colour-in-the-20-bet/|title=Make retro Game Boy games with the open source GB Studio, now with colour in the 2.0 Beta|website=GamingOnLinux|first=Liam|last=Dawe|date=26 August 2020|access-date=17 September 2023}}</ref> and the [[ZZT]] inspired MegaZeux<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eev.ee/blog/2016/10/06/succeeding-megazeux/|title=Succeeding MegaZeux|first=Evelyn|last=Wood|website=fuzzy notepad|date=6 October 2016|access-date=14 February 2023}}</ref> are also options. Versions of [[Mugen (game engine)|Mugen]] were made available for Linux,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://appuals.com/run-mugen-fighter-natively-linux-environment/|title=How to Run Mugen Fighter Natively in a Linux Environment|last=Arrows|first=Kevin|website=Appuals|date=28 April 2023|access-date=20 September 2023}}</ref> and open-source re-implementations such as IKEMEN Go are compatible.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dashfight.com/news/ikemen-go-rollback-open-alpha-launches-today-2332|title=IKEMEN Go Rollback Open Alpha Launches Today|first=Arthur|last=Blizen|website=DashFight|date=20 January 2023|access-date=20 September 2023}}</ref> The [[JavaScript]] based [[Ct.js]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2019/08/2d-game-editor-ctjs-goes-open-source-and-its-closing-in-on-a-new-major-release/|title=2D game editor ct.js goes open source and it's closing in on a new major release|website=GamingOnLinux|first=Liam|last=Dawe|date=21 August 2019|access-date=18 September 2023}}</ref> [[Pixelbox.js]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gamefromscratch.com/pixelbox-js-game-engine/|title=Pixelbox.js Game Engine|website=GameFromScratch|date=14 April 2020|access-date=18 September 2023}}</ref> and [[Superpowers (software)|Superpowers]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2016/01/superpowers-a-html5-development-environment-for-2d-3d-games-now-open-source/|website=GamingOnLinux|first=Liam|last=Dawe|title=Superpowers, a HTML5 development environment for 2D & 3D games now open source|date=17 January 2016|access-date=29 October 2023}}</ref> 
are also options.

====Level editors====
{{See also|GtkRadiant}}
Various [[level editor]]s exist for Linux, such as [[Qoole|wxqoole]], [[GtkRadiant]], [[TrenchBroom]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/make-quake-with-trenchbroom|website=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]]|title=Make Quake With TrenchBroom|first=Craig|last=Pearson|date=12 March 2013|access-date=17 September 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://linuxgamecast.com/2013/03/trenchbroom-modern-cross-platform-map-editor-for-quake-1/|title=TrenchBroom: Modern Cross Platform Map Editor For Quake 1|website=Linux Game Cast|first=Venn|last=Stone|date=1 March 2013|access-date=2 January 2024}}</ref> and J.A.C.K.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.teteos.net/d/149-jack-hammer-editor|title=J.A.C.K. Hammer Editor|website=TeTeOS.Net|first=Hasan|last=Merkit|date=22 March 2022|access-date=17 September 2023}}</ref> for the [[id Tech]] engines and related, Eureka,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/articles/eureka-offers-a-new-option-for-doom-mappers.1535|website=GamingOnLinux|title=Eureka offers a new option for Doom mappers|first=Hamish|last=Wilson|date=16 December 2012|access-date=17 September 2023}}</ref> SLADE<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.linuxmadesimple.info/2021/02/how-to-install-slade-3-on-chromebook.html|website=Linux Made Simple|title=How to install Slade 3 on a Chromebook|date=1 February 2021|access-date=17 September 2023}}</ref> and ReDoomEd<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2020/01/redoomed-a-port-of-the-original-doom-level-editor-was-released-on-linux/|title='ReDoomEd', a port of the original Doom level editor, was released on Linux|first=Daniel|last=Palacio|date=26 January 2020|access-date=17 September 2023}}</ref> for the [[Doom engine|''Doom'' engine]], and the general purpose [[tile map]] editors LDtk,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2022/03/free-and-open-source-level-designer-ldtk-10-is-out-now/|title=Free and open source level editor LDtk 1.0 is out now|first=Liam|last=Dawe|website=GamingOnLinux|date=30 March 2022|access-date=6 February 2023}}</ref> Ogmo,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gamefromscratch.com/ogmo-level-editor/|title=OGMO Level Editor|website=GameFromScratch|date=18 November 2019|access-date=17 September 2023}}</ref> and Tiled.<ref>{{cite web|first=Theodore|last=McKenzie|title=Tiled: A Flexible and Free-to-Use Level Editor|url=https://80.lv/articles/tiled-a-flexible-and-free-to-use-level-editor|date=21 June 2021|access-date=5 February 2023|website=80LV}}</ref>

====Debuggers====
{{See also|AMD CodeXL}}
Several game development tools have been available for Linux, including [[GNU Debugger]], [[LLDB (debugger)|LLDB]], [[Valgrind]], glslang and others. [[VOGL]], a [[debugger]] for [[OpenGL]] was released on 12 March 2014.

====<span class="anchor" id="APIs"></span>Available interfaces and SDKs====
There are multiple [[Application programming interface|interfaces]] and [[Software Development Kit]]s available for Linux, and almost all of them are [[cross-platform]]. Most are [[free and open-source software]] subject to the terms of the [[zlib License]], making it possible to static link against them from fully closed-source proprietary software. One difficulty due to this abundance of interfaces, is the difficulty for programmers to choose the best suitable audio API for their purpose. The main developer of the [[PulseAudio]] project, [[Lennart Poettering]], commented on this issue.<ref name="guideaudiojungle">{{cite web
| url=http://0pointer.de/blog/projects/guide-to-sound-apis.html
| title=A Guide Through The Linux Sound API Jungle
| last=Poettering
| first=Lennart
| publisher=0pointer.de/blog
| date=24 September 2008
| access-date=4 March 2014}}</ref>
Physics engines, audio libraries, that are available as modules for game engines, have been available for Linux for a long time.{{Time needed|date=October 2019}}{{Citation needed|date=October 2019}}

The book ''[[Programming Linux Games]]'' covers a couple of the available APIs suited for video game development for Linux, while ''[[The Linux Programming Interface]]'' covers the [[Linux kernel interfaces]] in much greater detail.
